subject: Mathematics

teaching_strategy: सिफारिश गणितीय बिन्दुहरू र संख्याहरू का उपयोग गरेर गुणा र योग संक्रियाहरू लाई दर्शाउने र विद्यार्थीहरूको बीच योगदान लाउने। उदाहरणका लागि, निर्दिष्ट संख्याहरू र बिन्दुहरू लाई गणितीय बोर्ड वा चित्रकला द्वारा दर्शाउने र विद्यार्थीहरूको बीच गुणा र योग संक्रियाहरू लाई अनुसरण गर्ने अभ्यास गर्ने।

subject: Mathematics
competency: समीकरणहरूको हल गर्ने र चेक गर्ने
teaching_strategy: समीकरणहरूको हल गर्ने लागि विभिन्न समीकरणहरूको उदाहरणहरू दिनु र उनलाई हल गर्ने व्यवस्था गर्नुहोस्। उदाहरणका लागि, निर्दिष्ट समीकरणहरूको उदाहरणहरू दिनु र उनलाई हल गर्ने व्यवस्था गर्नुहोस्।

subject: Mathematics
competency: संख्याहरू भाग र गुणा गर्ने र मान पत्ता लगाउने।
teaching_strategy: संख्याहरू गणना गर्ने लागि काउंटर वा नीपार रुपयाका नोटहरू उपयोग गर्ने।

subject: Mathematics

subject: Mathematics
competency: संख्याहरूको गुणन गणना गर्ने र गुणनफल निर्धारण गर्ने क्षमता विकसित गर्ने

competency: समीकरणहरू र उनको हल गर्ने तरिका विकसित गर्नुहोस्। यो गणितको मूल संकल्प हो।
teaching_strategy: समीकरणहरू र उनको हल गर्ने अभ्यास गर्ने लागि वास्तविक दृश्यहरू र उदाहरणहरू उपयोग गर्नुहोस्। यसको माध्यममा बचाले र विद्यार्थीहरूले अभ्यास गर्न सक्छन्।

competency: संख्याहरूको व्यवस्थापन र गणना गर्ने क्षमता विकसित गर्ने
teaching_strategy: नर्सरी क्रमांक ब्याज दिएको नोटहरू वा गणित ग्राफिकल तत्वहरू उपयोग गरेर गणना गर्ने अभ्यास गर्ने

teaching_strategy: संख्याहरूको गुणन र भाग गर्ने अभ्यास गर्ने र यसको लागि गुणन र भाग गर्ने गणित शिक्षण ग्राफिकल तत्वहरू उपयोग गरेर गर्ने

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and differentiate between finite and infinite sets through observation and discussion.
teaching_strategy: Use visual aids such as pictures of a rainbow and an aquarium to engage students in constructing sets. Have students count the elements in finite sets and discuss why the set of natural numbers is infinite.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Classify given sets as finite or infinite.
teaching_strategy: Provide sets such as natural numbers, whole numbers less than 30, even numbers, and square numbers up to 30. Use flashcards or guided practice to help students identify and classify these sets.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Write sets in set notation for given collections (days of the week, vowels, colors, square numbers, prime numbers).
teaching_strategy: Phonics games can be used to help students remember the elements of each set. For example, create flashcards with the days of the week, vowels, colors, etc., and have students match them to the correct set notation.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and understand the concept of a null set (empty set) and its representation.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing can be used to illustrate the concept of a null set. For example, have students act out scenarios where a set has no elements, such as a set of female Prime Ministers of Nepal or natural numbers between 1 and 2. Discuss the concept of the null set and its symbol ∅.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and classify sets as finite or infinite based on the number of elements
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with examples of finite and infinite sets. Have students categorize given sets as finite or infinite and justify their answers.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Determine the number of elements in a finite set
teaching_strategy: Provide guided practice with a variety of finite sets, encouraging students to count elements and write the total number. Use role-playing where students act as set members to count and verify the number of elements.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and determine equivalent and equal sets based on the number of elements and the elements themselves.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with sets of different objects (e.g., shapes, letters) to help students identify the number of elements in each set. Have students compare sets and discuss whether they are equivalent or equal.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and list elements of sets, determine the number of elements, and classify sets as equal.
teaching_strategy: Use a Venn diagram to visually represent sets A and B. Have students create their own sets and compare them using Venn diagrams. Provide flashcards with prime numbers, factors, and multiples for practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and classify sets as empty or non-empty, finite or infinite, and determine set equality and equivalence.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with sets on one side and their classification on the other. Have students match the sets to their correct classifications. For set equality, create Venn diagrams to visually compare sets A and B, and have students identify common elements.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and compare sets based on the number of elements and equality
teaching_strategy: Use Venn diagrams to visually represent the sets and their relationships. Engage students in a group activity where they create their own sets using classroom objects and compare them.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Determine if sets are equal or equivalent and understand the difference
teaching_strategy: Conduct a role-playing activity where students act as sets and demonstrate equality and equivalence through movement and interaction. Use flashcards with set elements for quick recognition and comparison.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and understand the concept of a universal set and its subsets
teaching_strategy: Divide students into groups to form sets of even, odd, square, cube, prime, and composite numbers. Discuss how the set of natural numbers (N) can cover all these sets. Similarly, create sets for girls, boys, and students wearing caps. Use these sets to introduce the concept of a universal set (U) that contains all the discussed sets.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and define the universal set using natural numbers up to 15
teaching_strategy: Divide students into groups, provide a dialogue scenario, and have them discuss and identify the universal set. Use a set of natural numbers up to 15 as the context.

subject: Mathematics
competency: List elements of given sets using the listing method
teaching_strategy: Guide students to list even numbers and prime numbers less than 15. Use flashcards with numbers for a hands-on activity.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and list elements of sets (square numbers, odd numbers, composite numbers, even numbers, multiples of 3, prime numbers) within a given universal set.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with numbers less than 25 to help students identify square numbers, odd numbers, and composite numbers. For even numbers and multiples of 3, create a number line from 5 to 20 and mark the appropriate numbers. Discuss prime numbers using a sieve of Eratosthenes activity.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Determine an appropriate universal set for given sets and understand the concept of set membership and exclusion.
teaching_strategy: Engage students in a group activity where they create their own universal sets for given sets A and B, and discuss the elements that should or should not be included. Use real-life examples to illustrate the concept of universal sets.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Understanding subsets and creating sets from a universal set
competency: Students will be able to identify and create subsets from a given universal set through group activities.
teaching_strategy: Divide students into groups and provide them with a universal set of tools. Have each group create different subsets as described in the activity. Use this as an opportunity to discuss the concept of subsets and their properties.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and classify subsets, including proper and improper subsets, and understand the concept of the empty set.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with sets and their subsets for students to identify and classify. Conduct a role-playing activity where students form sets and discuss the subsets they can create.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Determine the number of subsets, including proper and improper subsets, that can be formed from a given set.
teaching_strategy: Guide students through creating subsets from a given set using guided practice. Use a Venn diagram to visually represent the subsets and discuss the relationship between the number of elements in the set and the number of subsets.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and differentiate between proper and improper subsets of a given set.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with sets and subsets to help students recognize proper and improper subsets. Provide examples and non-examples to reinforce understanding.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Determine subsets of a universal set and classify them as proper or improper.
teaching_strategy: Engage students in a group activity where they form subsets from a given universal set and classify them. Use a universal set like {a, e, i, o, u} and have students create different subsets to practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify proper subsets and list all possible subsets of given sets
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with sets A, B, and C to identify proper subsets. Have students create flashcards for sets A, B, and C and practice identifying proper subsets. Use the table on page 20 to guide students in listing all possible subsets for given sets.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Apply knowledge of subsets to real-world scenarios
teaching_strategy: Conduct a classroom activity where students list items from their classroom and form sets based on characteristics. Have students create sets for different categories (e.g., stationary, furniture) and list all possible subsets for each set. Encourage students to present their findings to the class.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and classify sets, understand the concepts of equivalent and equal sets
teaching_strategy: Use Venn diagrams to visually represent sets A and B. Have students create their own examples of equivalent and equal sets using objects from the classroom.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Classify natural numbers, multiples, and even numbers
teaching_strategy: Create a number line activity where students identify and mark multiples of 2. Use flashcards with numbers for quick recognition of even and odd numbers.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Understanding Square Numbers and Square Roots
competency: Students will be able to identify square numbers and calculate square roots through visual representation and multiplication.
teaching_strategy: Use manipulatives like square tiles or blocks to create square figures. Have students count the number of boxes along the length and breadth, then calculate the total number of boxes. Discuss how this relates to the concept of square numbers. Introduce the square root symbol and have students find the square root of given square numbers using the tiles.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Finding the square root through subtraction of odd numbers
competency: Students will understand and apply the method of subtracting successive odd numbers from a square number to find its square root.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Create a 'Subtraction Race' where students take turns subtracting odd numbers from a given square number. The first student to reach zero wins and the number of steps taken is the square root.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Finding square root using prime factorization
competency: Students will learn to find the square root of a number by prime factorization.
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Divide students into groups and assign each group a number. Each group will find the prime factors of their assigned number and then determine the square root. They can present their findings to the class.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand the relationship between prime factors and square roots through prime factorization.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with prime numbers and have students identify and match them with their multiples. Conduct a guided practice session where students find the prime factors of numbers like 36 and 1225, and then calculate their square roots using the prime factorization method.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Finding the square root of a number through prime factorization
competency: Students will be able to find the square root of a perfect square by prime factorization and simplification.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with perfect squares and their square roots. Have students practice breaking down numbers into prime factors and then simplifying to find the square root.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Applying the concept of square roots to real-world problems
competency: Students will apply the concept of square roots to solve real-world problems involving areas of squares.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a role-playing activity where students measure and calculate the dimensions of a pretend seminar hall. Use a large square poster or a classroom floor as a visual aid to demonstrate the concept.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand and apply the division method to find the square root of a number.
teaching_strategy: Guide students through the division method using a step-by-step approach. Use a number line or a visual aid to show the pairing of digits and the process of finding the square root. Have students practice with different numbers, such as 2809 or 3136, to reinforce the concept.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Finding the square root using the division method
competency: Students will be able to calculate the square root of a number using the division method.
teaching_strategy: Guide students through the division method step-by-step using examples. Have students practice with different numbers, providing them with square numbers to start with and gradually increasing the complexity. Use flashcards with numbers for quick practice sessions.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will understand how to find the square root of a fraction and simplify the result.
teaching_strategy: Provide examples of square roots of fractions, such as √(144/169), and demonstrate the process of finding the square root of the numerator and denominator separately. Use role-playing where students take turns to find the square root of given fractions and simplify the results. Create a game where students match the simplified square roots with their original fractions.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Determine if a number is a perfect square and find the number that makes it a perfect square using prime factorization.
teaching_strategy: Use a factor tree game where students break down numbers into their prime factors and identify pairs. For example, create a factor tree for 12675 and discuss how to make pairs of prime factors to determine if it's a perfect square.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate square roots using both prime factorization and division methods.
teaching_strategy: Implement a 'square root scavenger hunt' where students find the square roots of given numbers using flashcards. For the division method, use a step-by-step guided practice where students divide the number to find the square root, similar to long division.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate square roots of numbers and determine if a number is a perfect square using prime factorization.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with square numbers and their roots for quick recall practice. Conduct a role-play where students are given numbers and must find their square roots using the continuous subtraction method.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate the area of squares and find the side length given the area.
teaching_strategy: Have students measure and draw squares of different lengths. Use a guided practice where they calculate the area and side length of squares with given areas.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Determine if a number is a square number and find the least number to multiply to make a square number
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with numbers for students to identify square numbers. Conduct a class activity where students work in pairs to find the least number that can be multiplied to a given non-square number to make it a square number. Provide real-life examples such as arranging desks in a classroom to form a perfect square.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will understand the concept of cube numbers and calculate the volume of a cube.
teaching_strategy: Use a Rubik’s Cube to demonstrate the concept of a cube and its volume. Have students count the unit cubes on the Rubik’s Cube to understand the multiplication of three identical numbers. Provide real-life examples such as the underground water tank to show the practical application of cube numbers in calculating volume.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Finding the cube root using prime factorization
competency: Students will be able to determine the cube root of a number by breaking it down into its prime factors and grouping them into triplets.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with prime numbers and have students practice breaking down numbers into their prime factors. Then, guide them to group the factors into triplets to find the cube root.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Finding the Cube Root of a Number
competency: Students will learn to find the cube root of a number by prime factorization and grouping the factors in sets of three.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with prime factors and have students group them in sets of three. Then, have them multiply the base number for each group to find the cube root.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Application of Cube Roots in Real-life Problems
competency: Students will apply the concept of cube roots to solve real-life problems, such as finding the height of a cubical tank given its volume.
teaching_strategy: Provide students with a variety of real-life scenarios involving volumes of cubical objects. Have them work in groups to find the dimensions of these objects using the cube root method.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Determine if a number is a perfect cube and find the least number to make it a perfect cube using prime factorization.
teaching_strategy: Use a factor tree game where students break down numbers into their prime factors. Have students work in pairs to identify the prime factors of given numbers and determine if they are perfect cubes. For numbers that are not perfect cubes, have them find the least number to multiply or divide to make them perfect cubes.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate the volume of a cube and the capacity of a cubical tank.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a hands-on activity where students measure the length of a cube and calculate its volume. Use a 1-meter cube model to demonstrate the concept of volume and capacity. Have students measure the length of the cubical tank and calculate its capacity in liters, converting cubic meters to liters.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and understand properties of cube numbers
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with the cube numbers of natural numbers from 1 to 10. Have students identify if the cube of an odd number is odd and if the cube of an even number is even. Provide real-life examples of cube numbers and have students present them in class.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Apply knowledge of cube numbers in practical scenarios
teaching_strategy: Assign students to find and present at least five examples of cube numbers used in daily life. Use guided practice to solve problems involving cubic measurements such as cubic meters and liters.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and calculate the HCF using prime factorization method
teaching_strategy: Use the prime factorization method to find the HCF of 20 and 35. Engage students in a group activity where they distribute 30 apples and 40 bananas equally among people to find the greatest number of people and the quantity each person gets.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Finding the Highest Common Factor (HCF) using Prime Factorization
competency: Students will be able to find the HCF of two or more numbers by prime factorization and apply it to real-life scenarios such as distributing items equally.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with prime numbers and have students identify the common factors. Then, guide them through the prime factorization of the given numbers (30 and 40) and demonstrate how to find the HCF. Provide additional examples like 100, 125, and 200 for practice.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Finding the Highest Common Factor (HCF) using the Division Method
competency: Students will be able to determine the HCF of given numbers through the division method by dividing the largest number by the smallest, then continuing the process until the remainder is zero.
teaching_strategy: Guide students through a group activity where they practice finding the HCF of given numbers using the division method. Provide examples and have students work in groups to solve problems like finding the HCF of 100, 125, and 200. Use flashcards with numbers for practice and encourage peer teaching.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will be able to find the HCF of three numbers and apply it to solve real-world problems involving distribution.
teaching_strategy: Use a game where students work in groups to find the HCF of given sets of numbers. Provide flashcards with numbers and have students race to find the HCF. After finding the HCF, guide them to divide the total quantity by the HCF to determine the number of students and the quantity each student gets.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Finding the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of three numbers and using it to solve a real-world problem
competency: Students will be able to determine the HCF of three given numbers and apply it to solve a practical problem involving subtraction and division.
teaching_strategy: Use a game where students work in pairs to find the HCF of three randomly chosen numbers. Then, have them solve a similar problem to the one in the example, where they need to find a number that, when 10 is subtracted, divides three given numbers exactly.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Finding the Highest Common Factor (HCF) using Prime Factorization and Division Methods
competency: Students will be able to find the HCF of given numbers using both prime factorization and division methods.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with prime numbers and practice finding factors. Conduct a game where students form teams to solve HCF problems using both methods. Provide guided practice with a variety of numbers.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Real-life Application of HCF in Distribution Problems
competency: Students will apply the concept of HCF to solve real-life distribution problems involving items like copies, pencils, food, and clothes.
teaching_strategy: Role-play scenarios where students distribute items equally among a group. Use props like small objects or pictures to represent the items. Encourage students to work in pairs or small groups to solve the problems.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will understand and find the least common multiples of given numbers through practical activities.
teaching_strategy: Use the activity method where students fill in the blanks and discuss the multiples of given numbers. Conduct a role-playing activity where students act as teachers explaining the concept of LCM to their peers.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Application of LCM in Real-life Scenarios
competency: Students will apply the concept of LCM to solve real-life problems involving distribution and grouping.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with real-life scenarios (e.g., distributing items among families) and have students solve them in groups. Follow up with a guided practice session where students create their own scenarios and solve them.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Determine the LCM of given numbers using the prime factorization method
teaching_strategy: Use the given rods to demonstrate the concept of LCM. Have students identify the multiples of each rod length and discuss how the shortest common multiple is 60 cm. Introduce the prime factorization method by breaking down the numbers 10, 20, and 30 into their prime factors and finding the LCM through this method.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Finding the Least Common Multiple (LCM) using Prime Factorization
competency: Students will be able to find the LCM of given numbers by prime factorization method and understand the process of identifying common and remaining prime factors to calculate the LCM.
teaching_strategy: Use a game where students work in pairs to find the prime factors of given numbers and then identify the common and remaining factors. This can be followed by a guided practice session where students calculate the LCM of different sets of numbers using the same method.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Least Common Multiple (LCM) using the Division Method
competency: Students will be able to find the LCM of given numbers using the division method.
teaching_strategy: Guide students through the division method for finding LCM by providing step-by-step instructions. Use a whiteboard or chart to demonstrate the process with the numbers 18, 24, and 36. Have students practice with different sets of numbers, such as 24, 36, and 56, to reinforce the concept. Encourage students to explain their reasoning and steps.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will understand and apply the concept of LCM to solve real-world problems involving grouping.
teaching_strategy: Use a game where students form groups of different sizes (e.g., 3, 5, and 6) and find the smallest number that can be evenly divided by all group sizes. This can be done through a role-playing activity where students act as students forming groups for different project works.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Finding the Least Common Multiple (LCM) to Determine Repeating Intervals
competency: Students will be able to calculate the LCM of two numbers to determine when two events with different intervals will coincide.
teaching_strategy: Use a game where students create intervals with different lengths of strings or sticks and find the LCM by physically aligning them. This can be followed by a guided practice where students calculate the LCM for given intervals.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Solving Real-World Problems Involving Time Intervals
competency: Students will be able to solve real-world problems involving time intervals by using both tabular and LCM methods.
teaching_strategy: Role-play a scenario where students are managing a school event with multiple activities happening at different intervals. Use a timeline or a large clock to visually demonstrate the intervals and when activities will coincide.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Finding the least number using the concept of LCM
competency: Students will be able to determine the least number that meets specific divisibility conditions through the application of LCM.
teaching_strategy: Use a game where students create numbers and apply the LCM method to find the least number that satisfies given divisibility conditions. For example, provide a set of numbers and ask students to find the least number that, when a certain number is added or subtracted, is divisible by the given numbers.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will be able to calculate the LCM of given numbers using the prime factorization method and apply it to solve real-world problems.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with prime numbers and have students identify the prime factors of given numbers. Conduct a guided practice session where students work in pairs to find the LCM of numbers like 28, 42, and 56. Use role-playing to simulate scenarios where LCM is needed, such as scheduling events or dividing students into groups.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Finding the Least Number Divisible by Multiple Numbers
competency: Students will be able to find the least number that is exactly divisible by multiple given numbers.
teaching_strategy: Create a game where students use a number line to find the least common multiple of numbers like 42, 49, and 63. Use manipulatives like blocks or counters to represent the numbers and visually demonstrate the concept. Encourage students to use the prime factorization method to solve these problems.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Find the least number that meets specific divisibility conditions and determine the LCM of given numbers through practical activities.
teaching_strategy: Use a paper strip or rod of different lengths (3 units, 11 units, and 33 units) to demonstrate the concept of LCM. Have students measure and find the smallest length that can be evenly divided by 3, 11, and 33. This can be done through hands-on activities like cutting strips or using rods to visually represent the LCM.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Representation of Integers on a Number Line
competency: Students will be able to identify and represent integers on a number line through group discussion and placement of given integers.
teaching_strategy: Divide students into groups and provide them with a number line. Have them identify and place integers represented by letters A, C, G, and I. Discuss how to represent integers 8, -2, 3, 0, and 6 on the number line. Use a number line to demonstrate moving 5 units to the right and left from any given point.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Addition of Integers Using Physical Objects
competency: Students will be able to add integers using physical objects and understand the concept of positive and negative numbers.
teaching_strategy: Use colored rectangular pieces of paper to represent positive and negative numbers. Have students take any two integers, place the appropriate number of '+' and '-' signs, and then pair them to find the sum. For example, demonstrate (-5) + (+3) by placing 5 '-' signs and 3 '+' signs, then removing pairs to find the result.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Addition of integers using number lines
competency: Students will be able to add integers by visualizing the process on a number line through group discussion and practical activities.
teaching_strategy: Use number lines for visual representation and have students engage in group discussions to solve addition problems. Provide guided practice by drawing number lines and marking the steps of addition.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand and apply the closure property of addition for integers.
teaching_strategy: Use number cards or a number line to demonstrate the closure property. Have students pick two integer cards, add them, and verify that the result is also an integer.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand and apply the commutative property of addition for integers.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a role-playing activity where students switch the order of numbers and add them, then compare the results to show that the sum remains the same regardless of the order.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand and apply the associative property of addition for integers.
teaching_strategy: Use number cards or a number line to demonstrate the associative property. Have students pick three integers, arrange them in different orders, and verify that the sum remains the same. For example, use cards labeled -3, -2, and -5 and show that [(–3) + (–2)] + (–5) = (–3) + [(–2) + (–5)].

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and use the additive inverse of integers.
teaching_strategy: Create flashcards with integers on one side and their additive inverses on the other. Use a game where students match the integers with their inverses. For example, use cards with -5 and +5, and (+2) and (-2). Discuss how the sum of any integer and its additive inverse is zero.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Addition of Integers Using Number Line
competency: Students will be able to add integers using a number line and understand the concept of positive and negative numbers.
teaching_strategy: Use a large number line on the classroom floor or create a digital number line. Have students physically move along the line to demonstrate addition of positive and negative integers. Provide flashcards with integer addition problems for guided practice.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Associative Law of Addition for Integers
competency: Students will understand and test the associative law of addition with integers.
teaching_strategy: Provide students with a set of integers and ask them to test the associative law through group activities or role-playing. Use real-life scenarios to make the concept more relatable.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Subtraction of Integers Using a Number Line
competency: Students will understand and perform subtraction of positive integers using a number line by moving right and left.
teaching_strategy: Use a physical or digital number line to demonstrate and practice moving right for positive values and left for negative values. Have students role-play Ram's journey, starting from the bus park and moving to point C, then back to point B. Provide additional examples for guided practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will apply the concept of integer subtraction to real-world scenarios.
teaching_strategy: Create a scenario where students calculate distances traveled in different directions. For example, a student goes 10 km east and then 7 km west. Use flashcards with positive and negative integer subtraction problems for quick practice.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Subtraction of Integers Using Number Line
competency: Students will be able to demonstrate the subtraction of integers using a number line and understand the concept of negative numbers.
teaching_strategy: Use a number line to visually represent the subtraction of integers. Have students perform the subtraction (–4) – (–5) and (–2) – (+5) on the number line, marking the starting point, the movement, and the final result. Provide flashcards with integer subtraction problems for guided practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will be able to simplify expressions involving addition and subtraction of positive and negative integers.
teaching_strategy: Provide students with a set of integer expression cards. Have them form groups and compete to see who can simplify the expressions the fastest. Use the example provided to guide the activity.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will understand the concept of absolute value and recognize that it represents the distance from zero on a number line, regardless of direction.
teaching_strategy: Use a number line to demonstrate the concept of absolute value. Have students identify the absolute values of various integers and discuss how they relate to the distance between points on the number line. Introduce the notation |a| and explain that it represents the absolute value of a.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Perform operations with integers using number lines and properties of integers (commutative and associative laws).
teaching_strategy: Use number lines to visually demonstrate addition and subtraction of integers. Engage students in role-playing where they act out addition and subtraction scenarios. Create flashcards for integers and their opposites for quick recall practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand and apply the concept of absolute value and opposites of integers.
teaching_strategy: Play a game where students match integers with their opposites and calculate absolute values. Use real-life examples to illustrate the concept of absolute value.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of integers
teaching_strategy: Use number lines and integer chips to demonstrate addition and subtraction of positive and negative integers. Engage students in a game where they move along a number line based on given integer operations.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate distance traveled in different directions
teaching_strategy: Create a role-playing activity where students act as bus drivers traveling different distances in various directions. Measure and compare distances to reinforce the concept of absolute value and direction.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand and apply the rules for multiplying integers with different signs.
teaching_strategy: Use a real-world example (bus travel) to introduce the concept of multiplying positive and negative integers. Provide a multiplication table activity to reinforce the rules, including both positive and negative integers.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Multiplication of Integers Using Number Lines
competency: Students will understand and apply the concept of multiplying positive and negative integers using number lines.
teaching_strategy: Use number line activities to visually demonstrate the multiplication of integers. Have students physically move along a number line to solve problems, reinforcing the concept of direction and magnitude in multiplication.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand and apply the closure and commutative properties of multiplication for integers.
teaching_strategy: Use a number line to demonstrate the multiplication of negative integers. Have students perform the multiplication (–2) × (–3) on a number line and verify the result is 6. Provide additional examples like (–5) × (+4) and (–4) × (–2) to illustrate the closure property. Use flashcards with pairs of integers for students to multiply in both orders, emphasizing the commutative property.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand and apply the associative property of multiplication with integers.
teaching_strategy: Have students work in pairs to choose three integers, calculate the product of the first two, and then multiply by the third. Discuss the results and confirm the associative property.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Apply the distributive property of multiplication over addition with integers.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with expressions like a(b + c) and a × b + a × c, and have students match the expressions to their simplified forms. Provide real-life examples such as distributing items among groups.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Multiplication of Integers Using Number Line
competency: Students will understand and apply the multiplication of positive and negative integers using a number line.
teaching_strategy: Use a large number line on the classroom floor or a digital number line for interactive activities. Have students physically move along the number line to demonstrate multiplication, reinforcing the concept of repeated addition and subtraction.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Multiplication of Integers with Multiple Factors and Associative Property
competency: Students will multiply integers with multiple factors and apply the associative property of multiplication.
teaching_strategy: Create a game where students form groups and are given sets of integers to multiply. Encourage them to explore different groupings and verify that the product remains the same, emphasizing the associative property. Use flashcards with integers for guided practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Apply the distributive property to simplify expressions involving integers.
teaching_strategy: Use a game where students match expressions with their simplified forms to reinforce the distributive property.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand and apply the rules for dividing integers with different signs.
teaching_strategy: Create flashcards with division problems and their solutions, then have students play a quick game where they match the problem to the correct answer.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Solve problems involving division and multiplication of integers using number lines and properties of operations.
teaching_strategy: Use number lines for visual representation and games like 'Integer Race' where students move forward or backward based on the operation to reinforce understanding.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Apply the associative and distributive properties of multiplication to simplify expressions.
teaching_strategy: Create flashcards with expressions and have students match them with their simplified forms. Use role-playing where students act out the properties in real-life scenarios.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Solve problems involving multiplication of integers using real-life scenarios.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with multiplication problems to reinforce the concept. Have students role-play scenarios where they apply multiplication of integers to solve real-life problems.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Application of Integer Rules in Quiz Scenarios
competency: Apply rules for scoring in a quiz contest involving positive and negative integers.
teaching_strategy: Create a quiz game where students earn points based on correct and incorrect answers. Use a scorecard to track points and discuss the outcomes of different answer combinations.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Multiplication of Integers on a Number Line
competency: Demonstrate understanding of multiplication involving positive and negative integers using a number line
teaching_strategy: Use a large number line on the classroom floor or create a digital number line. Have students physically move along the line to show the multiplication of integers. For example, for (+3) × (+2), students can start at +3 and move 2 steps to the right twice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Solve multiplication problems involving positive and negative integers
teaching_strategy: Create flashcards with multiplication problems. Use a game format where students race to solve the problems and place the correct answer on a board. For example, use (+3) × (–2) and (+3) × (–2) to practice negative integer multiplication.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Solve problems involving the simplification of integers using real-life scenarios (e.g., quiz contest scores).
teaching_strategy: Use a quiz contest scenario to engage students in solving problems related to the simplification of integers. Provide a real-life context to make the concept more relatable. Guide students through the process of translating the problem into a mathematical equation and solving it step-by-step.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will understand and apply the correct order of operations (PEMDAS/BODMAS) in solving arithmetic problems involving addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with expressions like (+12) + (–5) + (+25) ÷ (–5) – (–6) × (+7) to practice the order of operations. Have students identify and solve the operations in the correct order, discussing the importance of multiplication and division before addition and subtraction.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Application of Arithmetic in Real-Life Scenarios
competency: Students will apply arithmetic operations to solve real-life problems such as scoring in a quiz contest.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a role-playing activity where students act as quiz masters and contestants. Use the given scenarios to calculate scores based on correct and incorrect answers. This will help them understand the practical application of arithmetic in everyday situations.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate balance in a bank account after multiple transactions
teaching_strategy: Use a role-playing activity where students act as bank tellers and customers. Provide each student with a mock bank account and a set of transactions. Have them calculate the final balance and discuss their methods.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Solve for an unknown in a linear equation
teaching_strategy: Play a game where students are given a set of clues to find the value of a variable. For example, 'I am 2 more than five times your age. If I am 77, how old are you?' Use manipulatives or algebra tiles to help students visualize the equation.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand and apply operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division) on integers and recognize that division of integers may not always result in an integer.
teaching_strategy: Use number lines to demonstrate the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication of integers. Provide examples where division results in a non-integer, and introduce the concept of rational numbers.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Define rational numbers and understand their representation in the form of a/b where a and b are integers and b ≠ 0.
teaching_strategy: Create flashcards with fractions and have students identify which are rational numbers. Use real-life examples to illustrate the concept of rational numbers.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Definition and Identification of Rational Numbers
competency: Understand the definition of rational numbers and identify them as integers and natural numbers.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with examples of rational numbers (both integers and natural numbers) and non-rational numbers to help students differentiate. Engage students in a quick sort activity where they categorize numbers as rational or non-rational.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Recognize and apply the identity properties of addition and multiplication to rational numbers.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a role-playing activity where students act out the identity properties using real-life scenarios. For example, one student can be '0' and another '1', demonstrating how adding 0 or multiplying by 1 leaves the number unchanged.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand and apply the inverse properties of addition and multiplication for rational numbers.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pairs of rational numbers that are inverses of each other. Have students verify the inverse properties through role-playing scenarios where they demonstrate addition and multiplication operations resulting in zero and one, respectively.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Recognize and apply the commutative and associative properties of addition and multiplication for rational numbers.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a phonics game where students rearrange numbers to form equivalent expressions. For example, provide cards with numbers and operations, and have them form equations that demonstrate the commutative and associative properties. Use real-life examples to show how these properties are used in everyday situations.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand and apply the closure property for both addition and multiplication of rational numbers.
teaching_strategy: Use manipulatives or visual aids to demonstrate the closure property through examples. Have students create their own examples of adding and multiplying rational numbers to verify the closure property.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Convert fractions to decimal numbers and classify them as terminating or non-terminating recurring decimals.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a class activity where students convert given fractions into decimal numbers using division. Discuss the patterns observed in the decimal expansions to classify them as terminating or non-terminating recurring decimals.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand and differentiate between terminating and non-terminating decimals by converting fractions to decimal form and identifying patterns in the decimal representation.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with fractions on one side and their decimal equivalents on the other. Have students match the fractions with their decimal forms. Play a game where students take turns converting fractions to decimals and identifying whether the decimal is terminating or non-terminating.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Conversion of terminating decimal numbers into fractions
competency: Students will be able to convert terminating decimals into fractions by understanding the place value and using multiplication and division by the appropriate power of ten.
teaching_strategy: Use a number line to visually demonstrate the conversion of 0.75 to 3/4. Engage students in a game where they convert other terminating decimals to fractions using flashcards.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Conversion of non-terminating recurring decimal numbers into fractions
competency: Students will be able to convert non-terminating recurring decimals into fractions using algebraic methods.
teaching_strategy: Have students practice converting recurring decimals like 0.333... into fractions through role-playing where they solve for x in the equation 10x - x = 3. Provide guided practice with other recurring decimals.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and classify terminating and non-terminating recurring decimals
teaching_strategy: Use long division games or interactive division activities to demonstrate the conversion process. Have students practice with different fractions and categorize the results as terminating or non-terminating recurring decimals.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Convert decimal numbers to their fractional equivalents
teaching_strategy: Engage students in a fraction-decimal matching game where they convert given decimals to fractions and vice versa. Use flashcards with decimal numbers on one side and their fractional equivalents on the other.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will learn to find rational numbers between two given rational numbers by calculating the average of the numerators when denominators are the same, and by finding the average of the numbers themselves when denominators differ.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pairs of rational numbers to practice finding the average and identifying rational numbers in between. For example, use 1/2 and 5/6, and guide students to calculate the average of the numerators (1 and 5) and the average of the numbers themselves (0.5 and 0.833) to find rational numbers like 4/6 and 7/12.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will understand the method of converting repeating decimals into fractions.
teaching_strategy: Play a phonics game where students create repeating decimals and then convert them into fractions. For example, give them the decimal 0.4141..., and guide them through the steps of multiplying by 100, subtracting, and simplifying to find the fraction 41/99. Use role-playing to act out the steps of the problem, making it more engaging.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will be able to convert fractions into decimals and classify them as terminating or non-terminating recurring decimals.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with fractions on one side and their corresponding decimal representations on the other. Have students match the cards and discuss the differences between terminating and non-terminating recurring decimals.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will understand and calculate the additive and multiplicative inverses of given numbers.
teaching_strategy: Create a game where students roll a die and must find the additive or multiplicative inverse of the number rolled. For example, if a student rolls a 5, they must find the additive inverse (-5) or the multiplicative inverse (1/5).

subject: Mathematics
topic: Identifying Rational Numbers Between Two Given Fractions
competency: Students will be able to identify and write rational numbers between two given fractions.
teaching_strategy: Use number lines to demonstrate the placement of rational numbers between given fractions. Have students create their own number lines and identify rational numbers between two fractions.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will understand the properties of natural numbers, whole numbers, integers, and rational numbers.
teaching_strategy: Create a Venn diagram to show the relationships among natural numbers, whole numbers, integers, and rational numbers. Use flashcards with examples of each type of number to reinforce understanding. Conduct a class discussion to identify the characteristics of each set of numbers.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will be able to simplify fractions and add fractions with different denominators through group discussion and activity.
teaching_strategy: Use a group discussion to review fraction operations, followed by an activity where students calculate the total expenditure of Sirjana by adding fractions with different denominators.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Calculating Expenditure as a Fraction of Total Income
competency: Students will be able to calculate expenditure on specific items as a fraction of total income using both direct multiplication and model drawing methods.
teaching_strategy: Use a combination of direct calculation and model drawing to help students understand how to find a fraction of a total amount. Provide flashcards with different income and expenditure scenarios for guided practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate the number of boys and girls in a class given the fraction of boys.
teaching_strategy: Use a model drawing to visually represent the fraction of boys and girls in the class. Have students create their own model drawings using different numbers to practice the concept.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Solve problems involving ratios and proportions using basic arithmetic operations.
teaching_strategy: Use manipulatives like blocks or counters to represent boys and girls in the class. Have students physically count and group the blocks to find the number of boys and total students. This hands-on activity will help them understand the concept of proportions.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Compare and order fractions with different denominators by finding the least common multiple (LCM).
teaching_strategy: Create a fraction comparison game where students must quickly identify which fraction is larger or smaller. Use flashcards with fractions on them and have students compete to find the LCM and compare the fractions. This will make the learning process engaging and fun.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Convert fractions to have a common denominator and compare them
teaching_strategy: Use fraction circles or fraction bars to visually demonstrate the conversion process. Have students work in pairs to convert fractions to a common denominator and compare their results.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Perform addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division of fractions
teaching_strategy: Create a fraction scavenger hunt where students find and solve fraction problems hidden around the classroom. Use flashcards for quick practice sessions.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Solve problems involving fractions and decimals in real-life scenarios.
teaching_strategy: Use fraction games and role-playing to help students understand and apply fractions in practical situations. For example, create a role-play where students act out scenarios involving spending money and calculating fractions of amounts.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate and manage money based on given fractions and amounts.
teaching_strategy: Conduct guided practice sessions where students work in groups to solve money management problems. Use real-life examples and role-playing to make the learning more engaging and relatable.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will be able to solve problems involving fractions and present data in fractional form.
teaching_strategy: Use fraction games and role-playing to help students understand and apply fractions in real-life scenarios. For example, create a role-playing activity where students calculate the fraction of time spent on different activities during a school day.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will be able to handle and understand basic financial concepts such as money and parts of money.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with different amounts of money to practice identifying and calculating parts of money. For instance, create flashcards with Rs. 8,100 and ask students to find the part represented by Rs. 800.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will understand and apply the rules for adding, subtracting, multiplying, and dividing decimal numbers. They will also discuss the considerations for each operation in pairs.
teaching_strategy: Phonics games can be used to reinforce the pronunciation and spelling of decimal numbers. Role-playing can be employed to simulate real-life scenarios where decimal operations are needed, such as calculating money or measurements.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will calculate the perimeter of a rectangle using decimal measurements and understand the formula for perimeter.
teaching_strategy: Guided practice can be used where students measure objects in the classroom using rulers marked in decimal units and calculate their perimeters. Flashcards with decimal measurements can be used for quick recall practice.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Order of operations in simplifying expressions with decimals
competency: Students will understand and apply the correct order of operations (PEMDAS/BODMAS) when simplifying expressions involving decimals and multiple operations, including the use of brackets.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with expressions involving decimals and various operations. Have students identify the correct order of operations and simplify the expressions. Introduce the use of different types of brackets and their order of precedence through guided practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will be able to simplify complex arithmetic expressions and solve multi-step problems involving division, subtraction, and multiplication.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with arithmetic expressions for quick practice. Incorporate a 'math relay' game where students solve problems in teams, passing the answer to the next team member.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Area and Perimeter of Geometric Shapes
competency: Students will calculate the area and perimeter of triangles and rectangles, and solve for unknown dimensions given area or perimeter.
teaching_strategy: Create a 'real-world' activity where students measure and calculate the area and perimeter of different classroom objects. Use role-playing to act out scenarios where these measurements are needed, such as planning a garden or designing a room.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand and compare quantities using ratio
teaching_strategy: Use real-life examples like the weights of Anuja and Ramesh to introduce the concept of ratio. Have students calculate the difference and quotient to understand the concept of how quantities are compared.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and interpret ratios from given data
teaching_strategy: Conduct an activity where students observe a table of items and their prices. Ask them to discuss and calculate the ratio of prices to reinforce the concept of ratio.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate and simplify ratios, compare quantities using ratios, and understand the concept of ratio in different contexts.
teaching_strategy: Use real-life examples such as the price of items (copy, pencil, eraser) to introduce the concept of ratio. Engage students in a discussion about the relationship between the price of the copy and pencil, and the eraser and pencil. Introduce the concept of ratio as a comparison of two quantities. Provide a practical activity where students calculate the ratio of the diameter of a pencil to its length, emphasizing the importance of using the same units for comparison.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand the relationship between ratio and fraction, and apply it to real-world scenarios.
teaching_strategy: Use a circle divided into equal parts to demonstrate the concept of fractions and ratios. Have students draw their own circles and divide them into different numbers of equal parts. Ask them to write the fraction and ratio for the shaded and unshaded parts. Discuss the differences between fractions and ratios.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate and compare the capacity of different objects using ratios.
teaching_strategy: Provide students with two buckets of different capacities. Have them measure and record the capacities. Guide them to write the ratio of the capacities. Use this activity to reinforce the concept of ratio and its application in comparing quantities.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Solve problems involving ratios and proportions using practical activities like number line representations and real-life scenarios.
teaching_strategy: Use a number line to visually represent ratios. Have students create their own number lines and mark different segments to represent various ratios. For example, ask them to find the ratio of AB to BC on the given number line.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Compare fractions to determine which is greater and apply this to real-life situations.
teaching_strategy: Use a fraction wall or fraction circles to help students visualize and compare different fractions. Provide examples where students need to compare their own test scores or grades to understand the concept better.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will be able to find the ratio of two quantities and simplify them to the lowest terms.
teaching_strategy: Use a variety of examples, including real-life scenarios like the height of Anju and Aman, to demonstrate how to find and simplify ratios. Engage students with a 'ratio scavenger hunt' where they find and compare quantities in the classroom, such as the number of boys to girls or the number of desks to chairs. Provide flashcards with different pairs of numbers for students to practice simplifying ratios.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Interpreting Ratios on a Number Line
competency: Students will be able to interpret and find the ratio of distances on a given number line.
teaching_strategy: Create a number line on the floor using tape or chalk, and have students measure and find the ratio of different segments. Use role-playing where students are different points on the number line and act out the ratios. Provide guided practice with the given number line, asking students to find the ratios of various segments.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate and compare ratios of different quantities (students, teachers, heights, marks, and money).
teaching_strategy: Use real-life examples to demonstrate the concept of ratios. For example, use a set of colored blocks to represent students and teachers, and have students physically count and compare the quantities. Introduce the concept of ratios through role-playing scenarios where students act as teachers and students, and calculate the ratio of teachers to students in the classroom.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Divide a given amount of money in a specified ratio.
teaching_strategy: Create a game where students are given a set amount of play money and must divide it among themselves in a given ratio. For example, divide Rs 100 in the ratio of 3:2. Use flashcards with different ratios and amounts to practice this skill.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and create equivalent fractions through practical activities
teaching_strategy: Use the table completion activity to help students understand equivalent fractions. Provide additional examples for practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand the concept of proportion through visual representation
teaching_strategy: Use the squared paper activity to demonstrate the concept of proportion. Have students create their own figures and find the ratios to reinforce the idea.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand and apply the concept of proportions and ratios to compare scores in examinations.
teaching_strategy: Use a role-playing activity where students act as teachers comparing the scores of two students, Dipendra and Narmada, using ratios and proportions. Provide flashcards with different score combinations for students to practice identifying proportional relationships.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Determine if numbers are in proportion by comparing the product of the extremes and the product of the means, or by checking if the ratios of the corresponding numbers are equal.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pairs of numbers to practice calculating the product of the extremes and the product of the means. Have students work in pairs to check if given sets of numbers are in proportion using both methods.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will be able to identify and write ratios, determine if figures are in proportion, and solve problems involving ratios and proportions.
teaching_strategy: Use visual aids such as fraction circles or bars to demonstrate the concept of ratios. Engage students in a game where they match equivalent ratios using flashcards. For the proportion check, have students work in pairs to verify each other's answers using a truth table method.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will apply the concept of ratios to solve real-world problems.
teaching_strategy: Present a scenario where students need to calculate the score in science based on the given ratio. Use role-playing to simulate a classroom situation where students are scoring points in different subjects. Provide guided practice where students calculate the unknown value in a given ratio.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Solve problems involving proportional relationships in real-life scenarios such as pricing and mixing solutions.
teaching_strategy: Use a role-playing activity where students act as shopkeepers and customers to practice calculating prices of different quantities of oranges. Provide flashcards with various quantities and prices for practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand and apply the concept of ratio to solve practical problems involving mixing liquids.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a guided practice session where students measure and mix different volumes of water and honey to create lemonade, adjusting the quantities to maintain the same taste for varying numbers of people. Use a balance scale to visually demonstrate the concept of ratios.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate profit and loss using the formulas: Profit = Selling Price - Cost Price and Loss = Cost Price - Selling Price
teaching_strategy: Use real-life examples like Subas and Kamala to illustrate profit and loss. Have students solve similar problems in pairs or small groups.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Determine profit and loss percentage using the formulas: Profit Percentage = (Profit / Cost Price) * 100 and Loss Percentage = (Loss / Cost Price) * 100
teaching_strategy: Engage students in an activity where they analyze Mankaji's transactions. Use role-playing to simulate buying and selling scenarios, and have them calculate profit and loss percentages.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate profit and loss percentages using the given formulas
teaching_strategy: Use role-playing where students act as shopkeepers selling items at different prices. Provide them with cards with cost prices and selling prices. Have them calculate the profit or loss percentage and discuss their methods in groups.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Calculating Selling Price with Profit Percentage
competency: Students will be able to calculate the selling price of an item given the cost price and profit percentage using both direct calculation and model drawing methods.
teaching_strategy: Use a role-playing activity where students act as shopkeepers selling items at a certain profit. Provide flashcards with cost prices and profit percentages for practice. Introduce the concept of model drawing as a visual tool to solve such problems.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate cost price and selling price for a given profit percentage
teaching_strategy: Use role-playing where students act as mobile sellers to calculate cost and selling prices for different profit margins. Provide flashcards with varying selling prices and profit percentages for guided practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Solve simple algebraic equations to find unknown values
teaching_strategy: Create a game where students solve algebraic equations using physical objects or digital tools. Introduce the concept through a step-by-step guided practice session.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Profit and Loss Calculation Using Model Drawing
competency: Solve profit and loss problems using model drawing and algebraic methods
teaching_strategy: Use model drawing to visually represent the relationship between cost price, selling price, and profit/loss. Provide students with flashcards showing different cost and selling prices to practice identifying profit or loss and calculating the percentage.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate profit or loss percentage in various scenarios involving the purchase and sale of items.
teaching_strategy: Use real-life examples such as the ones provided in the textbook. Have students work in pairs to solve similar problems. Introduce a game where students role-play buying and selling items, calculating profit or loss percentages. Provide flashcards with different purchase and sale scenarios for quick practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Determine the cost price or selling price given the profit or loss percentage.
teaching_strategy: Create a role-playing activity where students act as shopkeepers and customers. Provide them with a set of items with known cost prices and have them negotiate selling prices based on a given profit margin. Use guided practice with flashcards showing different cost prices and profit percentages to calculate selling prices.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Apply the unitary method to find the price of a given number of objects based on the price of a single unit.
teaching_strategy: Use a real-life scenario like the banana purchase to demonstrate the unitary method. Have students work in pairs to solve the problem and discuss the steps involved.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand and identify direct variation between two quantities and explain the relationship between them.
teaching_strategy: Conduct an activity where students fill in the missing prices in a table based on the given prices. Discuss the relationship between the number of copies and the total price, emphasizing the concept of direct variation.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Solve problems involving direct proportion using ratios and division
teaching_strategy: Use a role-playing activity where students act as shopkeepers and customers to practice calculating prices of multiple items based on the price of a single item. Provide flashcards with different quantities and prices for practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand and apply the concept of indirect variation in practical scenarios.
teaching_strategy: Use role-playing to simulate the scenario of workers and days to complete a task. Have students act out different numbers of workers and observe how the time to complete the work changes. This will help them grasp the inverse relationship between the number of workers and the time required.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Solve problems involving indirect variation.
teaching_strategy: Create flashcards with pairs of numbers representing the number of workers and the corresponding days to complete a task. Use these flashcards in a guided practice session where students must determine the number of days given the number of workers or vice versa. This will reinforce their understanding of indirect variation through practical application.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Solve problems involving indirect variation
teaching_strategy: Use real-life examples such as the number of workers and days to dig a field. Create a role-playing activity where students act as project managers and allocate workers to complete tasks within a given time frame.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Differentiate between direct and indirect variation and solve related problems
teaching_strategy: Create flashcards with direct and indirect variation statements. Have students match the correct type of variation and solve the given problems using guided practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Solve real-life problems using linear equations
teaching_strategy: Use role-playing to act out scenarios where students buy items and calculate costs. Provide flashcards with different items and their prices for practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Convert units of speed and distance
teaching_strategy: Create a speedometer game where students convert speeds from km/h to m/min. Use a timer to measure how long it takes to travel a certain distance at different speeds.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate the number of chairs in a square arrangement and determine the percentage increase in chairs.
teaching_strategy: Use a physical square arrangement of chairs to demonstrate the concept. Have students work in groups to solve the problem using manipulatives and discuss their methods.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Find the next time when traffic lights change together based on their intervals.
teaching_strategy: Create a timeline or use a number line to visually represent the intervals and find the LCM. Engage students in a role-playing activity where they act out the changing of traffic lights.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate the cost price and selling price of eggs to achieve a specific profit or loss percentage.
teaching_strategy: Use real-life examples and role-play scenarios where students act as shopkeepers selling eggs. Provide flashcards with different egg quantities and prices to practice calculations.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Determine the work rate of workers and calculate the time required to complete a task.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a guided practice session where students calculate the work rate of different numbers of workers. Use a large wall or board to visually represent the wall being painted and have students estimate the time needed.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Prove the associative and distributive properties of integers
teaching_strategy: Use manipulatives or number lines to demonstrate the associative and distributive properties. Have students work in pairs to verify the properties using specific integers.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Solve problems involving addition and multiplication of integers, and find integers based on given conditions
teaching_strategy: Create a game where students form teams to find pairs of integers that meet specific criteria (e.g., sum, difference). Use flashcards with integers for practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and work with rational numbers
teaching_strategy: Use a number line to demonstrate the placement of rational numbers between given fractions. For example, plot 1/2 and 2/3 on a number line and ask students to find two rational numbers between them. Provide flashcards with fractions and have students identify numbers that lie between them.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Solve real-world problems involving rational numbers
teaching_strategy: Create a role-play scenario where students have to calculate the total number of pages read by a character over two days. Use manipulatives like fraction circles or fraction bars to help students visualize the addition of fractions. Encourage students to explain their reasoning and methods.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Perimeter and Area of Geometric Shapes
competency: Calculate the perimeter and surface area of given solid objects and understand the concept of perimeter for triangles.
teaching_strategy: Divide students into groups and have them measure the edges of a set square to calculate the perimeter. Use physical objects like set squares to make the concept tangible.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand the concept of direct variation through practical activities.
teaching_strategy: Conduct an activity where students measure the lengths of the edges of different shapes and calculate the perimeter to explore the relationship between the lengths of the sides and the perimeter.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate the perimeter of a triangle given the lengths of its sides
teaching_strategy: Use physical objects or a digital tool to measure and add the lengths of the sides of different triangles. Have students create their own triangles with given side lengths and calculate the perimeter. Provide real-life examples such as calculating the length of a fence needed for a triangular garden.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Application of Perimeter in Real-Life Scenarios
competency: Apply the concept of perimeter to solve practical problems
teaching_strategy: Conduct a role-playing activity where students are given the role of a land developer or a farmer. They need to calculate the perimeter of different plots of land with given dimensions and determine the length of fencing required. Use a variety of shapes and dimensions to challenge students.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate the length of an unknown side of a triangle given the perimeter and lengths of the other two sides.
teaching_strategy: Use a hands-on activity where students measure and cut strips of paper to represent the sides of a triangle. Have them calculate the length of the missing side using the given perimeter.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Determine the total cost of materials needed to fence a triangular area based on the perimeter and cost per unit length.
teaching_strategy: Create a role-playing scenario where students act as shopkeepers and customers. Provide them with different lengths of wire and prices, and have them calculate the total cost for fencing a triangular plot.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate the cost of materials based on given rates and quantities
teaching_strategy: Use real-life scenarios to demonstrate cost calculation. Provide students with different rates and quantities to practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Determine the perimeter of irregular shapes by summing the lengths of all sides
teaching_strategy: Have students measure and add the lengths of sticks or strings to find the perimeter of various shapes. Use physical objects or interactive software for hands-on learning.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate the perimeter of given triangles using the formula P = a + b + c
teaching_strategy: Use physical cutouts of triangles to demonstrate the concept of perimeter. Have students measure the sides and calculate the perimeter. Provide flashcards with different triangle dimensions for practice.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Application of Perimeter in Real-life Scenarios
competency: Apply the concept of perimeter to solve real-life problems such as fencing a triangular land
teaching_strategy: Conduct a role-playing activity where students act as land developers. They must calculate the perimeter of a triangular plot and determine how many times a given length of wire can be used to fence it. Use a 540 m wire and an equilateral triangle with a side of 18 m for practical calculations.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate the perimeter of a triangle and determine the cost of materials needed to enclose it multiple times.
teaching_strategy: Use a real-world scenario where students measure the perimeter of a triangular garden and calculate the cost of enclosing it 20 times using a plastic rope. Provide students with a plastic rope and have them measure and mark the lengths on the ground. Discuss the concept of cost per unit length and calculate the total cost.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Determine the unknown lengths of sides in given triangles using the perimeter formula.
teaching_strategy: Engage students in a hands-on activity where they use sticks and a rope to form triangles and measure the perimeters.
