teaching_strategy: Have students draw the shapes on graph paper and label the vertices. Conduct a role-playing activity where students describe the properties of the shapes formed, such as the number of sides and angles. Use guided practice to reinforce the concepts.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Plotting points and identifying coordinates of a square
competency: Students will be able to plot points on a coordinate plane and determine the coordinates of vertices of a square.
teaching_strategy: Use graph paper and have students plot the points J(-4, 4), K(4, 4), and L(4, -4). Guide them to identify the coordinates of point M and the length of JK through discussion and measurement.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Creating and analyzing geometric figures on a coordinate plane
competency: Students will create a geometric figure on a large graph paper and identify the coordinates of its vertices.
teaching_strategy: Provide each student with a large graph paper. Instruct them to draw a figure and label the coordinates of at least five vertices. Encourage them to present their work in class and discuss the coordinates.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and classify symmetrical figures and understand the concept of axis of symmetry
teaching_strategy: Divide students into groups and have them discuss and identify symmetrical figures from given examples. Use tracing to reinforce the concept of line symmetry.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand and apply the concept of line symmetry
teaching_strategy: Provide hands-on activity where students trace figures to identify lines of symmetry. Discuss the number of lines of symmetry in each figure.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and count the number of lines of symmetry in given figures
teaching_strategy: Have students draw figures with different numbers of lines of symmetry. Provide cutouts of various shapes and ask them to fold the shapes to identify the lines of symmetry. Discuss the concept of axis of symmetry and mirror line through practical activities.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Apply the concept of symmetry in real-life situations
teaching_strategy: Conduct an activity where students fold a piece of paper and cut out shapes. Discuss the number of lines of symmetry in the resulting shapes. Encourage students to create their own symmetrical designs.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and count the number of axes of line symmetry in given figures
teaching_strategy: Provide students with various figures and have them identify and count the axes of symmetry. Use physical objects or transparencies for hands-on practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand and demonstrate point symmetry through practical activities
teaching_strategy: Conduct an activity where students trace figures on transparent plastic, press at the center point, and rotate to observe the symmetry. Encourage class discussion and presentation of findings.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify letters and shapes with point symmetry through rotation
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with letters and shapes. Have students rotate the cards around a central point to identify those that remain symmetrical.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and complete figures based on axis of symmetry and count the number of lines of symmetry.
teaching_strategy: Provide students with cutouts of the given figures. Have them fold the figures along the axis of symmetry to see where the lines of symmetry lie. Encourage them to draw the lines of symmetry on the figures and count them. Use flashcards with different figures to reinforce the concept.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Recognize figures with point symmetry and perform 180° rotations around a center point.
teaching_strategy: Use a pin and a paper to demonstrate point symmetry. Place the pin at the center point and rotate the paper 180° to show how the figure looks the same. Provide students with tracing paper and have them trace and rotate the given figures around point O. Discuss the properties of figures with point symmetry.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and create figures with line and point symmetry through practical activities
teaching_strategy: Provide students with different colored papers and guide them to fold and cut the papers to form figures with line and point symmetry. Encourage them to present these figures in class and discuss their findings.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Recognize and classify tessellating shapes in real-life objects
teaching_strategy: Show students various figures and have them identify the types and number of shapes used. Discuss examples of tessellations found in household items such as Nanglo, carpets, Doko, brick or stone walls, and footballs. Encourage students to observe and discuss how these tessellations are maintained.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Create and discuss tessellations using geometric shapes
teaching_strategy: Students will cut and paste triangular pieces on chart paper to create a tessellation, then discuss the concept with peers.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and create triangular tessellations through practical activities such as drawing, coloring, and project work.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with different triangular shapes for identification. Engage students in group activities where they create tessellations using given dots and real-life objects like tiles and carpets. Encourage them to observe and replicate patterns found in their surroundings.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and discuss properties of reflection in figures
teaching_strategy: Use physical objects like mirrors or reflective surfaces to demonstrate and discuss the properties of reflection with students. Have students observe and answer questions about the distance and size of images in mirrors.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Perform and understand the concept of folding as a form of transformation
teaching_strategy: Conduct a hands-on activity where students fold a piece of paper to understand the concept of reflection and symmetry. Discuss how the folded paper represents the reflection of an object.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand the concept of reflection, identify the image of an object, and determine the axis of reflection.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a hands-on activity where students fold a paper to create a line of symmetry. Have them identify the image of a given object and measure the distance from the axis of reflection. Encourage group discussion to reinforce the concept.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Recognize and label the axis of reflection in geometric figures.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with different geometric shapes folded along their lines of symmetry. Ask students to identify the axis of reflection and the image of each point. Provide guided practice by asking them to draw the axis of reflection and the image of given points on a coordinate plane.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and understand the properties of reflection, including congruence and equal distance from the axis of reflection.
teaching_strategy: Use a mirror or tracing paper to demonstrate reflection. Have students identify the axis of reflection and measure the distance between the object and its image. Conduct a role-playing activity where students reflect points across the X-axis and record the coordinates of the images.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand the concept of reflection on the X-axis and the transformation of coordinates.
teaching_strategy: Create a game where students use flashcards with coordinates to practice finding the reflected points. Provide guided practice where students reflect points across the X-axis and record the new coordinates.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Reflection of Points on the Coordinate Plane
competency: Understand and apply the rules for reflecting points about the X-axis and Y-axis
teaching_strategy: Use graph paper and markers to plot points and their images. Have students create their own examples and swap papers to find the images of each other's points. Introduce the concept of symmetry and discuss how the coordinates change during reflection.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will be able to draw and write the image of given geometrical figures with reflection lines.
teaching_strategy: Use tracing paper or mirrors to demonstrate reflection. Have students practice drawing reflections of points and lines across the X-axis and a given line m. Provide flashcards with various geometrical figures for guided practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will be able to reflect points and lines across the Y-axis and X-axis using graph paper and identify the coordinates of the reflected points.
teaching_strategy: Use graph paper and markers to demonstrate the reflection of points and lines across the Y-axis and X-axis. Have students practice by plotting the given points and lines, and identifying the coordinates of the reflected points. Use flashcards with coordinates for quick practice sessions.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will be able to find the length of segments formed by the original and reflected points.
teaching_strategy: Introduce the distance formula and demonstrate how to calculate the length of segments using the coordinates of the original and reflected points. Provide guided practice where students calculate the lengths of TT' and PP' using the distance formula. Use a ruler and graph paper for practical measurement exercises.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and describe the translation of points on a coordinate plane
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with coordinates to practice identifying translated points. Have students play a game where they must quickly identify the translated coordinates of given points.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Define and explain the concept of translation in geometry
teaching_strategy: Conduct a role-playing activity where students act out translations of simple shapes. Discuss the direction and distance involved in each translation.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Translation of Points and Line Segments
competency: Students will understand and apply the concept of translation to congruent objects and learn to translate points and line segments accurately.
teaching_strategy: Use a grid or coordinate plane to demonstrate translation. Have students perform translations using graph paper, where they draw a line segment and then translate it in a given direction and magnitude. Use flashcards with points and line segments for guided practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will understand and perform translations of geometric figures with given magnitude and direction.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with geometric figures and have students translate them on graph paper, marking the original and translated points. Provide real-life examples such as sliding a book on a table to illustrate the concept.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will apply the concept of translation to real-life scenarios.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a role-playing activity where students simulate sliding objects (like toys or books) on different surfaces and discuss whether the movement is a translation. Use a game where students have to identify if given movements are translations.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will understand and identify cardinal and intercardinal directions using a compass and be able to explain the significance of each direction.
teaching_strategy: Engage students in a group activity where they create a compass rose. Provide each group with a piece of paper and instruct them to fold it twice to form a compass rose. Discuss the meaning of each direction (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW) and their applications.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will learn the concept of bearing and practice creating scale drawings to represent directions.
teaching_strategy: Divide students into small groups and have them create scale drawings of a simple map using the bearing concept. Provide them with a compass and a ruler to accurately measure and draw directions. Encourage them to label each direction clearly and discuss the practical applications of bearing in real-life scenarios.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Understanding and Measuring Angles in Compass Directions
competency: Students will be able to identify and measure angles between compass directions and understand the concept of bearing.
teaching_strategy: Use a compass rose diagram to demonstrate the angles between different compass directions. Engage students in a hands-on activity where they fold a paper to create a compass rose and measure the angles using a protractor. Discuss the concept of bearing and have students practice identifying and measuring angles in various directions.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will be able to identify and determine the bearing of various places within a municipality using a base point.
teaching_strategy: Have students trace the given figure in their exercise books and use the municipality building as a reference point. Divide them into groups and ask them to find the bearing of the Temple, School, Buspark, Hospital, Police station, and Water tank. Encourage them to discuss their findings with their peers and present their results in class.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will understand and apply the concept of scale in drawing and measurements.
teaching_strategy: Form groups and provide each group with a scale drawing of a volleyball court. Explain the scale (1 cm = 200 cm) and ask students to measure and calculate the actual dimensions of the court. Use this activity to reinforce the concept of scale and its practical application.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will understand and apply the concept of scale and ratio to measure and represent real-world objects in a smaller or larger scale.
teaching_strategy: Use a real-life example of a volleyball court to demonstrate how to calculate the scale and apply it to create a map. Engage students in a hands-on activity where they measure the dimensions of the court and then create a scaled-down map using a 1 cm = 200 cm scale. Discuss the importance of accuracy in measurements and the practical applications of scale in mapping and design.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Application of Scale in Real-World Problems
competency: Students will solve problems involving scale and ratio to find real distances from scaled measurements.
teaching_strategy: Provide students with a map example where the scale is 1 cm = 500 m. Have them work in groups to calculate the real distance between two places given the scaled distance. Use a guided practice session where students solve similar problems, reinforcing the concept of scaling and ratio. Encourage students to explain their thought process and solutions to the class.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will be able to determine the bearing of points on a map and calculate real distances using a given scale.
teaching_strategy: Use a compass rose to demonstrate the concept of bearing. Have students practice by identifying the bearing of different points on a map. For the scale calculation, use a ruler and a scale model to show how to convert map distances to real distances. Provide hands-on activities where students measure and calculate real distances based on given scales.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will be able to read and interpret real maps to determine bearings between different locations.
teaching_strategy: Provide a real map of Nepal and have students identify and mark the locations of the cities mentioned in the questions. Use a protractor to measure the bearings between these points. Encourage students to use a compass to understand the direction and angles involved.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Apply scale drawing to represent real-world objects and calculate dimensions.
teaching_strategy: Use a ruler and a piece of graph paper to draw the room map. Discuss the concept of scale and how it is used in real-life applications such as maps and blueprints.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate real dimensions from given scale drawings and vice versa.
teaching_strategy: Provide students with different scale drawings of objects and have them calculate the real dimensions. Use flashcards with scale drawings to make the activity more engaging.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify congruent angles and determine symmetry in geometric figures
teaching_strategy: Use tracing paper to overlay the figure and demonstrate congruence. Conduct a hands-on activity where students create their own figures with congruent angles and discuss the types of symmetry present.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand the concept of reflection and its effect on congruence
teaching_strategy: Use graph paper and markers to plot points and reflect them across the x-axis. Have students compare the original and reflected figures to identify congruence. Introduce the concept of transformations and discuss the properties of congruent figures.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify letters with line symmetry and find their images after reflection
teaching_strategy: Use mirror activities to demonstrate line symmetry in letters V and H. Have students identify and draw lines of symmetry for other letters like A, M, O, etc. Use flashcards for practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Determine coordinates of points and their reflections on axes
teaching_strategy: Use graph paper and markers to plot points and reflect them on the X-axis and Y-axis. Engage students in a game where they call out the coordinates of reflected points to reinforce learning.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will be able to calculate distances and bearings using scale drawings and apply this knowledge to real-world scenarios.
teaching_strategy: Use a map or a large-scale drawing on the board. Have students practice by creating their own scale drawings. Conduct a group activity where students trace the given figure and calculate the bearing of different places from Kathmandu using a protractor and a compass. Provide flashcards with different locations for additional practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Use a given scale to calculate real distances
teaching_strategy: Provide students with a map or diagram of a village and a scale (1 cm = 100 m). Have them measure the distances between different points (e.g., Hat bazar to Health post, Temple to Post office) using a ruler and then calculate the real distances. Use flashcards with distances to reinforce the concept.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Determine the bearing of one location from another
teaching_strategy: Use a compass or a protractor to demonstrate how to determine the bearing of one location from another. Have students practice by identifying the bearing of the school, Hat bazar, and post office from the health post. Conduct a role-playing activity where students navigate from one location to another using bearings.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will understand and complete a frequency distribution table for given data.
teaching_strategy: Provide students with additional sets of numerical data and have them create their own frequency distribution tables. Use flashcards with different sets of numbers to practice tallying and frequency counting.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Analyze and extract information from a line graph to answer questions about sales data.
teaching_strategy: Use Dolma's sales data to create a line graph on the board. Have students work in pairs to answer the questions (a) to (d). Encourage them to discuss their findings and justify their answers.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Understand the steps involved in constructing a line graph.
teaching_strategy: Guide students through the steps of constructing a line graph using the given data. Provide flashcards with sample data for practice. Have students create their own line graph based on a different set of data.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Analyze and extract data from a line graph to answer questions about sales trends over time.
teaching_strategy: Use a similar line graph with different data points and have students work in pairs to answer questions. Provide flashcards with months and their corresponding sales numbers for reference.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Construct a frequency table based on the data presented in a line graph.
teaching_strategy: Guide students through the process of creating a frequency table using the given data. Use role-playing where students act as shopkeepers and customers to practice recording sales data.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will learn to plot and interpret data on a line graph using rainfall measurements over a week.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with rainfall data to practice plotting points on a graph. Have students create their own line graph using different data sets for practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Analyze and extract information from a line graph, create a frequency table, and understand temperature variations over time.
teaching_strategy: Use a temperature line graph to conduct a class discussion on interpreting data. Have students play a game where they create their own line graph based on given temperature data. Introduce the concept of frequency tables by having students count and categorize the data points.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Represent data in line graphs and understand trends over time or across different years.
teaching_strategy: Create a timeline of the school's enrollment growth using the provided data. Use this as a basis for a role-playing activity where students act as school administrators discussing the changes in student numbers over the years. Introduce the concept of line graphs by having students plot the given enrollment data.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Measure and record daily temperatures at different times and represent them in a line graph.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a practical activity where students measure the temperature at 10 am, 12 pm, 2 pm, and 4 pm using thermometers. Have them record the temperatures and create a line graph to visualize the temperature changes throughout the day.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Interpret and analyze data presented in a multiple bar graph.
teaching_strategy: Use the provided bar graph to teach students how to read and interpret multiple bar graphs. Engage them in a discussion to answer the questions (a) to (d) and create similar bar graphs based on their own data on game preferences.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Analyze and interpret data presented in a multiple bar graph to answer questions about the number of students, boys, and girls in different classes.
teaching_strategy: Use the bar graph to conduct a class discussion and have students work in pairs to answer the questions. Provide flashcards with class numbers and have students match them with the correct bar heights. Use a guided practice session where students create their own multiple bar graphs based on given data.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Identify and explain the characteristics of a multiple bar graph, including the representation of multiple sets of data and the equal width of bars.
teaching_strategy: Explain the concept of a multiple bar graph by comparing it to a simple bar graph. Use visual aids to demonstrate the differences. Have students create their own simple and multiple bar graphs using provided data to reinforce the concept.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Represent and interpret data using multiple bar graphs
teaching_strategy: Provide students with different sets of data and have them create multiple bar graphs. Use flashcards with pre-drawn axes and scales for guided practice. Encourage students to label axes, title the graph, and include a key to differentiate between categories.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Analyze and extract data from a multiple bar diagram to answer questions about student performance across different grades.
teaching_strategy: Use the bar graph to conduct a class discussion on interpreting data. Have students work in groups to answer the questions and then share their findings. Utilize flashcards with different grades and bar heights for a visual aid.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Students will be able to represent and interpret data using multiple bar graphs.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with different data sets for students to practice creating multiple bar graphs. Have students work in pairs to create and interpret multiple bar graphs based on provided data.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Analyze and interpret data from multiple bar graphs to answer questions about student performance and production statistics.
teaching_strategy: Use the provided SEE results bar graph to conduct a class discussion on interpreting bar graphs. Have students work in groups to answer the questions and then present their findings to the class. Follow up with a project where students collect and represent their own data on student participation in various games.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Create and interpret bar and line graphs, calculate temperature changes, and understand interest rates over time.
teaching_strategy: Use real-life data to create bar and line graphs. Have students role-play as meteorologists presenting weather data or as bankers explaining interest rates. Provide flashcards with temperature data for practice.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Calculate temperature differences and understand annual interest rate trends.
teaching_strategy: Engage students in guided practice with temperature data using flashcards. Use the line graph to discuss interest rate trends over years, and have students calculate interest amounts for given periods.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Analyze data to identify trends and patterns
teaching_strategy: Use a game where students compete to find the year with the highest and lowest interest rates. Provide a set of cards with different years and interest rates. Students can use a bar graph to visually compare the rates.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Compare and contrast data to draw conclusions
teaching_strategy: Create a role-playing activity where students represent the village and discuss the population changes over the years. Use flashcards with years and population numbers to facilitate quick comparisons.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Interpret data from a multiple bar graph
teaching_strategy: Guide students through a guided practice session where they analyze the sales data for potatoes and cauliflowers. Use the graph to teach them how to read and compare data visually.

subject: Mathematics
competency: Analyze and interpret data from a given graph to answer questions about sales quantities and fluctuations.
teaching_strategy: Use a bar graph or line graph to represent the sales data. Have students work in pairs to answer the questions, discussing their methods and reasoning. Introduce the concept of percentage increase using the third week's cauliflower sales data as an example.

subject: Mathematics
competency: संख्याहरूको विभाजन गर्ने तथा विभाजन गुणांक पत्ता लगाउने।
teaching_strategy: स्टूडेंटहरूले 24 र 8 दहाइका विभाजन गर्न सक्नुहुन्छन्। यसको लागि नेपाली न्यूर्सी कुर्सरी नोटहरू वा गणितको गणना गर्ने वस्तुहरू उपयोग गर्न सकिन्छ।

subject: Mathematics
competency: संख्याहरूको गुणन गर्ने र गुणन गुणांक पत्ता लगाउने।
teaching_strategy: स्टूडेंटहरूले 24 र 8 दहाइका गुणन गर्न सक्नुहुन्छन्। यसको लागि गुणन गुणांक गणना गर्ने वस्तुहरू उपयोग गर्न सकिन्छ।

subject: Mathematics
competency: सेटको वर्गीकरण गर्ने तथा खालील सेटहर सक्रिय अभ्यास गर्ने।
teaching_strategy: सेटको वर्गीकरण गर्ने लागि काउंटर वा फसल जस्ता वस्तुहर अभ्यास गर्नुहोस्। उदाहरणका लागि, बालकहरूले काउंटर वा फसलहरूले ग्रुप बनाउन सक्छन् जुन त्यसमा खालील सेटहर वर्गीकरण गर्नुपर्छ। यदि बालकहरूले खालील सेटहर अभ्यास गर्नुपर्दछन् त्यसपर उनलाई दिइएको फसलहरूले ग्रुप बनाउन सक्छन्।

subject: Mathematics
competency: खालील सेटको परिभाषा र उदाहरणहरू देखिने तथा उनको वर्गीकरण गर्ने।
teaching_strategy: फसल वा कुर्सीहरूले ग्रुप बनाउन खालील सेटहर उदाहरणहरू देखिने तथा उनको वर्गीकरण गर्नुहोस्। उदाहरणका लागि, बालकहरूले फसलहरूले ग्रुप बनाउन खालील सेटहर उदाहरणहरू देखिने तथा उनको वर्गीकरण गर्न सक्छन्।

subject: Mathematics
competency: सेटहरूको समानता र बराबरता पत्ता लगाउने
teaching_strategy: सेटहरूको उदाहरणहरू दिएको र विद्यार्थीहरूले सेटहरूको समानता र बराबरता ज्ञात गर्ने अभ्यास गराउने

subject: Mathematics
competency: समुच्चय र समुच्चय समानता र अन्तर निर्धारण
teaching_strategy: समुच्चय र उनको समानता र अन्तर लागि विकल्पहरू तर संबंधित उदाहरणहरू उपयोग गर्नुहोस्। उदाहरणका लागि, विद्यार्थीहरूले विभिन्न समुच्चयहरू तर उनको समानता र अन्तर जान्नको लागि विकल्पहरू तर उदाहरणहरू उपयोग गर्नुहोस्।

subject: Mathematics
competency: समग्र सेट विश्लेषण र वर्गीकरण गर्ने क्षमता पत्ता लगाउनुहोस्
teaching_strategy: संख्याहरूको समग्र सेट बनाउनुपर्ने व्यवस्थित शिक्षण गर्नुहोस्, जसमा विभिन्न संख्याहरूको वर्गीकरण र उनको समग्र सेट निर्धारण छात्रहरूको लागि अनुकूल छ।

subject: Mathematics
competency: संख्याहरूको विभिन्न वर्गहरूमा वर्गीकरण र उनको समग्र सेट निर्धारण गर्ने क्षमता पत्ता लगाउनुहोस्
teaching_strategy: संख्याहरूको वर्गीकरण गर्ने अभ्यास र उनको समग्र सेट निर्धारण गर्ने अभ्यास गर्नुपर्ने व्यवस्थित शिक्षण गर्नुहोस्, जसमा छात्रहरूले विभिन्न संख्याहरूको वर्गीकरण र समग्र सेट निर्धारण गर्न सक्नुपर्छ।

subject: Mathematics
competency: सम संख्याहरू र विषम संख्याहरूलाई पत्ता लगाउनुहोस् र उनका फरक ज्ञात गर्नुहोस्।
teaching_strategy: सम संख्याहरू र विषम संख्याहरूलाई गणितको ग्राफ पर दर्शाउँछौं र उनका फरक गणना गर्नुहोस्। उदाहरणका रूपमा, 2, 4, 6, 8 र 3, 5, 7, 9 जस्ता संख्याहरूलाई दिइयो र उनका फरक गणना गर्नुहोस्।

subject: Mathematics
competency: समुच्चय र उनको अन्तर ज्ञात गर्ने
teaching_strategy: समुच्चय र उनको अन्तर जान्ने लागि विभिन्न समुच्चय ले ग्राहकहरूको बीच तर्क गर्नुहोस्। उदाहरणका रूपमा अंक र वस्तुहरूको समुच्चय ले ग्राहकहरूले गणना र तर्क गर्न सक्नुहुन्छ।

subject: Mathematics
competency: संख्या अनुक्रम र उनको अनुक्रम संख्या ज्ञात गर्ने
teaching_strategy: संख्या अनुक्रम ले ग्राहकहरूले अनुक्रम संख्या ज्ञात र गणना गर्न सक्नुहुन्छ। उदाहरणका रूपमा अंक र वस्तुहरूको अनुक्रम ले ग्राहकहरूले गणना र तर्क गर्न सक्नुहुन्छ।

subject: Mathematics
competency: समुच्चय र उपसमुच्चय सम्बन्धित अवधारणाहरू विश्लेषण र तर सम्बन्ध जान्नु
teaching_strategy: समुच्चय र उपसमुच्चय उदाहरणहरू उपयोग गरेर व्याख्या गर्नुहोस्। उदाहरणका साथ विद्यार्थीहरूले समुच्चय र उपसमुच्चय जान्नकाली दिएका समुच्चयहरूको उपसमुच्चयहरू ज्ञात गर्नुहुन्छ।

subject: Mathematics
competency: समुच्चय का अनुक्रम र उपसमुच्चय ज्ञान र पत्ता लगाउने
teaching_strategy: समुच्चय र उपसमुच्चय जानकारी दिन्छ र उदाहरणहरू साथ उदाहरण दिन्छ। उदाहरण रूपमा अल्फाबेट र संख्याहरू वाले समुच्चय र उपसमुच्चय ले व्यवस्थित शिक्षण गर्न सकिन्छ।

subject: Mathematics
competency: समुच्चय का सम्बन्ध ज्ञान र पत्ता लगाउने

teaching_strategy: संख्याहरूको अनुपात र अनुपातीको अनुपात गणना गर्दा विद्यार्थीहरूले विभिन्न संख्याहरूको अनुपात र अनुपातीको अनुपात गणना गर्ने र उनको अनुपातीको अनुपात निर्धारण गर्ने अभ्यास गर्नुपर्छ। यसको लागि विद्यार्थीहरूले विभिन्न संख्याहरूको अनुपात र अनुपातीको अनुपात गणना गर्ने र उनको अनुपातीको अनुपात निर्धारण गर्ने अभ्यास गर्नुपर्छ।

subject: Social Studies
topic: संख्याहरूको योग र अंतर निर्णय गर्ने
competency: संख्याहरूको योग र अंतर निर्णय गर्दै र उनको व्याख्या गर्ने।
teaching_strategy: संख्याहरूको योग र अंतर निर्णय गर्ने लागि न्यूपाउट र न्यूरोलर नोटहरूको दिइयो र छात्रहरूले योग र अंतर निर्णय गर्नुपर्छ।

subject: Social Studies
competency: संख्याहरूको अनुपात र अनुपातीको गणना गर्ने तथ्य र अनुसार गणना गर्ने क्षमता विकसित गर्नुहोस्। यसमा दहाइ, सय र पत्ता लगाउने जस्ता अनुपातीको गणना शामिल छन्। उदाहरण र अभ्यासहरू दिएको छन्।
teaching_strategy: संख्याहरूको अनुपात र अनुपातीको गणना गर्ने तथ्यहरू देखि उदाहरणहरू दिएको छन्। यसमा दहाइ, सय र पत्ता लगाउने जस्ता अनुपातीको गणना शामिल छन्। यसको लागि नोट्स, बीचमा र बीचमा दहाइ र सय लगाउने अभ्यास गर्नुपर्छ।

subject: Social Studies
competency: संख्याहरूको अनुपात र अनुपातीको गुणनफल गणना गर्ने तथा उनको अनुपात ज्ञात गर्ने क्षमता पनि विकसित गर्नुहोस्।
teaching_strategy: संख्याहरूको अनुपात र अनुपातीको गुणनफल गणना गर्दा नीतिबाट गुना र भाग गणितका अभ्यास समावेश गर्नुहोस्। उदाहरण र अभ्यास सामग्री दिइएको छ।

subject: Social Studies
competency: संख्याहरूको योग र घटाहरू गर्ने तथ्य र अनुप्रयोग समावेश गर्नुहोस्।
teaching_strategy: संख्याहरूको योग र घटाहरू गर्ने अभ्यास सामग्री उपयोग गर्नुहोस्। उदाहरणका लागि, नीपर र बीकर र नीपर र बीकरको योग र घटाहरू गर्ने अभ्यास सामग्री उपयोग गर्नुहोस्।

subject: English
competency: Describe personal experiences and activities during educational tours
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Students can act out scenarios where they are on an educational tour, discussing what they did and where they went.

subject: English
competency: Match words with their meanings and understand context
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images to reinforce vocabulary. Create a game where students match words to their meanings using a jumbled word format.

subject: English
competency: Answer questions related to a scenario and develop reasoning skills
teaching_strategy: Role-play the scenario of a school trip to the zoo. Have students take turns asking and answering the questions in small groups. Encourage them to provide logical reasons for their answers.

subject: English
competency: Practice pronouncing words with stress marks and use of would/could in dialogue.
teaching_strategy: Have students practice pronouncing the given words and then act out the dialogue in pairs. Use flashcards with the words for drilling and repetition.

subject: English
competency: Form questions using would, could, and can in real-life situations.
teaching_strategy: Provide scenarios and have students form questions using would, could, and can. Use role-playing activities where students can practice these questions in pairs or small groups.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to convert statements into yes/no questions using appropriate auxiliary verbs.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Create a phonics game where students form yes/no questions by changing the statements provided. Use flashcards with statements and have students form questions by flipping the cards and rearranging them.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to use can, could, and would in appropriate contexts and apply negation.
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Conduct role-playing activities where students practice using can, could, and would in different scenarios. For example, one student can ask another if they can help with a task, and the other can respond using could or would.

subject: English
competency: Develop listening skills by analyzing a picture and audio, and completing a timetable.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures for the listening activity. Play the audio and have students fill in the timetable based on the information provided. Conduct a role-play where students ask and answer questions similar to those in the audio.

subject: English
competency: Identify text type and content summary.
teaching_strategy: Create a game where students match different text types (e.g., narrative, descriptive, informative) with their descriptions. Have students read the given text and discuss what they think it is about.

subject: English
competency: Students will learn to write a formal letter requesting additional resources for a computer lab, including specific details about the current situation and the desired improvements.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students act as students writing a letter to the headteacher requesting more computer lab resources. They can use the provided letter as a model and modify it to fit their own needs.

subject: English
topic: Identifying and addressing needs in a computer lab
competency: Students will identify the current deficiencies in a computer lab and propose solutions to improve the learning environment.
teaching_strategy: Group discussion where students list the necessary components of a well-equipped computer lab and discuss the benefits of each. Follow with a brainstorming session to suggest ways to address the identified deficiencies.

subject: English
competency: Unscramble and write words based on their meanings
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Use phonetic sounds to unscramble the words. For example, 'amirdaleb' can be broken down into 'a-mi-r-de-l-a-b' and then matched with the meaning 'admiring'.

subject: English
competency: Understand and answer questions based on a given letter
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Assign students roles to read and act out the letter. Discuss the questions as a class to enhance comprehension.

subject: English
topic: Impact of Computer Lab on Studies
competency: Discuss the impact of the computer lab on studies
teaching_strategy: Group Discussion: Divide students into small groups and ask them to discuss how the computer lab is affecting their studies. Encourage them to share personal experiences and insights.

subject: English
competency: Complete sentences using appropriate words
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Provide students with similar sentences and ask them to complete them. Use flashcards with missing words to reinforce vocabulary and sentence structure.

subject: English
competency: Form and use present simple tense to construct correct sentences
teaching_strategy: Provide students with flashcards containing verbs and prepositions. Have them form sentences using the example provided, such as 'The bus to Dharan leaves at 9:00 a.m.' Encourage them to create their own sentences using the given verbs and context.

subject: English
competency: Identify and use correct form of verbs in present simple tense
teaching_strategy: Use a guided practice method where students fill in the blanks with the correct form of the verbs provided in the brackets. For example, 'Peter Hanson starts his day at 7:00. He has his breakfast in the kitchen with all the family.' This can be done through a worksheet or interactive online activity.

subject: English
competency: Understand and describe daily routines and activities of the Hanson kids
teaching_strategy: Role-playing the daily activities of the Hanson kids using flashcards to represent different activities and times of the day.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and interpret a sports timetable
teaching_strategy: Create a sports timetable for a class event, use a similar format as the one provided, and have students fill in the dates and times for different activities.

subject: English
competency: Design and create a weekly timetable for a class, incorporating subject allocation, time slots, and days of the week. Enhance presentation skills by making the timetable visually appealing.
teaching_strategy: Divide students into groups and provide them with a template or guide to help them design their timetables. Encourage creativity and critical thinking by allowing them to propose their preferred study times and subjects. Use this activity to teach time management and organization skills.

subject: English
competency: Identify and understand common abbreviations used in dictionaries to enhance vocabulary and comprehension skills.
teaching_strategy: Create flashcards with the abbreviations and their meanings. Use role-playing activities where students have to interpret sentences or phrases written in abbreviated form. Provide a list of sample sentences and have students identify the abbreviations and their meanings.

subject: English
competency: Analyze situational contexts to infer appropriate permissions
teaching_strategy: Use role-playing scenarios where students act out situations and practice asking for and granting permissions.

subject: English
competency: Describe scenes based on visual cues
teaching_strategy: Create flashcards with different scenes and have students describe what they see, focusing on key details.

subject: English
competency: Developing skills for independent travel, including safety measures and packing essentials.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out scenarios where they are traveling independently, practicing what to say to parents or guardians when requesting permission to travel alone and what items to pack.

subject: English
competency: Understanding the importance of family bonds and responsibilities towards family members.
teaching_strategy: Discussion: Facilitate a class discussion on the importance of visiting grandparents and the responsibilities that come with it. Encourage students to share their own experiences.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand the importance of emotional support and develop coping mechanisms to handle fear and anxiety.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out the scenario where the boy feels scared on the train. Encourage them to come up with their own coping mechanisms and share them with the class.

subject: English
competency: Students will recognize the role of parental guidance and effective communication in providing comfort and security.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Discuss the importance of open communication between parents and children. Have students write a letter to a family member expressing their feelings and seeking comfort.

subject: English
competency: Analyze sentences to determine the speaker and the purpose of the remarks.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity: Have students act out the scenarios in the sentences, assigning different students to be the speakers and explaining their purposes.

subject: English
competency: Understand and answer questions related to the story.
teaching_strategy: Discussion: Pose the comprehension questions to the class and facilitate a group discussion to encourage critical thinking and analysis of the story.

subject: English
competency: Practice matching questions with appropriate responses and role-playing scenarios
teaching_strategy: Pair work and role-playing

subject: English
competency: Study given situations and take turns asking for and responding to permission
teaching_strategy: Scenario-based role-playing and guided practice

subject: English
competency: Developing question formation skills in response to given statements
teaching_strategy: Phonics games where students match statements with questions to practice question formation.

subject: English
competency: Transforming declarative sentences into questions
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activities where students act out scenarios and transform statements into questions.

subject: English
competency: Develop the ability to form and answer yes/no questions and provide honest responses.
teaching_strategy: Use a 'Question of the Day' activity where students ask and answer questions related to their daily lives. Incorporate a role-playing game where students pair up and practice asking and answering questions.

subject: English
competency: Create a story based on given outlines and develop a suitable title.
teaching_strategy: Engage students in a storytelling session where they brainstorm ideas for the story. Use a 'Story Map' template to guide them in structuring their narrative. Encourage creativity by discussing the moral or lesson the story might convey.

subject: English
competency: Analyze the impact of personal changes on broader communities and the world.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing Activity: Divide students into small groups and assign each group a different level of change (world, nation, town, family). Have them discuss and present how changes at one level can influence the others.

subject: English
competency: Develop critical thinking skills by analyzing and interpreting text and images.
teaching_strategy: Questioning Game: Use the picture and the text to create a questioning game. Ask students to formulate questions based on the picture and the poem, encouraging them to think deeply about the content.

subject: English
competency: Students will learn and apply vocabulary words such as change, suddenly, realize, focus, impacts, and indeed in context.
teaching_strategy: Phonics games and flashcards can be used to reinforce the pronunciation and spelling of these words. Guided practice can be done through completing sentences.

subject: English
competency: Students will analyze a poem to understand the poet's emotions and intentions, and discuss the implications of the poet's actions.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing can be used to help students understand the poet's feelings and motivations. Discussion questions can be used to guide the analysis of the poem.

subject: English
competency: Determine the truth of statements and answer questions based on a conversation
teaching_strategy: Play the conversation audio twice. For the first listen, students complete the True or False statements. For the second listen, they answer the questions using one-word answers. Use flashcards with the statements and questions for reinforcement.

subject: English
competency: Compose a formal email requesting permission
teaching_strategy: Provide students with a model email. Have them identify key components such as the salutation, body, and closing. Conduct a role-playing activity where students write and deliver their own emails requesting permission for school activities.

subject: English
competency: Compose a response email to a request for using the school hall.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into pairs. One student acts as the headteacher, and the other acts as Kabir Jha. They practice writing and delivering the reply email.

subject: English
competency: Create a poem on a chosen topic and present it to the class.
teaching_strategy: Flashcard activity: Create flashcards with different topics (e.g., nature, love, friendship). Students pick a card and write a poem on the given topic. Share poems in small groups.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to identify common places for announcements and discuss scenarios where announcements might be made.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing different scenarios where announcements are made (e.g., school assembly, public announcements in a market) and have students act out the situations. Follow up with a class discussion on the effectiveness and importance of announcements in these settings.

subject: English
competency: Understand and deliver formal announcements
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity: Students can practice delivering pre-flight announcements in pairs or groups. Each student can take turns being the announcer and the audience can provide feedback on clarity and tone.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and participate in school celebrations
teaching_strategy: Cultural event simulation: Organize a mock Parents Day celebration in the classroom. Students can prepare speeches, organize a photo session, and perform a short play or skit. This activity helps students understand the importance of such events and their role in the school community.

subject: English
competency: Understand and apply safety rules and etiquette during air travel
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out scenarios where they are boarding an airplane. Assign roles such as passengers, flight attendants, and pilots. Discuss and practice the correct responses to pre-flight announcements and safety instructions.

subject: English
competency: Identify and organize key elements of event planning and announcements
teaching_strategy: Guided practice: Provide students with a list of announcements and events. Ask them to categorize the announcements and identify the purpose of each. Create a mock event and have students write and deliver relevant announcements.

subject: English
competency: Understand and articulate the significance of Parents Day, organize a school event, and engage in communication activities.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students role-play as class captains/monitors preparing an announcement for Parents Day. Encourage them to include details such as the event, date, venue, participants, and how to attend. Use flashcards with key phrases to practice pronunciation and communication skills.

subject: English
competency: Improve pronunciation of specific English sounds.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Create a phonics game where students must identify and pronounce words with the 'r' sound correctly. Use the provided words as examples and have students practice saying them out loud.

subject: English
competency: Practice making and responding to requests in real-life situations through pair work and role-playing
teaching_strategy: Divide students into pairs and provide them with picture cards. Have them practice making and responding to requests based on the scenarios provided. Encourage the use of different expressions and phrases.

subject: English
competency: Utilize contextual clues to make and respond to requests effectively
teaching_strategy: Provide students with a set of clues related to the scenarios. Instruct them to take turns making requests and responding, using the clues to guide their conversation. This activity helps improve their comprehension and communication skills.

subject: English
competency: Developing skills to understand and interpret spoken English through context-based questions
teaching_strategy: Use role-playing to act out the scenario described in the audio. Have students take turns being the girl, her father, and her brother or friend. This will help them better understand the context and improve their listening skills.

subject: English
competency: Enhancing critical thinking and communication skills by analyzing visual and auditory information
teaching_strategy: Create a 'Question of the Day' activity where students bring in pictures or short audio clips and ask questions about them. This encourages active participation and prepares them for real-world communication.

subject: English
competency: Match questions with their reported speech and identify changes.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Create a phonics game where students match questions to their reported speech forms. Use flashcards with questions on one side and reported speech on the other. Encourage students to identify the changes in sentence structure.

subject: English
competency: Convert questions into reported speech.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Provide students with a set of questions and guide them through the process of converting them into reported speech. Use role-playing activities where students act out the scenarios, such as a father asking his daughter about her spending habits and a farmer discussing the sale of oxen.

subject: English
competency: Students will learn to sort laundry by fabric type and color, check care labels, and use appropriate washing methods for delicate items.
teaching_strategy: Use sorting games where students categorize clothes into piles based on fabric type and color. Have students act out washing scenarios, demonstrating the correct use of a washing machine, including adding detergent and fabric softener according to the machine's manual.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand the importance of not overloading the washing machine and the correct use of washing cycles.
teaching_strategy: Create a role-playing activity where students simulate using a washing machine. Provide them with different load sizes and fabric types, and have them choose the appropriate washing cycle based on the care label. Use flashcards with washing machine settings to reinforce learning.

subject: English
competency: Identify appropriate water temperature settings for different types of laundry based on fabric type and dirt level.
teaching_strategy: Create a sorting game where students categorize laundry items into hot, warm, and cold water washes using flashcards with images and labels.

subject: English
competency: Understand the importance of regular cleaning and proper air drying of washing machines.
teaching_strategy: Role-play a scenario where students demonstrate the correct way to clean and air out a washing machine, emphasizing the use of a cleaning solution and leaving the door open.

subject: English
competency: Understand the importance of separating laundry and maximize clothes cleanliness.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into groups and assign roles such as a family member discussing the importance of separating laundry. Each group can present their role-play to the class.

subject: English
competency: Recognize the importance of cleaning the washing machine and its effects of overloading.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Provide students with a washing machine model and have them identify parts that need regular cleaning. Discuss the consequences of overloading the machine through a group discussion or a short quiz.

subject: English
competency: Understand and apply the rules for using commas in series, after transitional phrases, and in direct quoted speech and tag questions.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Create a phonics game where students form sentences using commas correctly. Provide examples like 'He bought bananas, apples, oranges, and cheese.' and have students identify and correct any errors.

subject: English
competency: Understand and apply the rules for using semicolons to connect independent clauses and separate items in a series with commas, and use colons to introduce items or lists and to qualify sentences by introducing meaning or an explanation.
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Divide students into groups and assign them to create sentences using semicolons and colons correctly. For example, 'I am going to America this year; I will study MBBS there.' and 'She was feeling really down last week: she had failed her exam and lost her job.' Each group can present their sentences to the class for feedback.

subject: English
competency: Develop skills in observing and describing visual content
teaching_strategy: Use the pictures to engage students in a descriptive activity. Have students describe the activities in the pictures using adjectives and verbs. For example, 'The person is skiing down the snowy hill.'

subject: English
competency: Share personal experiences to enhance communication skills
teaching_strategy: Organize a role-playing activity where students share their recent visits to new places. Provide flashcards with common travel-related vocabulary to support their speech.

subject: English
competency: Understand the unique cultural and geographical aspects of Mustang, Nepal, including its recent opening to tourism and the challenges of visiting during winter months.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students act as tourists planning a trip to Mustang, discussing the necessary permits and the impact of tourism on local culture.

subject: English
competency: Describe interactions with local communities during a visit to Mustang, emphasizing the hospitality and daily living conditions.
teaching_strategy: Flashcard activity where students match descriptions of daily living conditions with images or short videos of local life in Mustang.

subject: English
topic: Cultural and Religious Significance of Muktinath Temple
competency: Understand the cultural and religious importance of Muktinath Temple for both Hindus and Buddhists, and the significance of the five elements symbolized by the flags.
teaching_strategy: Create a role-playing activity where students act as pilgrims from different religions, discussing their reasons for visiting the temple and the meaning of the five elements.

subject: English
topic: Travel Experience and Community Life in Marpha
competency: Describe the experience of visiting Muktinath and Marpha, including the natural scenery and the unique architecture of Marpha.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of the Himalayas, Muktinath Temple, and Marpha houses to help students visualize the locations. Have students create their own flashcards and share their descriptions of the places.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to use new vocabulary in context and understand the cultural and historical significance of architecture and pilgrimages.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards for vocabulary practice. Have students role-play scenarios where they use the new words in sentences.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to sequence events in a narrative and improve their comprehension skills.
teaching_strategy: Create a timeline activity where students arrange the sentences in the correct order. Discuss the sequence and its significance in the story.

subject: English
competency: Understand the historical context of tourism in Mustang and sequence events of a journey.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing the journey from Kathmandu to Mustang, using flashcards with key locations like Pokhara, Tatopani, and Kagbeni. Have students sequence the events of the journey based on the given sentences.

subject: English
competency: Identify and use different verb tenses in narrative writing.
teaching_strategy: Guided practice with underlined verbs in the paragraph. Create a game where students match verbs with their tenses and discuss the context in which each tense is used.

subject: English
topic: Verb Tenses and Past Simple vs. Present Perfect
competency: Students will be able to distinguish between past simple and present perfect tenses and use them appropriately in sentences.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with sentences in both past simple and present perfect tenses. Have students match the correct tense to the given context. Conduct a role-play activity where students create their own sentences using the verbs provided in the box.

subject: English
topic: Past Simple vs. Present Perfect Continuous
competency: Students will understand the difference between past simple and present perfect continuous tenses and apply them correctly.
teaching_strategy: Create a timeline on the board showing different time periods. Give students scenarios and ask them to write sentences using the correct tense. Use a game where students have to quickly identify and correct sentences with incorrect tenses.

subject: English
competency: Identify and use past simple tense in sentences
teaching_strategy: Provide flashcards with sentences in past simple tense and have students fill in the blanks with the correct verb. Use role-playing to act out scenarios involving the past simple tense.

subject: English
competency: Understand and complete sentences based on audio input
teaching_strategy: Play the audio and have students write down the missing words. Use guided practice to fill in the blanks with appropriate words. Follow up with a discussion on the speaker's experiences.

subject: English
competency: Engage in discussions about the value of volunteering and express personal opinions.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into groups and assign roles (e.g., volunteers, community members). Have them discuss the benefits and challenges of volunteering.

subject: English
competency: Compose paragraphs based on personal experiences and include relevant details.
teaching_strategy: Guided Writing: Provide students with a structured outline (event, time, lesson learned) and have them write about a memorable experience. Use the provided examples as a reference.

subject: English
competency: Practice asking and answering questions in pairs to share personal experiences.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into pairs and have them take turns asking and answering the provided questions. Use real-life examples to make the conversation more engaging.

subject: English
competency: Understand and interpret a diary entry to answer related questions.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Read the diary entry aloud and ask students to identify key details. Use flashcards with questions to test comprehension and encourage discussion.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand and appreciate the cultural and social aspects of rural life in Nepal, including traditional food, family interactions, and community support.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out scenes of introducing themselves to a new family, preparing and serving a traditional meal, and playing games with children. Use flashcards with pictures of Nepali dishes and animals to enhance learning.

subject: English
competency: Students will develop observational and descriptive skills by documenting their experiences and surroundings during a trip, including noting the physical environment and interactions with locals.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Provide students with a journal or diary template. Ask them to write about a day in their own community, focusing on the environment, people they meet, and activities they engage in. Encourage them to include descriptive details and reflections on their experiences.

subject: English
competency: Understand word meanings and apply them in context
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with the words and their meanings to reinforce learning. Create a matching game where students match the words in Column A with their correct meanings in Column B.

subject: English
competency: Read and comprehend texts, and make inferences based on the information provided
teaching_strategy: Role-play the scenario where Neil visits Nepal. Ask students to infer Neil's feelings and experiences based on the given statements. Discuss as a class to ensure understanding.

subject: English
competency: Students will practice forming sentences using past simple and present perfect tenses, including negative forms.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Create a phonics game where students form sentences using the correct verb tenses. For example, provide them with verb cards and sentence structure cards, and have them match and form correct sentences.

subject: English

subject: English
topic: Past Tense and Present Perfect Tense

subject: English
competency: Form questions using auxiliary verbs and future tense.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a role-playing activity where students ask each other questions about future plans. For example, 'Will you visit a museum this weekend?' 'Did you sing a song just now?'

subject: English
competency: Identify and classify open, closed, and hyphenated compound words in English.
teaching_strategy: Create a sorting game where students categorize given compound words into open, closed, and hyphenated types. Use flashcards with examples and have students work in pairs to sort them.

subject: English
competency: Describe actions of people in pictures and propose convincing strategies.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out scenarios where they need to convince others to do something. For example, one student can be Bikash watching TV, and another can be a parent asking Bikash to help in the kitchen. Encourage students to use persuasive language and logical arguments.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and discuss the concept of fairy tales and imaginative thinking.
teaching_strategy: Discussion and Storytelling: Initiate a class discussion on fairy tales. Ask students if they have heard or read any fairy tales. Provide examples of common fairy tale elements and encourage students to share their own stories or ideas. Use flashcards with images of magical creatures or settings to spark imagination and creativity.

subject: English
competency: Recognize the importance of not harming others and the value of making wise decisions.

subject: English
competency: Apply logical reasoning to solve problems and meet needs.
teaching_strategy: Guide students through a problem-solving activity where they brainstorm other items the couple might request from the lime tree and discuss the potential outcomes of each request.

subject: English
competency: Understand and analyze the moral of the story through character actions and dialogue.

subject: English
competency: Identify and use new vocabulary and complex sentence structures in context.

subject: English
competency: Identify and use synonyms in context
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Create a phonics game where students match words with their synonyms. For example, 'terrified' can be matched with 'scared', 'pleaded' with 'asked', 'delighted' with 'happy', 'idiot' with 'fool', and 'scared' with 'afraid'.

subject: English
competency: Arrange events in chronological order
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Have students act out the sequence of events from the story. Assign roles such as the old man, old woman, and the lime tree. Guide them to arrange the events in the correct order and discuss the implications of each event.

subject: English
competency: Understand and answer questions based on a story about an old man and a lime tree, including the old people's benefits and personal opinions.

subject: English

subject: English

subject: English

subject: English
competency: Identify and use correct forms of direct and indirect speech in sentences involving negative commands and requests.

subject: English

subject: English
competency: Encourage students to set goals and overcome challenges through determination and courage

subject: English

subject: English

subject: English

subject: English

subject: English

subject: English

subject: English

teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out scenarios where they encourage a friend to participate in activities they enjoy, such as a dance competition or athletics. Use the provided examples to guide the role-play.

subject: English
competency: Correct and apply punctuation rules in writing
teaching_strategy: Phonics games: Use a game where students must add correct punctuation marks to sentences. Provide the sentence 'David didn't really like school but he did enjoy practical subjects where he could use his hands to make things. He also loved biology because he could draw lots of diagrams and do experiments.' for practice.

subject: English
competency: Understand and apply common prefixes in English words
teaching_strategy: Create a prefix bingo game where students match prefixes with their meanings and examples. Use flashcards with words containing different prefixes for a quick review session.

subject: English

teaching_strategy: Develop a suffix scavenger hunt where students find and categorize words with specific suffixes in a given text. Use role-playing to demonstrate the usage of suffixes in sentences.

subject: English

teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of various activities. Have students describe the actions and then engage in a role-playing activity where they act out the scenes from the pictures.

subject: English

teaching_strategy: Create a circle discussion where each student shares their last experience of attending a celebration. Use guided questions to ensure all students participate.

subject: English

subject: English

subject: English

subject: English

subject: English

subject: English

teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Divide students into groups and assign each group a sentence to act out. After each group performs, discuss the sentence structure and categorize it into the correct column.

subject: English

subject: English
competency: Identify and use correct verb forms in different contexts.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Create flashcards with verbs in different tenses (e.g., 'service', 'take', 'open', 'buy', 'clean', 'do', 'play', 'check'). Use a timer and have students race to match the correct verb form with the action. For example, 'service' - 'having the mechanic service her scooter'.

subject: English

subject: English

subject: English

teaching_strategy: Play the audio clip and have students work in pairs to answer the questions. Follow up with a class discussion to review the answers.
