subject: English
competency: Learn the pronunciation of college-related words
teaching_strategy: Use phonics games or a mobile app for pronunciation practice

subject: English
competency: Identify adjectives and form their comparative and superlative forms
teaching_strategy: Create flashcards with adjectives and their comparative and superlative forms for guided practice

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to make and understand comparative and superlative sentences using 'bigger', 'scarier', 'slim', 'expensive', 'windier', 'juicier', and 'tidier'.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a pair activity where students ask and answer questions using given clues. Provide examples and encourage students to create their own comparisons.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to compare weather conditions and daily observations.
teaching_strategy: Use real-life examples or weather reports to discuss and compare weather conditions. Engage students in a guided practice session where they compare current weather with past weather conditions.

subject: English
competency: Identify similarities and differences between objects and concepts
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of the objects (train/aeroplane, lemon/orange, etc.) and have students match and discuss similarities and differences. Use role-playing to act out scenarios involving 'our neighbours/yours' and 'tiger/lion' to practice context-specific comparisons.

subject: English
competency: Understand and compare information about frogs and toads
teaching_strategy: Play the audio about frogs and toads. Use a Venn diagram to fill in the information about their similarities and differences. Conduct a guided practice session where students listen to the audio again and answer the questions about their physical characteristics and behaviors.

subject: English
topic: Comparison of Cultural and Economic Characteristics of Bhujung and Bhada Villages
competency: Students will be able to compare and contrast the cultural, economic, and geographical features of two different villages and present their findings in a written description.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards to list key features of each village. Divide the class into groups, assign each group a village, and have them research and compile a list of similarities and differences. Afterward, have each group present their findings to the class, followed by a class discussion to consolidate the information.

subject: English
competency: Understand the significance of smartphones in daily life and their various uses.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity: Divide students into groups and assign each group a scenario where they need to use a smartphone for a specific task (e.g., checking the weather, sending an urgent message, making a video call). Have them act out the scenario and discuss the importance of smartphones in their daily lives.

subject: English
competency: Recognize the impact of easy access to information on memory and behavior.
teaching_strategy: Discussion activity: Ask students to reflect on how they use smartphones to find information and discuss the potential drawbacks of relying heavily on instant information access. Use flashcards with examples of information that can be easily retrieved to facilitate the discussion.

subject: English
topic: Impact of Smartphones on Daily Habits
competency: Analyze the influence of smartphones on daily routines and behavior.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students act out different scenarios of daily activities involving the use of smartphones. Discuss the implications of constant connectivity and the convenience it brings.

subject: English
competency: Identify and use new vocabulary in context.
teaching_strategy: Flashcard game where students match words with their meanings. Use the given letters to fill in the blanks and discuss the context of each word.

subject: English
competency: Analyze the emotional and physical effects of mobile phone usage and discuss the benefits and drawbacks.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing scenarios where students act out different feelings when missing their mobile phones and discuss ways to use smartphones productively. Use flashcards to list positive and negative impacts of constant mobile phone use.

subject: English
competency: Identify and use adverbs and comparative forms in sentences.
teaching_strategy: Create a game where students match adverbs with their comparative forms and use them in sentences. For example, 'carefully' - 'more carefully', 'hard' - 'harder', 'beautifully' - 'more beautifully'. Use a competitive activity where students race to complete sentences correctly.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand and use comparative and superlative forms of adjectives and adverbs.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pairs of words (e.g., good/better, bad/worse) and have students match them. Conduct a role-play where students compare two scenarios using comparative and superlative forms.

subject: English
competency: Students will conduct a survey, collect data, and present it in a graphical format.
teaching_strategy: Divide the class into small groups and assign each group a different purpose of mobile phone use. Guide them through the process of creating a survey form, collecting data, and then presenting the findings in a pie chart or bar graph. Discuss the importance of accurate data representation.

subject: English
competency: Identify and use appropriate vocabulary
teaching_strategy: Create a word matching game where students match the meanings with the correct words from the text. Use flashcards for each word and its definition.

subject: English
competency: Understand and interpret text
teaching_strategy: Have students read the text and answer the questions. Discuss the answers as a class to ensure comprehension and provide additional context where necessary.

subject: English
competency: Correctly pronounce words with -tion and -sion endings and understand their sounds.
teaching_strategy: Phonics games where students match words with their correct pronunciations.

subject: English
competency: Write a vacancy advertisement and use prepositions correctly in sentences.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing scenarios where students create and read out vacancy advertisements, followed by guided practice using prepositions in sentences.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use time-related phrases and expressions in context.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing daily routines. Have students act out scenarios where they brush their teeth in the evening and start school on Monday.

subject: English
competency: Identify and use prepositions correctly in sentences.
teaching_strategy: Flashcard activity. Create flashcards with prepositions and have students place them in sentences like 'Put the papers in the dustbin.'

subject: English
competency: Practice making and responding to invitations in various social contexts
teaching_strategy: Role-playing and pair work

subject: English
competency: Engage in discussions about personal preferences and social interactions
teaching_strategy: Creative writing and group discussion

subject: English
topic: Invitations and Formal vs. Informal Communication
competency: Students will learn to recognize and write both formal and informal invitations, understanding the appropriate context for each.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into pairs. One student acts as Rahim, sending an informal invitation, and the other acts as Pratik, responding to the invitation. Switch roles after each round.

subject: English
topic: Cultural Practices: Inviting Guests to Home Functions
competency: Students will understand and practice the language used to invite guests to various home functions.
teaching_strategy: Flashcards: Create flashcards with different home functions (e.g., birthday party, wedding, dinner). Students should practice using appropriate invitation language for each function.

subject: English
competency: Read the given texts and answer questions based on the context.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out scenarios where they send and receive emails. Use the Rahim and Pratik example to practice writing and understanding email content.

subject: English
competency: Identify family members and understand the significance of community events.
teaching_strategy: Flashcards: Create flashcards with names and relationships. Use them to practice identifying family members. Discuss the importance of community events like Bratabandha.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to form and use question tags correctly in sentences.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Create a phonics game where students match question tags to their corresponding statements. For example, provide cards with statements and question tags, and have students find the correct pair.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to analyze and discuss social interactions and their implications.
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Divide the class into small groups and assign roles to Rahim and Pratik. Have them act out different scenarios of inviting friends, discussing the reasons and methods behind the invitation, and then present their scenarios to the class.

subject: English
topic: Expressions for inviting, accepting, and declining invitations
competency: Students will learn and practice expressions used in social interactions to invite, accept, and decline invitations.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing scenarios where students practice inviting friends for coffee, dinner, or a party. Use flashcards with invitation phrases for guided practice.

subject: English
competency: Understand the life and contributions of Sir Isaac Newton in mathematics and science
teaching_strategy: Role-playing Isaac Newton's life journey, from his early years as a farmer to his achievements at Cambridge University. Use flashcards to highlight key events and inventions.

subject: English
competency: Explore Newton's interest in the behavior of light and its impact on scientific discoveries
teaching_strategy: Conduct a simple experiment to demonstrate light refraction using prisms. Discuss how Newton's work on light led to improvements in telescopes.

subject: English
competency: Understand the role of Isaac Newton in the development of optics and his theory of gravitation.
teaching_strategy: Use a timeline activity where students place key events in Newton's life and discoveries. Have students create a short play or skit demonstrating Newton's thought process leading to his theory of gravitation.

subject: English
competency: Recognize the consequences of absent-mindedness and its impact on social interactions.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a role-playing activity where students act out scenarios of absent-mindedness, such as forgetting appointments or leaving items behind. Discuss the importance of being mindful and considerate in social interactions.

subject: English
competency: Understanding word meanings and their application in context
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with the words and their meanings. Have students match the words from Column A to Column B and then use the matched words in sentences.

subject: English
competency: Applying vocabulary in context
teaching_strategy: Create a game where students fill in the blanks with the correct words. Use role-playing to act out scenarios where these words can be used, such as a host welcoming guests or discussing interrupted work.

subject: English
competency: Identify and use different types of sentences and parts of speech
teaching_strategy: Use sentence completion exercises to practice identifying and using nouns, verbs, and adjectives. Create a game where students fill in the blanks with appropriate words and then discuss the sentences.

subject: English
competency: Understand and analyze the life and contributions of historical figures
teaching_strategy: Role-play Newton's life events. Have students act out key moments in Newton's life, such as the apple incident, to understand the context and impact of his discoveries.

subject: English
competency: Identify and discuss Newton's other discoveries
teaching_strategy: Ask students to research and present one of Newton's lesser-known discoveries in small groups.

subject: English
competency: Practice tongue twisters to improve pronunciation
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with tongue twisters and have students compete in pairs to see who can say them fastest and most accurately.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and construct complex sentences using relative clauses
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Provide students with additional sentence pairs to combine using relative clauses. Use flashcards with simple sentences on one side and their combined versions on the other side for self-checking.

subject: English
competency: Use relative pronouns correctly in sentences.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Create a phonics game where students match relative pronouns with their correct sentences. Use flashcards with relative pronouns on one side and sentences on the other. Students can play in pairs or small groups to reinforce learning.

subject: English
competency: Join sentences using suitable relative pronouns.
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Divide students into pairs and assign them to create and act out scenarios where they need to join sentences using relative pronouns. For example, one student can be a teacher and the other a student, discussing past events or introducing new colleagues.

subject: English
competency: Write a short biography of Pasang Lhamu Sherpa based on given information.
teaching_strategy: Guide students through the process of writing a biography by providing a structured outline. Use Pasang Lhamu Sherpa's life as a case study. Have students create a timeline of her life events and then write a cohesive biography. Encourage the use of descriptive language and chronological order.

subject: English
competency: Understand the concept of national parks and identify some national parks in Nepal.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of different national parks in Nepal to introduce the concept. Conduct a class discussion on the importance of national parks. Assign a role-playing activity where students can act as park rangers and explain the significance of national parks to visitors. Provide a list of national parks and have students research and present on one of them.

subject: English
competency: Understand the geographical and ecological features of Khaptad National Park, including its location, size, and biodiversity.
teaching_strategy: Use a map to locate Khaptad National Park in Nepal. Create a poster or a digital presentation highlighting the park's features such as its altitude, area, and biodiversity. Organize a role-playing activity where students act as park rangers explaining the importance of the park's unique ecosystem.

subject: English
competency: Recognize the significance of cultural and religious sites within the park, including Khaptad Baba Ashram, Triveni, and Sahashra Linga.
teaching_strategy: Develop a flashcard game where students match the names of the sites with their descriptions. Conduct a guided tour around the classroom, where each site is represented by a different student who provides information about the site's history and significance. Encourage students to create their own mini-projects on one of the sites, presenting their findings to the class.

subject: English
topic: Religious and Cultural Sites in Khaptad National Park
competency: Identify and respect cultural and religious sites in the national park.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students act as park visitors and practice respectful behavior towards religious and cultural sites.

subject: English
competency: Understand and follow park regulations and responsibilities as a visitor.
teaching_strategy: Create a mock permit application process where students fill out forms and discuss the importance of permits and fees.

subject: English
topic: Biodiversity and Wildlife in Khaptad National Park
competency: Identify and categorize different species of animals and plants in the park, understand the concept of biodiversity.
teaching_strategy: Create a wildlife bingo game where students match species names to their descriptions. Use flashcards with images and names of animals and plants. Conduct a role-playing activity where students act as park rangers identifying and explaining the significance of different species.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use context clues to fill in gaps with appropriate words from the text.
teaching_strategy: Use the provided table for a fill-in-the-blank activity. Provide additional sentences for practice where students must use context clues to fill in the blanks. Use a word bank with the words from the text to make the activity more challenging.

subject: English
competency: Describe the features and significance of Khaptad National Park
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of the park's highest point and elevation to reinforce the concept of altitude. Conduct a role-playing activity where students act as park guides explaining the park's features to visitors.

subject: English
competency: Understand the role of local communities in supporting national parks
teaching_strategy: Organize a guided practice session where students create a timeline of events showing how the patans have supported the local community. Use a map to locate the Shiva temple and discuss its significance.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to write a set of rules for a given place using specific grammatical structures such as don't + infinitive and V-ing.
teaching_strategy: Have students select a place (e.g., classroom, playground) and write a set of rules for it. Use flashcards with different rule structures for guided practice.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to use articles correctly in sentences.
teaching_strategy: Create a game where students must complete sentences with the correct article (a, an, the) or a cross if no article is needed. Use real-life examples and role-playing to reinforce usage.

subject: English
competency: Use plural nouns and articles correctly in sentences.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Create a game where students form sentences using plural nouns and the correct articles. For example, provide cards with nouns and articles, and have students match them to form correct sentences.

subject: English
competency: Understand and answer questions based on a given audio and picture.
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Divide the class into groups and assign roles. Have one group act out the story while another group listens and answers questions. This can be followed by a discussion on the importance of community and honesty.

subject: English
competency: Understand the history, duration, and reasons for visiting Sirubari village homestay, and recognize the significance of community-based tourism.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into groups and assign each group a different question from the multiple-choice section. Have them discuss and present their answers to the class. Use flashcards with dates, durations, and reasons for visiting to reinforce learning.

subject: English
competency: Identify the roles of the Tourism Management Committee in managing tourist activities and facilities.
teaching_strategy: Guided practice: Create a scenario where students act as members of the Tourism Management Committee. Assign them tasks such as planning a day for tourists, arranging food and lodging, and managing sightseeing activities. Use a checklist to ensure all aspects are covered.

subject: English
competency: Conduct research and write a descriptive essay using visual aids.
teaching_strategy: Assign students to form groups and choose a famous place in their province. Guide them through the research process, encouraging the use of both written and visual sources. Have students present their findings using a combination of written descriptions and pictures. Provide feedback on their writing and presentation skills.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use common informal expressions in context.
teaching_strategy: Create flashcards with informal expressions on one side and their standard equivalents on the other. Use role-playing activities where students must use these expressions in sentences. Provide examples of when and how to use these expressions in everyday conversations.

subject: English
competency: Develop skills in interpreting visual cues and inferring personal interests through discussion and questioning.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Create a 'Hobby Hunt' game where students match pictures of people with their potential hobbies. Encourage students to justify their choices based on visual details.

subject: English
competency: Enhance reading comprehension and cultural awareness by analyzing a brief biography of a notable Nepalese personality.
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Assign students to role-play as Hari Sharan Nepali and his friends. Have them discuss his hobbies and the nickname 'Kazi Dai', emphasizing his contributions to birding and ornithology.

subject: English
competency: Understand the impact of shared interests and mentorship in shaping career paths
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students act out a scenario of a mentor and mentee sharing a passion, followed by a discussion on how such relationships can influence personal and professional development.

subject: English
competency: Appreciate the value of fieldwork and outdoor learning in environmental education
teaching_strategy: Organize a field trip to a local park or nature reserve where students can observe and identify local flora and fauna, using binoculars and field guides. Encourage students to document their findings and share them in class.

subject: English
competency: Understand the evolution of ornithological science from bird identification and preservation to satellite tracking and digital recording of bird species.
teaching_strategy: Use satellite tracking data and digital recordings of bird species as visual aids. Create a role-playing activity where students simulate the process of satellite tracking and digital recording.

subject: English
competency: Recognize the contributions of Kazi Dai in ornithological research, conservation, and education.
teaching_strategy: Develop a flashcard activity where students match Kazi Dai's contributions (e.g., Biodiversity Profiles Project, Lumbini Crane Sanctuary) with their descriptions. Conduct a guided discussion on the impact of Kazi Dai's work on bird conservation.

subject: English
topic: Understanding and using vocabulary related to social values and personal development
competency: Students will learn to use words such as mentoring, diversity, nurturing, and enhanced in context and understand their implications in social and personal contexts.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with the words and their meanings. Have students create sentences using these words in different scenarios, such as community service, personal growth, and professional development.

subject: English
topic: Appreciating the use of language in describing cultural and personal traits
competency: Students will learn to appreciate the use of words like genteel and lifestyle in describing cultural and personal traits.
teaching_strategy: Role-play different scenarios where students can use the word 'genteel' in sentences, emphasizing its connotation of refined behavior. Discuss the concept of lifestyle and its impact on personal and social values.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and compare organizations
teaching_strategy: Ask students to match the organizations (BCN, WWF, IrUC) with their respective logos or symbols if available, and discuss their roles.

subject: English
competency: Understand the factors that contribute to friendship and recall personal experiences
teaching_strategy: Role-play scenarios where students discuss what makes a good friend and share their own experiences of friendship.

subject: English
topic: Present Simple Negative and Interrogative Forms
competency: Students will be able to form and use present simple negative and interrogative sentences.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Create a phonics game where students form negative and interrogative sentences using the verbs provided in the page. For example, 'I don't like playing basketball.' and 'Do you like playing basketball?'

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to express likes and dislikes and ask about others' preferences.
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Divide students into pairs and have them role-play conversations similar to the ones in the text. Encourage them to use the given clues to discuss their likes and dislikes.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to use correct verb forms in sentences and fill in gaps with appropriate verb tenses.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with verb forms and have students match them with their correct conjugations. Play a game where students fill in the gaps with the correct verb forms and then role-play the sentences.

subject: English
competency: Students will complete sentences using appropriate verbs in active voice and understand the context of the sentences.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Use flashcards with sentences and have students complete them by filling in the blanks. Role-playing: Act out scenarios where students practice using the verbs in active voice.

subject: English
competency: Students will write an essay on their hobbies and interests, including reasons, goals, and support needed.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Provide a structured outline for the essay and have students fill in the details. Peer Review: Have students exchange essays and provide constructive feedback.

subject: English
competency: Identify reasons for preferences and dislikes in context.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing and discussion

subject: English
competency: Create a list or mind map of personal preferences and hobbies, and discuss with peers.
teaching_strategy: Group discussion, personal reflection, and peer sharing

subject: English
competency: Identify and create rhyming words, and practice creative writing.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Create a rhyming word game where students match words that rhyme with given words. For example, provide a list of words like 'odd, true, town' and have students come up with their own rhyming words. Flashcards can be used to reinforce learning.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use vocabulary related to eating and cooking in context.
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Divide the class into pairs and have them act out a scenario where one student is a teacher and the other is a student in a cooking class. Use the words 'approved, tasted, strange' in their dialogue. For example, the student can say, 'I tasted the dish and it was strange, but the teacher approved it.'

subject: English
competency: Rewrite statements in indirect speech using given words as starters
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out scenarios where they convert direct speech to indirect speech using provided starters. For example, one student can say, 'Pravu is in class eight,' and another can respond, 'Who is in class eight?'

subject: English
topic: Grammar: Past Simple and Present Simple
competency: Match statements with their corresponding questions
teaching_strategy: Phonics games: Create flashcards with statements and questions. Students must match the correct question to the statement. For example, 'My father is washing the car' should be matched with 'What is your father doing?'

subject: English
competency: Understand and use question tags in sentences
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with sentences on one side and question tags on the other. Have students match the sentences with the correct question tags.

subject: English
competency: Identify and categorize different genres using -ology terms
teaching_strategy: Create a game where students match the -ology terms with their respective fields of study. For example, use flashcards with terms like 'ornithology' and 'anthropology' and have students match them with 'study of birds' and 'study of humans'.

subject: English
competency: Analyze and discuss the representation of data in charts
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with different types of charts to identify and discuss their names and purposes. Have students create their own charts using data related to their favorite fruits and present them to the class.

subject: English
topic: Evaluating the impact of data changes
competency: Assess the implications of data variations
teaching_strategy: Conduct a role-playing activity where students take turns increasing or decreasing the number of tigers in a hypothetical scenario and discuss the potential impacts on the ecosystem.

subject: English
competency: Understand the significance of periodic wildlife surveys and the impact of conservation efforts on tiger populations.
teaching_strategy: Use a timeline activity where students plot the tiger population data from 2009 to 2022. Discuss the role of conservation efforts and the importance of periodic assessments.

subject: English
competency: Analyze the factors contributing to the decline of tiger populations and the importance of ecosystem health.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a debate on the factors affecting tiger populations, such as habitat loss and poaching. Use flashcards with key terms like 'apex predator', 'habitat loss', and 'poaching' to enhance vocabulary.

subject: English
competency: Understand the efforts and initiatives taken in Nepal to conserve tigers and their habitats.
teaching_strategy: Use a timeline activity where students create a visual timeline of tiger conservation milestones in Nepal, including the establishment of Banke National Park and the extension of Parsa National Park. Discuss the roles of different levels of government and community-based units in tiger conservation.

subject: English
competency: Identify current threats to tiger populations and the need for sustainable management strategies.
teaching_strategy: Role-play scenarios where students act as wildlife conservationists, discussing and planning strategies to manage human-tiger conflicts and protect tiger habitats. Use flashcards with images of tiger prey species to reinforce the importance of habitat management.

subject: English
competency: Understand the importance of corridors in tiger habitat management
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity: Divide students into groups and assign each group a role (e.g., tiger, prey, human). Have them act out scenarios where corridors are used for tiger dispersal, emphasizing the importance of maintaining these pathways.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and use key terms related to conservation and habitat management
teaching_strategy: Flashcard game: Create flashcards with words from Column A on one side and their meanings from Column B on the other. Use these cards for a quick vocabulary review. Then, have students complete the sentences in Part B using the correct terms from the text.

subject: English
competency: Analyze data and information related to tiger surveys, conservation initiatives, and historical events.
teaching_strategy: Use a timeline game where students place key events related to tiger conservation, such as the St. Petersburg declaration, on a timeline. Discuss the importance of each event.

subject: English
competency: Evaluate the effects of conservation activities on ecosystems and biodiversity.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a role-playing activity where students represent different stakeholders (e.g., conservationists, local communities, wildlife) discussing the potential impacts of conservation activities on the ecosystem.

subject: English
competency: Developing listening skills through picture analysis and audio completion
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures for question a and b. For the audio comprehension, play the audio and have students fill in the blanks with the missing information. This can be done in pairs or small groups to encourage discussion.

subject: English
competency: Understanding and using quantifiers in context
teaching_strategy: Create a game where students have to match quantifiers with appropriate sentences. For example, 'most', 'some', 'many', 'few'. Provide real-life examples and have students create their own sentences using these quantifiers.

subject: English
topic: Quantifiers with Countable and Uncountable Nouns
competency: Identify and use appropriate quantifiers for different types of nouns in sentences.
teaching_strategy: Provide flashcards with countable and uncountable nouns. Have students match quantifiers to the correct nouns. Use role-playing to create sentences with the given quantifiers.

subject: English
competency: Apply quantifiers in various sentence structures to convey appropriate meaning.
teaching_strategy: Use real-life scenarios to create sentences with different quantifiers. For example, discuss meal preparation, shopping, or weight management. Encourage students to create their own sentences using the quantifiers provided.

subject: English
competency: Describe the object in the picture and explain its purpose.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Have students describe objects using phonics rules. For example, 'mousetrap' can be broken down into sounds: m-ouse-s-trap.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and describe the reactions of different characters to the mousetrap.
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Assign students to act out the dialogue between the mouse and the chicken. Encourage them to express the emotions of the characters through their voices and body language.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to understand and act out a story involving characters like Mr. Lamb, Mrs. Buffalo, and the Chicken. They will practice dialogue and emotional expressions through role-playing activities.
teaching_strategy: Divide students into groups and assign each group a character. Have them act out the story, focusing on the emotions and dialogue of each character. Use props like a toy mousetrap, a small stuffed animal as the snake, and a chicken cutout to enhance the role-playing experience.

subject: English
competency: Students will learn about the dangers of snake bites and the importance of seeking medical attention. They will also understand the concept of first aid and the role of a doctor in treating injuries.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a discussion on the dangers of snake bites and the importance of immediate medical attention. Use the story to illustrate the sequence of events and the role of the doctor. Create a simple first aid kit and demonstrate how to use it in a controlled, safe environment.

subject: English
competency: Understand the moral of the story and apply it in real-life situations
teaching_strategy: Role-playing the characters in the story to discuss the importance of helping others in need.

subject: English
competency: Arrange sentences in a logical order to form a coherent narrative
teaching_strategy: Cut out the sentences and have students arrange them in the correct order to retell the story.

subject: English
competency: Identify and use correct forms of present simple and present continuous verbs in context
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Create a phonics game where students match verbs in present simple and present continuous forms with their correct usage in sentences. For example, 'give' vs. 'are giving'.

subject: English
competency: Differentiate and use past simple and present perfect verb tenses
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Have students act out scenarios where they use past simple and present perfect tenses. For example, 'get up' vs. 'have got up'.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to identify and use correct verb tenses in sentences and complete them appropriately.
teaching_strategy: Provide flashcards with verb phrases in different tenses. Have students match the phrases with the correct sentences. Use role-playing to practice different scenarios where these sentences might be used.

subject: English
topic: Present Continuous and Present Simple Tenses
competency: Students will understand the difference between present continuous and present simple tenses and use them correctly in context.
teaching_strategy: Create a game where students have to identify whether a sentence is in present continuous or present simple tense. Use real-life examples and ask students to form sentences using both tenses.

subject: English
competency: Analyze and describe processes through writing
teaching_strategy: Have students create their own flowcharts for a simple process (e.g., making lemonade) and then write a short description of the process. Use the orange juice flowchart as a model.

subject: English
competency: Extract and use information from tables to answer questions
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with state names and key information (year, area, population) for a memory game. Then, have students take turns asking and answering questions based on the table.

subject: English
competency: Conduct a survey, organize data, and present findings using a bar graph
teaching_strategy: Organize students into groups to visit different classes, count the number of boys and girls, and record the data. Guide them to create a bar graph using the collected data and present it to the class.

subject: English
competency: Use appropriate vocabulary to describe changes in data
teaching_strategy: Introduce and practice using vocabulary related to increases and decreases in data. Have students use these terms to describe the trends they observe in their bar graphs.

subject: English
competency: Analyze and infer actions and settings from visual cues
teaching_strategy: Use role-playing activities where students act out different scenarios based on the pictures. Provide flashcards with various actions and locations for students to match and discuss.

subject: English
competency: Identify and analyze deceptive practices in social situations
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students act out scenarios involving the barber and potential brides. Discuss the implications of setting unfair conditions and the importance of transparency.

subject: English
competency: Understand and evaluate the impact of social influence and peer pressure
teaching_strategy: Group discussion on the reasons why the young ladies did not want to look into the mirror. Use flashcards with different social scenarios to practice identifying and resisting peer pressure.

subject: English
competency: Analyze the character's motivations and actions in a story
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students role-play the king and the shepherd girl. Discuss their motivations and the consequences of their actions.

subject: English
competency: Evaluate the implications of the shepherd girl's decision to look into the magic mirror
teaching_strategy: Guided discussion: Lead a discussion on the risks and benefits the shepherd girl faced. Ask students to reflect on their own values and bravery.

subject: English
competency: Analyze the context and meaning of idiomatic expressions in a narrative.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into groups and assign each group a different sentence from the text. Have them act out the scene, focusing on the idiomatic expressions and their meanings.

subject: English
competency: Identify and define key vocabulary terms in context.
teaching_strategy: Flashcards: Create flashcards with the given words and their meanings. Use the flashcards for quick vocabulary quizzes and pair activities where students match the words with their definitions.

subject: English
topic: Identifying True, False, and Not Given Statements
competency: Students will be able to read passages and determine the accuracy of given statements based on the text.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with the statements on one side and the correct answer (True, False, or NG) on the other. Have students match the statements with the correct answers and discuss their reasoning.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to comprehend the passage and answer questions based on the text.
teaching_strategy: Role-play the scenario in the passage with students. Assign roles such as the king, the shepherd girl, and the watchman. Have students act out the scene and then answer the questions based on their performance.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and pronounce words differently in British and American English
teaching_strategy: Have students practice pronouncing the given words in both British and American English. Use flashcards and a pronunciation guide provided by the teacher.

subject: English
competency: Understand and form conditional sentences
teaching_strategy: Use role-playing activities where students create scenarios and form conditional sentences. For example, they can role-play a situation where they win a lottery and discuss the consequences.

subject: English
competency: Form and use conditional sentences in context
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with conditional sentence structures to practice forming sentences. Have students role-play scenarios to apply the sentences in real-life situations.

subject: English
competency: Understand and interpret spoken sentences
teaching_strategy: Show pictures of people speaking and have students write down what they think the people are saying. Discuss the meanings of the sentences as a class.

subject: English
competency: Develop critical thinking by understanding the consequences of actions through group activities and storytelling.
teaching_strategy: Use the provided examples and clues to engage students in creating chains of events. Encourage students to think about the logical outcomes of their actions. For instance, use the example 'drink coffee/stay awake tonight/feel sleepy in class tomorrow' to guide them in forming their own chains. This activity can be turned into a game where students take turns adding to the chain, fostering teamwork and language skills.

subject: English
competency: Apply logical reasoning to real-life situations by analyzing cause and effect relationships.
teaching_strategy: Present real-life scenarios such as 'rain heavily/stay inside/mother happy/provide delicious food' and ask students to predict the outcomes. This can be done through role-playing where students act out the scenarios. Alternatively, use flashcards with different scenarios and have students match them with their logical outcomes. This helps in developing their analytical and predictive skills.

subject: English
competency: Practice forming and using conditional sentences in context.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing scenarios where students act out the given situations, using the conditional structure to respond. For example, students can role-play finding a purse and deciding what to do, or dealing with bad weather and making decisions about going out.

subject: English
topic: Verb Tenses and Contextual Story Completion
competency: Complete stories using appropriate verb tenses and forms.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with verbs in different tenses. Have students complete the story by filling in the blanks with the correct verb forms. Encourage students to discuss the context and implications of each verb choice.

subject: English
competency: Identify benefits and challenges of cycling as a mode of transportation
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into groups and have them role-play scenarios where they discuss the benefits of cycling, such as health and cost savings. Use props like small signs indicating 'parking is expensive' and 'public transport not available'.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use numbers in context
teaching_strategy: Number Line Activity: Create a number line on the floor or a large piece of paper. Place markers for each person and have students count and place them correctly. Discuss the concept of sharing spaces.

subject: English
competency: Describe and compare characters and actions in a text, and discuss the impact of a superhero's role in society.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity: Divide students into groups and assign each group a different superhero from the text. Have them act out scenes from the poem, focusing on the unique powers and actions of their assigned superhero. Encourage discussion on how each superhero contributes to making the world a better place.

subject: English
competency: Identify and analyze poetic devices and themes in a text, and discuss their significance.
teaching_strategy: Phonics game: Create flashcards with key words from the poem (e.g.,

subject: English
competency: Students will identify and fill in key phrases from a poem, fostering comprehension and critical thinking skills through creative writing.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with phrases from the poem for a memory game. Have students role-play the speaker of the poem, discussing their intentions and the impact of their actions.

subject: English
competency: Students will read and analyze a news story, enhancing their reading comprehension and critical thinking skills.
teaching_strategy: Provide students with the news story and guide them through a discussion on the significance of Nepal exporting cement to India. Use guided questions to encourage deeper analysis and debate.

subject: English
competency: Identifying and summarizing key elements of a news story
teaching_strategy: Ask students to identify and write down the headline, by-line, date, and lead paragraph from the given text. Discuss the importance of each element in a news story.

subject: English
competency: Crafting a news article based on given information
teaching_strategy: Provide students with the guidelines and information about Mohammad Irfan. Have them write a short news story about his achievement, focusing on the key points provided. Encourage the use of active voice and clear, concise language.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to form and use different types of conditional sentences in English.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with conditional sentence structures to help students identify the correct form. Have students role-play scenarios where they can practice forming and using conditional sentences in context.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to express hypothetical situations and outcomes.
teaching_strategy: Create a game where students suggest hypothetical situations and their outcomes. For example, 'If I were a superhero, I would save the world.' Encourage students to use their creativity and form different types of conditional sentences.

subject: English
competency: Students will draft and present a speech on hypothetical leadership roles, focusing on critical thinking and public speaking skills.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing and peer feedback sessions can be used to enhance students' public speaking abilities. Encourage students to practice their speeches in front of a mirror or with a small group before presenting to the class.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand and identify the key components of a news story, including headline, byline, dateline, and lead paragraph.
teaching_strategy: Create a news story about a local event and have students work in groups to identify and label the different parts of the story. Use flashcards with examples of headlines, bylines, datelines, and leads to reinforce learning.

subject: English
competency: Students will observe pictures and discuss the importance of objects, animals, and places.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of various objects, animals, and places. Divide the class into small groups and have them discuss why each item is important. Encourage students to share their thoughts and reasons.

subject: English
competency: Students will read a text and answer questions related to the content.
teaching_strategy: Display the picture from the text and ask students to identify plants and animals. Then, guide them through answering the questions. Use a question board or cards to make the activity interactive. For example, place the question cards around the classroom and have students move to the card they want to answer.

subject: English
competency: Understand the concept of natural habitat and its significance for living creatures.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity: Divide students into groups representing different animals (e.g., polar bears, lions, elephants). Each group should discuss and present their natural habitat, including the climate, vegetation, and why it is suitable for them.

subject: English
competency: Recognize the importance of conservation efforts and the initial steps taken by conservationists.
teaching_strategy: Guided practice: Provide students with a list of endangered species and ask them to research and present the reasons for their endangerment and the conservation measures that can be taken to protect them.

subject: English
competency: Understand the importance of protecting natural habitats and biodiversity for human survival.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity: Divide students into groups representing different species and habitats. Have them discuss the impact of human activities on their survival and the importance of conservation.

subject: English
competency: Explore the concept of finding alternative habitats for species due to environmental degradation.
teaching_strategy: Guided discussion: Use the James Webb Space Telescope as a case study. Discuss the importance of current conservation efforts and the potential for future solutions.

subject: English
competency: Identify and define key terms from context
teaching_strategy: Word Association Game: Provide flashcards with the words and their meanings. Have students match the words with their definitions.

subject: English
competency: Evaluate statements and answer questions based on text
teaching_strategy: Debate Activity: Divide the class into two groups. One group should argue for the statements, and the other against. This will encourage critical thinking and discussion.

subject: English
topic: Exploring New Species and Their Impact
competency: Discuss the discovery of new species and their significance, and understand the role of other creatures in human life.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into groups and assign each group a new species. Have them present their species and discuss its habitat, contribution to humans, and why it is important to protect it.

subject: English
competency: Identify essential items for survival on a new planet and justify the choices.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Provide students with a list of items and ask them to select five items they would take to a new planet. Have them discuss their choices with classmates and present their reasoning.

subject: English
competency: Develop conversational skills through role-playing
teaching_strategy: Pair students to ask questions and provide explanations based on the given sentence structure. Use pictures to enhance understanding and engagement.

subject: English
competency: Understand basic banking activities
teaching_strategy: Discuss the context of withdrawing money and its relevance in daily life. Use real-life examples or role-playing to reinforce the concept.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand and use conditional sentences and comprehend the concept of survival in the context of environmental issues.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with conditional sentences to practice filling in the blanks. Conduct a role-play activity where students discuss the survival of different species and the impact of global warming.

subject: English
competency: Students will identify and use conjunctions to express cause-effect relationships and understand their importance in conveying meaning.
teaching_strategy: Create a game where students match conjunctions with their appropriate sentences. Use guided practice to discuss real-life scenarios where conjunctions are used to express cause and effect.

subject: English
competency: Develop and express personal opinions on social issues through essay writing
teaching_strategy: Phonics games can be used to improve vocabulary and sentence structure. Role-playing can be employed to practice articulating opinions.

subject: English
competency: Analyze and interpret visual information and answer questions based on it
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images to enhance visual recognition and comprehension. Guided practice with similar questions can improve analytical skills.

subject: English
competency: Students will match words with their meanings and understand key terms related to public health and education.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with the words and their meanings. Have students match the words in Column A with Column B. Conduct a quick quiz to reinforce learning.

subject: English
topic: Comprehending and Responding to a Notice
competency: Students will comprehend a notice, answer related questions, and draft a message in their own words.
teaching_strategy: Provide a sample notice about school closure due to an infection outbreak. Guide students to answer the questions. Then, have them draft a similar notice for a one-day closure, focusing on clear and concise communication.

subject: English
competency: Combine sentences using appropriate connectives such as although, in spite of, so that, however, because, because of, and, but.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Create a connective bingo game where students match connectives with their meanings. Role-playing: Have students act out scenarios using the given connectives in sentences.

subject: English
competency: Answer questions based on visual information and express personal preferences.
teaching_strategy: Flashcards: Use flashcards with pictures and questions. Guided Practice: Provide students with pictures and ask them to formulate questions and answers.

subject: English
competency: Evaluate the ethical considerations of keeping animals in zoos through listening and discussion
teaching_strategy: Phonics games to improve listening comprehension and vocabulary related to animal welfare, followed by a class discussion on the ethical implications of zoos.

subject: English
competency: Understand the importance of conservation and the role of zoos in protecting endangered species
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activities where students act as zookeepers and endangered animals, emphasizing the need for conservation and the role of zoos in this process.

subject: English
competency: Identify and use various connectives and transition words to enhance writing coherence and clarity.
teaching_strategy: Create a connective chain game where students form sentences using different connectives and transition words. Provide examples and have students practice by writing short paragraphs using these words.

subject: English
competency: Practice storytelling and turn-taking to enhance communication skills.
teaching_strategy: Have students form pairs and take turns telling stories using the pictures as prompts. Encourage them to ask each other follow-up questions to engage in a dialogue.

subject: English
competency: Develop understanding of personal preferences and reasons behind food choices.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a class discussion on food preferences. Use the provided questions as a guide. Create a survey where students can vote on their favorite foods and discuss the results in class.

subject: English
competency: Understand the personal and health-related reasons for adopting a vegan lifestyle.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students can discuss and share their own reasons for making lifestyle changes, followed by a group discussion on the benefits of a vegan diet.

subject: English
topic: Differences between a strict vegan and a flexible vegan
competency: Recognize the spectrum of veganism and the flexibility in dietary choices.
teaching_strategy: Flashcard activity where students match terms like 'strict vegan', 'flexible vegan', and 'plant-based diet' with their definitions. Follow up with a guided practice session where students create their own dietary choices based on given scenarios.

subject: English
competency: Identify the correct contextual meaning of given words in a sentence.
teaching_strategy: Provide flashcards with the words and their meanings. Have students match the words with their correct definitions. Use a game where students have to choose the correct meaning of a word in a sentence.

subject: English
competency: Recognize the impact of dietary choices on health.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a role-playing activity where students discuss and role-play scenarios of choosing healthy food options. Use a guided practice where students create a meal plan that includes alternatives to dairy products.

subject: English
topic: Fill in the gaps using appropriate verbs
competency: Understand and use appropriate verbs in context
teaching_strategy: Phonics games: Create a phonics game where students match verbs with their correct forms in sentences. Use the sentences from the page as examples.

subject: English
topic: Decide the correct tense and form of the sentence
competency: Identify and use correct tense and form of sentences
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into groups and assign them different sentences. Each group must act out the sentence using the correct tense and form, and the class will decide if it is correct or not.

subject: English
topic: Answer questions related to the text
competency: Extract and answer information from the text
teaching_strategy: Guided practice: Provide students with a set of questions similar to the ones given in the page. Guide them through the process of finding the answers in the text.

subject: English
competency: Discuss personal experiences related to food choices
teaching_strategy: Group discussion

subject: English
competency: Identify and pronounce words with silent letters
teaching_strategy: Phonics games where students identify and pronounce words with silent letters

subject: English
competency: Form and use past simple tense in sentences
teaching_strategy: Role-playing and guided practice

subject: English
competency: Form and use past continuous tense in sentences
teaching_strategy: Phonics games and flashcards

subject: English
competency: Use past simple tense in context
teaching_strategy: Role-playing and guided practice

subject: English
competency: Understand and respond to audio content
teaching_strategy: Audio playback and discussion

subject: English
competency: Arrange sentences to form a coherent narrative
teaching_strategy: Phonics games: Create a phonetic sequence game where students arrange phonetic sounds to form words, then sentences, and finally a story. This helps in understanding the logical flow of a narrative.

subject: English
competency: Understand the consequences of developing or changing habits
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into groups and assign roles (wise man, businessman, son, gardener). Act out the story to emphasize the difficulty of changing habits as one grows older.

subject: English
topic: Types of Pens and Their Evolution
competency: Identify and describe the historical development of writing instruments, including reed pens and quill pens, and their uses in writing.
teaching_strategy: Create a timeline activity where students place different types of pens (reed pen, quill pen) in chronological order. Use flashcards with images of each pen type and have students match them to the correct period in history.

subject: English
competency: Understand the role of writing fluid in early pens and how it was applied.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a hands-on activity where students use a small tube (like a plastic straw) and a liquid (like food coloring in water) to simulate the flow of ink. Discuss the importance of squeezing the tube to release the liquid.

subject: English
topic: Invention and Evolution of Writing Instruments
competency: Understand the historical development of writing tools from quills to fountain pens and ballpoint pens, emphasizing key inventors and their contributions.
teaching_strategy: Create a timeline activity where students place major inventions and their inventors in chronological order. Use flashcards with images of different writing instruments to reinforce learning.

subject: English
competency: Identify and discuss the improvements in pen design, such as the introduction of fountain pens and ballpoint pens, focusing on their practical benefits.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a guided practice session where students compare and contrast the use of different writing instruments. Have students role-play as inventors explaining their design choices and the problems they aimed to solve.

subject: English
topic: Types of Pens and Their Inventors
competency: Identify and describe the historical development of ballpoint pens.
teaching_strategy: Ask students to identify the types of pens mentioned in the text and their inventors. Provide flashcards with the names of the pens and their inventors. Have students match the correct pen with the inventor. Conduct a class discussion on the significance of the ballpoint pen in the evolution of writing instruments.

subject: English
topic: Impact of Technology on Writing Instruments
competency: Understand the shift from traditional writing instruments to modern technology.
teaching_strategy: Discuss the decline in the use of pens due to the advent of technology. Use a guided practice session where students compare the features of ballpoint pens with modern writing devices like smartphones and tablets. Encourage students to share their personal experiences with using different writing tools.

subject: English
competency: Understand the evolution of writing tools and their impact on writing practices.
teaching_strategy: Create a timeline activity where students can fill in key dates and events related to the development of writing instruments. Use flashcards with images of different writing tools to enhance visual learning. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of each tool to understand the progression in technology and materials.

subject: English
competency: Describe a historical event in writing.
teaching_strategy: Assign students to write a couple of paragraphs about a historical event they are interested in. Encourage them to use the timeline they created as a reference. Conduct a peer review session where students can share and provide feedback on each other's writing.

subject: English
competency: Collaborate in group settings and document school events
teaching_strategy: Divide students into small groups and provide them with a list of events that occurred in the school last month. Have them work together to create a short paragraph summarizing these events.

subject: English
competency: Understand and identify blended words
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards to introduce and practice blended words. Engage students in a game where they create their own blended words using parts of existing words, encouraging them to think about the properties of the original words.

subject: English
topic: Identifying characters and inferring social status
competency: Develop critical thinking and inference skills through visual analysis
teaching_strategy: Use role-playing where students act out different social statuses and discuss the indicators of wealth or poverty in their roles.

subject: English
competency: Enhance observational and descriptive skills
teaching_strategy: Create flashcards with different pictures of people in various settings and have students describe what they see and infer about the characters' lives.

subject: English
competency: Analyze the character traits of Naresh and the stranger, and discuss their motivations and actions.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into pairs. One student will play Naresh, and the other will play the stranger. Have them act out the scene where Naresh offers help to the stranger. Discuss their motivations and the impact of their actions.

subject: English
competency: Identify the economic challenges faced by Naresh and his family and discuss the importance of income for a family's well-being.
teaching_strategy: Guided discussion: Present a scenario where students have to manage a family budget. Discuss the importance of income and how it affects the family's ability to meet basic needs. Use flashcards with different income sources and expenses to help students understand budgeting.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand the importance of helping others and the positive outcomes of generosity.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide the class into groups and assign roles (Naresh, his wife, the stranger). Have students act out the story to emphasize the moral values of kindness and helping those in need.

subject: English
competency: Students will learn to solve problems creatively and discover hidden resources.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Present students with a scenario where they need to find a hidden resource. Use flashcards with different objects and ask them to think of creative ways to uncover or find them. Discuss the importance of persistence and resourcefulness.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use context clues to fill in the blanks and complete sentences.
teaching_strategy: Use a fill-in-the-blank activity where students complete the sentences based on the story. Provide flashcards with the words 'friendship', 'kindness', 'independent', and 'stranger' to reinforce vocabulary.

subject: English
competency: Analyze the characters' actions and emotions in the story and discuss their motivations.
teaching_strategy: Role-play the conversation between Naresh and the stranger. Have students act out the scene where Naresh thanks the stranger and expresses his gratitude. Discuss the emotions and motivations behind their actions.

subject: English
competency: Analyze the story and retell it in one's own words, considering the lesson learned.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing and storytelling

subject: English
competency: Practice pronouncing contractions and other phrases.
teaching_strategy: Phonics games and listening exercises

subject: English
topic: Making offers and responding in social situations
competency: Practice making offers and responding in various scenarios
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into pairs and have them act out the given situations. For example, one student can be the friend at home, and the other can offer a cup of tea. Switch roles after each scenario.

subject: English
competency: Identify and match active sentences with their passive counterparts
teaching_strategy: Flashcards: Create flashcards with active sentences on one side and passive sentences on the other. Students can match the sentences in pairs or small groups.

subject: English
competency: Identify and convert active sentences to passive form
teaching_strategy: Provide students with flashcards containing active sentences. Have them convert these sentences to passive form in small groups. Use role-playing to act out scenarios where one student performs the action and another describes it in passive voice.

subject: English
topic: Passive Voice in Present and Past Continuous
competency: Recognize and use passive voice in continuous tenses
teaching_strategy: Use guided practice where students listen to sentences and identify if they are in active or passive voice. Then, provide them with sentences in active voice and ask them to convert them to passive voice, focusing on continuous tenses.

subject: English
competency: Write a reply to an email offer, considering acceptance or rejection
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Students can role-play as Mr. Dangol and Sukla Devkota. One student reads the email, and the other responds with a reply, either accepting or denying the offer.

subject: English
competency: Describe actions and personal experiences
teaching_strategy: Flashcards: Create flashcards with pictures of people doing various activities. Students describe what the person is doing. For the second question, students can share their experiences of visiting friends' houses, encouraging them to use descriptive language.

subject: English
competency: Develop listening skills and answer questions based on audio content
teaching_strategy: Play the audio and have students work in pairs to answer the questions. Use role-playing to act out the dialogue for better understanding.

subject: English
competency: Engage in creative writing and collaborative activities
teaching_strategy: Pair students and have them write about activities they did together. Encourage sharing and discussion of their experiences.

subject: English
competency: Define and use new vocabulary and understand the imagery in a poem.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with the words hedge, ditch, troop, and wink. Have students create their own sentences using these words. For the summary, provide a set of cards with the phrases and have students match them to the correct blanks in the summary. This activity will help them understand the context and meaning of the poem.

subject: English
competency: Identify and describe the imagery used by the poet to convey the speed and movement of the train.
teaching_strategy: Create a role-playing activity where students act out the scenes described in the poem. Divide the class into groups, each representing a different scene (e.g., passing through a village, seeing a cart, etc.). Use props like toy trains, miniature models of bridges and houses, and flashcards with the phrases from the summary. This will help students visualize the poem and understand the poet's imagery.

subject: English
competency: Analyze and describe the relative movement and observed actions in a given context.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of trains and meadows to help students understand comparative adjectives. Role-play scenarios where students describe the movement of objects or people in different settings.

subject: English
competency: Compose a formal letter in response to an invitation.
teaching_strategy: Provide students with a sample letter and have them fill in the blanks with appropriate responses. Conduct a peer review session where students exchange and critique each other's letters.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use passive voice in different tenses (present simple, present continuous, past simple, past continuous, past perfect, and future simple and perfect).
teaching_strategy: Create a 'Passive Voice Relay Race' where students form groups and take turns to construct sentences in passive voice using given active sentences. Provide flashcards with active sentences and have students race to write the passive form.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and use modal verbs in passive voice constructions.
teaching_strategy: Develop a 'Modal Verb Role-Play' activity where students act out scenarios using sentences with modal verbs in passive voice. For example, 'The project can be completed by the end of the week.'

subject: English
competency: Students will observe pictures, generate hypotheses, and share opinions in groups.
teaching_strategy: Use a set of diverse images related to road safety. Divide students into small groups and have them discuss and predict events based on the images. Encourage them to share their thoughts and discuss necessary precautions for road safety.

subject: English
competency: Students will identify and discuss safety measures while driving.
teaching_strategy: Prepare flashcards with different road safety signs and scenarios. Conduct a role-playing activity where students act out driving situations and use the flashcards to identify and discuss appropriate safety measures.

subject: English
competency: Identify key factors such as driver's negligence, lack of discipline and maturity, and the role of motorbikes in Nepal.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing scenarios where students act out safe and unsafe driving behaviors. Discuss the consequences of each scenario.

subject: English
competency: Understand the potential impact of increasing the minimum age for obtaining a driving license.
teaching_strategy: Create a debate where students argue for or against increasing the minimum driving age. Use real-life examples and statistics to support their arguments.

subject: English
competency: Understand the importance of responsible driving and the consequences of drinking and driving.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing scenarios where students act as drivers and passengers to discuss the dangers of drinking and driving. Use flashcards with safety rules and consequences to reinforce learning.

subject: English
competency: Analyze the impact of poor road conditions on road safety and the need for better infrastructure.
teaching_strategy: Guided practice where students create a mock road map with different scenarios (e.g., narrow lanes, potholes, landslides) and discuss potential solutions. Use a map of Nepal to highlight areas with poor road conditions.

subject: English
competency: Understand the role of perspective in judging others and its impact on understanding societal issues.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students act out scenarios from different perspectives to explore how perspective influences judgment and empathy.

subject: English
competency: Identify key factors contributing to road safety and infrastructure issues.
teaching_strategy: Group discussion and brainstorming session to identify local road safety issues and propose solutions, followed by a presentation to the class.

subject: English
competency: Act out conversations in pairs to discuss the impact of working late and the role of social media in modern society.
teaching_strategy: Divide students into pairs and assign them different roles to act out the conversations. Encourage students to use the given dialogues as a guide but allow them to improvise and add their own ideas.

subject: English

subject: Social Studies

competency: संयुक्त राष्ट्र र अशियाई संयुक्त राष्ट्रको अवस्थाको विश्लेषण गर्ने तथ्य र जानकारी पठन र सम्बन्धित प्रश्नहरू समावेश गर्ने क्षमता विकसित गर्नुहोस्।
teaching_strategy: संयुक्त राष्ट्र र अशियाई संयुक्त राष्ट्रको अवस्थाको विश्लेषण गर्ने अभ्यास दिइएको छन्। छात्रहरूले यस विषयको जानकारी अनुसार अपनै कार्यक्रम बनाउन सक्छन्।

subject: Social Studies
competency: क्रमांक र संख्याहरूको रिकार्ड लेने

subject: Social Studies
competency: सय र रिकार्ड लेने
teaching_strategy: सय रिकार्ड लेने लागि छात्रहरूले सय र संख्याहरूको गणना र रिकार्ड लेने अभ्यास गर्नुपर्छ। यसमा नेपाली रुपय नोटहरू वा गेमहरू उपयोग गर्नुपर्छ।

subject: Social Studies
competency: संख्याहरूको फरक र अनुपात निर्धारण गर्ने क्षमता पनि विकसित गर्नुहोस्। यसमा दोहो संख्याहरूको फरक र अनुपात निर्धारण गर्ने व्यवस्था गर्नुपर्छ।
teaching_strategy: 1. दोहो संख्याहरूको फरक र अनुपात निर्धारण गर्ने व्यवस्था गर्नुहोस्। उदाहरणका लागि, 199 र 207 दिइयो र फरक र अनुपात निर्धारण गर्नुपर्छ। 2. नेपाल पाउरको नोटहरू दिइयो र छात्रहरूले फरक र अनुपात निर्धारण गर्नुपर्छ।

subject: Social Studies
competency: संख्याहरूको अनुपात र अनुपातीको अनुपात गणना गर्ने र उनको अनुपातीको अनुपात निर्धारण गर्ने पाठ्यक्रम अभ्यास गर्ने।
teaching_strategy: क्षेत्रमा निर्धारित अनुपात र अनुपातीको अनुपात गणना गर्ने अभ्यास गर्नुहोस्। उदाहरणका लागि, निर्धारण गर्ने अभ्यास गर्नुहोस् कि यदि एक बालक र एक बालीका बीच अनुपात 2:3 छ भने, त्यसको अनुपातीको अनुपात कस्तो हुन्छ।

subject: Social Studies
competency: संख्याहरूको अनुपात ज्ञान र अनुपात गर्ने तथ्य
teaching_strategy: 6 संख्याहरू देखि उनको अनुपात ज्ञान र अनुपात गर्ने अभ्यास गर्नुहोस्। उदाहरण र अभ्यास दिनुहोस्।

subject: English

subject: English

subject: English

subject: English

subject: English

subject: English
competency: Students will practice and perform introduction and greeting dialogues using real names and contextual information.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing and group practice

subject: English
competency: Students will learn and use expressions for introducing others, including their origin and occupation.
teaching_strategy: Flashcards and guided practice

subject: English
