teaching_strategy: Use the provided excerpt from William Wordsworth's poem. Have students identify and discuss the imagery and the poet's emotional response to the scene. Encourage them to write their own short poems inspired by the scene.

subject: English
topic: Understanding and using synonyms and context clues
competency: Students will be able to define and use synonyms effectively in context, and identify the correct word to complete sentences.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with synonyms and antonyms to create a matching game. Provide sentences with blanks and have students fill in the correct word using context clues.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to analyze a poem, identify key imagery and descriptive language, and understand the speaker's perspective.
teaching_strategy: Role-play the speaker of the poem, discussing the emotions and observations. Use guided practice to identify and discuss key phrases and their meanings.

subject: English
competency: Analyze the use of imagery and its impact on the poem's theme. Understand the speaker's perspective and the impression created about a place.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a group discussion where students analyze the poet's use of imagery (valley, rock, hill) and discuss how these elements contribute to the overall mood and theme of the poem. Have students write a short paragraph on the impression of London created by the speaker and the techniques used.

subject: English
competency: Identify geographical features and their significance. Understand and use geographical terms and concepts in context.
teaching_strategy: Use a globe or map to identify the regions mentioned in the audio. Create a flashcard activity where students match geographical features with their descriptions. Play the audio and have students take notes on the information provided, then quiz them on the details of the Pan-American Highway.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to use future simple, be going to, future continuous, and future perfect or future perfect continuous tenses in context.
teaching_strategy: Create a future timeline activity where students predict future events in their lives using different future tenses. Provide flashcards with verbs in brackets and have students form sentences using the correct future tense. Use role-playing to act out scenarios where these tenses are used.

subject: English
competency: Students will learn to write notices and understand the structure of a notice. They will also practice using time expressions in context.
teaching_strategy: Provide students with the example notice and have them identify the key components such as the date, purpose, and call to action. Then, have them write their own notice for the Child Club's upcoming programme, focusing on clear and concise language.

subject: English
competency: Students will research and identify projects of national pride and their benefits, fostering critical thinking and research skills.
teaching_strategy: Assign students to form groups and use the internet to research various national pride projects. Have them present their findings and discuss the benefits of these projects, encouraging them to reflect on how they can contribute positively to their community.

subject: English
topic: Spelling Differences Between American and British English
competency: Identify and understand common spelling differences in English words
teaching_strategy: Create flashcards with American and British spellings. Have students match the words and discuss the differences. Use role-playing to act out scenarios where characters use the correct spelling in their dialogue.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and apply correct word endings in American and British English
teaching_strategy: Play a phonics game where students listen to words and identify the correct ending. Use guided practice with sentences where students rewrite words with the correct endings.

subject: English
competency: Analyze factors influencing population change and present ideas on population data
teaching_strategy: Use picture analysis and discussion to engage students in understanding population dynamics. Provide real-world data (e.g., population census data) for students to present their ideas.

subject: English
topic: World population trends over the 20th and 21st centuries
competency: Analyze the historical and projected growth of the global population, including key milestones and factors affecting growth rates.
teaching_strategy: Use a timeline or a graph to plot the population growth from 1950 to 2050. Have students identify the periods of fastest growth and discuss the reasons behind these trends. Use role-playing to simulate the impact of different fertility rates on population growth.

subject: English
competency: Evaluate the factors contributing to the uncertainty in global population projections and understand the role of demographic processes in determining future population size.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a debate on the factors affecting population growth and the reliability of projections. Use flashcards with key terms like 'fertility', 'mortality', and 'demographic processes' to enhance vocabulary and comprehension.

subject: English
topic: Population Distribution and Growth in Different Regions
competency: Analyze population distribution and growth trends in various regions of the world, including Central and Southern Asia, Europe and Northern America, and Sub-Saharan Africa.
teaching_strategy: Use a world map to mark the regions mentioned and have students calculate the population growth rate for each region using provided data. Create a timeline to show the growth trajectory of Sub-Saharan Africa and Europe/Northern America since the mid-20th century.

subject: English
competency: Understand global population projections for 2030 and 2050 and compare them with the current population.
teaching_strategy: Create a bar graph comparing the projected population of different regions in 2022, 2030, and 2050. Discuss the implications of these projections on resource allocation and sustainable development goals.

subject: English
competency: Analyze regional population growth rates and their implications
teaching_strategy: Use a world map to mark the regions mentioned (Central and Southern Asia, sub-Saharan Africa, Europe, Northern America) and have students discuss the projected population changes. Create a timeline activity where students plot the projected growth rates of different regions.

subject: English
topic: Impact of population growth on global ranking
competency: Evaluate the impact of population growth on global rankings
teaching_strategy: Role-play a scenario where students are global leaders making decisions based on population projections. Use flashcards with country names and their current population rankings to reinforce learning.

subject: English
competency: Define and use key demographic terms
teaching_strategy: Flashcards and matching game: Create flashcards with words on one side and their meanings on the other. Use the matching game to reinforce learning.

subject: English
competency: Understand and interpret population projections
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into groups and have them role-play scenarios where they predict future population trends based on given data.

subject: English
competency: Analyze population growth and decline in various regions of the world.
teaching_strategy: Use a world map to mark the regions mentioned (Eastern and South-Eastern Asia, sub-Saharan region, Europe and Northern America, and India). Have students fill in the blanks with the correct population figures or time periods based on the information provided. This can be done through a group activity where each group focuses on a different region and presents their findings to the class.

subject: English
competency: Identify factors that influence population growth and decline.
teaching_strategy: Create a cause-and-effect chart where students list factors affecting population growth (fertility, mortality) and their effects. Use flashcards with key terms like 'fertility rate', 'mortality rate', and 'population growth rate' for vocabulary reinforcement. Conduct a role-play activity where students act as demographers discussing the impact of these factors on different regions.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and pronounce words with silent /r/ sound
teaching_strategy: Phonics games where students identify and pronounce words with silent /r/ sound, such as 'world', 'furthermore', and 'fertility'.

subject: English
competency: Interpret and explain visual information
teaching_strategy: Role-playing where students interpret and explain the first aid chart to their peers, focusing on the steps for treating an unconscious person.

subject: English
competency: Analyze the distribution of various household facilities among households in Nepal based on the 2011 census data.
teaching_strategy: Create a bar graph or pie chart using the provided data. Discuss the implications of the distribution with students, encouraging them to form hypotheses about the socio-economic conditions of different regions in Nepal.

subject: English
competency: Construct meaningful sentences by matching and combining sentence halves, enhancing understanding of conjunctions and their usage.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with sentence halves. Have students match and construct sentences, then role-play scenarios where these sentences could be used in real-life situations. Provide guided practice with additional examples.

subject: English
competency: Understand the reasons and patterns of bird migration
teaching_strategy: Use a guided discussion to explore the historical misconceptions about bird hibernation and introduce the correct understanding of their migration patterns. Engage students in a role-playing activity where they act as different bird species, sharing their migration stories and reasons for moving to new places.

subject: English
competency: Analyze the distribution of population based on language
teaching_strategy: Create a bar graph or pie chart using data from the 2011 population census to visually represent the distribution of languages in Kathmandu Metropolitan. Discuss the implications of this distribution and encourage students to form hypotheses about the reasons behind the language distribution.

subject: English
competency: Understand the concept of bird migration, including the challenges and strategies involved in long-distance travel.
teaching_strategy: Use a map to trace the migration paths of birds like the Chinook salmon and white-winged scoters. Have students create a timeline of a bird's migration journey, considering factors such as weather, energy management, and habitat changes.

subject: English
competency: Recognize that migration is not limited to birds but occurs in various animal species.
teaching_strategy: Organize a role-playing activity where students act out the migration of different animals (birds, insects, mammals) using flashcards with images and descriptions. Discuss the reasons for migration in each species and the challenges they face.

subject: English
competency: Understand the different migration behaviors of birds, including partial migration, stopover points, and the factors influencing their journey.
teaching_strategy: Create a bird migration map on the board. Have students identify and discuss the different migration patterns of birds such as brindled titmice, mountain chickadees, and robins. Use flashcards with images of birds to reinforce learning. Conduct a role-playing activity where students act as different bird species, sharing their migration stories and stopover experiences.

subject: English
competency: Recognize the importance of stopover sites for birds and the role of energy sources in their migration.
teaching_strategy: Set up a station with various objects representing different energy sources (e.g., berries, corn, insects). Have students sort and categorize these sources based on the type of bird that would use them. Use guided practice to discuss how birds use these sources during their migration. Create a game where students must match birds to their preferred stopover sites based on the available resources.

subject: English
competency: Understand and describe the reasons and behaviors of bird migration
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students act out different bird behaviors (e.g., feeding, flying in groups, migrating). Use flashcards with migration scenarios to prompt students to act out the correct behavior.

subject: English
competency: Identify different types of bird migration patterns
teaching_strategy: Guided practice where students match migration patterns (e.g., partial migration, complete migration) with their descriptions using a worksheet. Conduct a quiz where students categorize birds based on their migration patterns.

subject: English
topic: Reasons for animal migration and population status
competency: Listening and comprehension
teaching_strategy: Discuss the reasons for animal migration and have students brainstorm possible answers. Use role-playing to act out migration scenarios.

subject: English
competency: Reading and analysis
teaching_strategy: Provide students with the incomplete sentences and have them fill in the blanks with the correct words or phrases. Use flashcards to reinforce vocabulary related to wildlife and conservation.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to use appropriate conjunctions and conditional sentences in context.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a conjunctions and conditional sentences game where students match the correct conjunctions with given sentences. Provide flashcards with conjunctions and sentences for guided practice.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand and discuss the efforts made by Nepal to conserve wildlife.
teaching_strategy: Organize a role-playing activity where students discuss and present different efforts Nepal is making to save wildlife. Use current news articles or documentaries as references.

subject: English
competency: Identify and understand different types of adjectives and their usage in sentences.
teaching_strategy: Create a game where students categorize adjectives into types (descriptive, proper, quantity, numerical, quality) using flashcards. Provide examples and non-examples for each type.

subject: English
competency: Identify and use demonstrative, interrogative, possessive, and distributive adjectives in sentences.
teaching_strategy: Create a game where students categorize given adjectives into demonstrative, interrogative, possessive, and distributive. Use flashcards with examples like 'this vitamin', 'Whose pen is this?', 'my watch', and 'each man'.

subject: English
competency: Discuss favorite travel destinations in groups and justify preferences
teaching_strategy: Role-playing in groups where students act as travel agents and clients, discussing and justifying their travel choices

subject: English
competency: Express personal opinions about travel and favorite tourist spots
teaching_strategy: Phonics games focusing on vocabulary related to travel and tourism, followed by guided practice in answering questions about personal travel experiences

subject: English
topic: Cultural Heritage and Tourism in Nepal
competency: Understand the significance of cultural heritage sites and the impact of tourism on local culture.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity: Divide students into groups and assign each group a different historical site in Nepal (e.g., Patan Durbar Square, Kathmandu Durbar Square, and Bhaktapur Durbar Square). Have each group research the site, create a short presentation, and present it to the class. Encourage students to discuss the importance of preserving these sites and the role of tourism in promoting cultural awareness.

subject: English
topic: Urban and Rural Scenery in Nepal
competency: Describe the characteristics of different regions in Nepal and the unique features of each.
teaching_strategy: Flashcard Activity: Create flashcards with images and descriptions of Kathmandu, Chitwan, and Pokhara. Use these flashcards to quiz students on the unique features of each location. Follow up with a discussion on the differences and similarities between urban and rural settings in Nepal.

subject: English
topic: Cultural Practices and Beliefs in Nepal
competency: Understand the significance of cultural practices and beliefs in different parts of Nepal, including Durbar Squares, Pashupatinath Temple, and Chitwan National Park.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out different cultural scenarios, such as interacting with college students about the importance of skill over education, participating in a memorial ceremony, and meeting sadhus in Pashupatinath Temple.

subject: English
topic: Tourism and Cultural Experiences in Nepal
competency: Identify various tourist attractions and cultural experiences in Nepal, such as Thamel for nightlife, and Chitwan for wildlife and jungle activities.
teaching_strategy: Guided practice: Create a travel brochure or a presentation on different tourist destinations in Nepal, focusing on the cultural and natural experiences available.

subject: English
competency: Describe the unique features and attractions of Pokhara and Chitwan as tourist destinations.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity: Divide students into groups and assign each group a tourist destination (Pokhara or Chitwan). Each group should prepare a short presentation highlighting the key attractions and features of their assigned location. Encourage the use of descriptive language and vivid imagery to engage the audience.

subject: English
topic: Cultural and Natural Beauty of Nepal
competency: Identify and appreciate the natural and cultural landmarks in Nepal.
teaching_strategy: Guided practice: Show students pictures or videos of Pokhara and Chitwan. Ask them to identify the landmarks, natural features, and cultural elements discussed in the text. Follow up with a writing activity where students describe their ideal travel destination in Nepal, incorporating the elements they have learned.

subject: English
topic: Cultural and Historical Sites in Nepal
competency: Identify and describe key cultural and historical landmarks in Nepal, including their significance and local perceptions.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into groups and assign each group a landmark (e.g., Pashupatinath Temple, Kathmandu Durbar Square, Chitwan National Park). Have them research and prepare a short presentation on their assigned site, focusing on its historical significance and local perceptions. Encourage students to use the text as a reference.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and differentiate the pronunciation of various consonants in English.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Create a phonics game where students match words with similar consonant sounds. Use the provided examples and add more words to practice different consonant pronunciations. For instance, create a card for /tʃ/ with words like

subject: English
competency: Practice and develop conversational skills through role-playing
teaching_strategy: Divide students into groups of three and have them act out model conversations. Encourage students to create their own conversations based on given scenarios.

subject: English
competency: Enhance listening and speaking abilities by engaging in group discussions and role-plays
teaching_strategy: Use the provided model conversations as a basis for guided practice. Have students take turns being the speaker and listener, and provide feedback on pronunciation, intonation, and clarity.

subject: English
competency: Students will practice communication skills and role-playing through dialogues about living situations and aspirations.
teaching_strategy: Conduct role-playing activities where students pair up to discuss their living situations and future aspirations. Use the provided dialogue as a guide, encouraging students to improvise and add their own context.

subject: English
competency: Students will explore the roles and responsibilities within different family structures and the impact on personal development.
teaching_strategy: Have students analyze the dialogue to identify the roles of different family members (e.g., mother as a mason, father as a teacher). Discuss how these roles influence the students' lives and aspirations. Use flashcards with family roles to reinforce learning.

subject: English
competency: Identify and match sentences with their appropriate question tags
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Create a phonics game where students match sentences with their correct question tags. Use flashcards with sentences on one side and question tags on the other. Students can play in pairs or small groups to reinforce their understanding.

subject: English
competency: Form question tags for given sentences
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Have students role-play scenarios where they need to form question tags. For example, one student can say a sentence and another student must quickly form the correct question tag. This activity can be done in pairs or small groups to encourage interaction and practice.

subject: English
competency: Analyze and compare visual and textual descriptions of different seasons, identifying key characteristics and personal preferences.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of different seasons. Have students match the images with the textual descriptions provided in the poem. Conduct a role-playing activity where students act out the behaviors of the cuckoo and the shepherd in different weather conditions.

subject: English
competency: Identify words with similar meanings in a text and comprehend their usage in context.
teaching_strategy: Create a matching game where students match the given words/phrases with their synonyms found in the poem. Use flashcards for each word and have students work in pairs to find the correct matches.

subject: English
competency: Analyze and interpret the actions and descriptions of characters and natural elements in the poem.
teaching_strategy: Role-play the different characters in the poem (e.g., nightingale, girls, cuckoo, beeches, rooks) and have students act out the scenes described in the poem. This will help them understand the poem's narrative and the actions of the characters.

subject: English
competency: Describe the differences between summer and winter seasons and their impact on nature and human activities.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of summer and winter landscapes to help students identify the differences. Conduct a role-playing activity where students act as different animals and humans reacting to the weather conditions of summer and winter.

subject: English
competency: Understand the symbolic representation of seasons in poetry and relate it to the human life cycle.
teaching_strategy: Create a guided practice where students match different weather conditions with their symbolic meanings. Use a phonics game to reinforce the vocabulary related to seasons and weather.

subject: English
competency: Students will learn to prepare a brochure for a local tourist destination, including essential details such as name, location, accessibility, major attractions, entry requirements, and contact information.
teaching_strategy: Have students visit a local tourist spot, gather information, and create a brochure using provided details. Encourage creativity and attention to layout and design.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand and identify contractions, their formation, and appropriate usage in informal writing.
teaching_strategy: Introduce contractions through examples, explain their formation, and provide exercises where students identify and use contractions in sentences. Use games or quizzes to reinforce learning.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use common contractions in English
teaching_strategy: Create a flashcard game where students match contractions with their expanded forms. Use role-playing scenarios to practice using contractions in sentences.

subject: English
competency: Engage in discussions about personalities and places in Nepal using visual aids.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of famous personalities and places of Nepal. Have students pair up and practice asking and answering questions about the images.

subject: English
competency: Extract information from a visual and answer related questions.
teaching_strategy: Provide students with a variety of images and ask them to identify the subject and their notable features or achievements. Use guided practice to enhance their reading comprehension skills.

subject: English
competency: Understand the impact of life's adversities and develop resilience.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity: Divide students into groups and assign each group a character from the text. Have them act out scenes where the character faces challenges and how they overcome them. This will help students empathize and learn about resilience.

subject: English
competency: Analyze the influence of cultural beliefs on personal experiences and societal perceptions.
teaching_strategy: Discussion: Facilitate a class discussion on how cultural beliefs can shape one's life and the perceptions of others. Use the text as a case study and encourage students to share their own experiences or examples from their communities.

subject: English
competency: Develop empathy towards individuals with disabilities by understanding their struggles and challenges.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing exercises where students act as caregivers or individuals with disabilities to experience the limitations and emotions involved.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and discuss the social and physical barriers faced by individuals with disabilities in their daily lives.
teaching_strategy: Group discussions and case studies on historical figures with disabilities to highlight their contributions and challenges.

subject: English
competency: Identify antonyms and synonyms in context
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Create a word matching game where students match antonyms and synonyms. Use flashcards with words like 'calm' and 'opposite' or 'wish' and 'hope' to reinforce the concept.

subject: English
competency: Evaluate statements and draw inferences from the text
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Divide the class into groups and assign each group a statement to discuss and decide if it is true or false. Encourage them to justify their answers using evidence from the text.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to distinguish and pronounce homophones correctly based on their meanings.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with homophones on one side and their meanings on the other. Conduct a game where students have to match the correct pronunciation with the appropriate meaning.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to engage in a conversation using appropriate language and context.
teaching_strategy: Role-play the conversation between the woman and the police inspector. Divide the class into pairs and have them practice the dialogue. Encourage students to improvise and add their own context to the conversation.

subject: English
competency: Develop descriptive skills by describing people and places
teaching_strategy: Pair work and role-playing to describe friends, teachers, or parents; read and describe a village

subject: English
competency: Identify and understand relative clauses
teaching_strategy: Read a conversation and underline relative clauses used

subject: English
competency: Correctly use relative pronouns in sentences
teaching_strategy: Relative Pronoun Fill-in-Blanks Game: Provide students with a set of sentences with blanks and a list of relative pronouns. Have them fill in the blanks with the correct relative pronoun to complete the sentences. This can be done individually or in small groups, and can be made more engaging by turning it into a relay race where the first student to correctly fill in the blank gets a point for their team.

subject: English
competency: Understand and construct relative clauses
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing Activity: Divide the class into pairs. One student will be given a character and a situation, and the other will be asked to describe the character or situation using a relative clause. For example, if one student is a farmer, the other might say, 'The person who grows a lot of vegetables is a farmer.' This activity helps students practice forming and understanding relative clauses in context.

subject: English
competency: Identify and understand different sentence structures (declarative, imperative, and exclamatory) and their usage in context.
teaching_strategy: Use sentence building games where students create sentences using different structures. For example, provide a set of words and ask students to form declarative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences.

subject: English
competency: Write a short biography using provided outlines and factual information.
teaching_strategy: Assign students to write a short biography of Til Bikram Nembang Limbu using the given outlines. Provide them with additional information about his life and works to enrich their writing.

subject: English
competency: Identify and describe natural landmarks and their significance in a specific region.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of Sugarloaf Mountain, Morro de Babilonia, and Morro de Urca. Have students match the landmarks to their descriptions. Conduct a role-playing activity where students pretend to be tour guides explaining the significance of these landmarks to visitors.

subject: English
competency: Understand the concept of urban rock-climbing and its popularity.
teaching_strategy: Organize a simulated rock-climbing activity using a large ball or a soft climbing wall. Discuss the safety measures and the thrill of conquering a natural landmark. Have students write a short paragraph about their experience or what they would do if they were to climb Sugarloaf Mountain.

subject: English
topic: Cultural and Historical Significance of Sugar Loaf Mountain
competency: Understand the cultural and historical importance of Sugar Loaf Mountain in Rio de Janeiro, including its appearances in films and its role in colonial history.
teaching_strategy: Show students clips from the mentioned films and discuss the significance of Sugar Loaf Mountain in each. Use flashcards to list important historical facts and have students role-play as tour guides explaining the history to visitors.

subject: English
competency: Identify geographical features and tourist attractions in Rio de Janeiro, such as Sugar Loaf Mountain and Morro de Urca, and understand their accessibility and amenities.
teaching_strategy: Create a map activity where students plot the locations of Sugar Loaf Mountain and Morro de Urca, and discuss the amenities available at each. Use guided practice to have students describe the views and activities available at each mountain.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to form adjectives by adding '-ing' or '-ed' to verbs and use them in sentences.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Create a phonics game where students match verbs with their '-ing' or '-ed' adjectives. For example, 'annoy' - 'annoying', 'unfold' - 'unfolded'.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to read and comprehend short paragraphs and match them with appropriate headings.
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Assign each student a paragraph and have them read it aloud. Then, ask them to match their paragraph with the correct heading. This can be done in pairs or small groups.

subject: English
competency: Evaluate tourist attractions and activities
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into groups and assign each group a tourist attraction (Sugarloaf Mountain, Guanabara Bay). Have them prepare a short presentation on the location, history, and activities available. Encourage students to discuss the feasibility of rock-climbing and the preferences of children.

subject: English
competency: Comprehend and respond to spoken English
teaching_strategy: Listening Game: Play the audio clip and have students work in pairs to complete the sentences. Follow up with a discussion on the characters' appearance and the story's context.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to correctly use prepositions in various contexts.
teaching_strategy: Provide flashcards with prepositions and have students match them with the correct sentences. Use role-playing to act out scenarios where the correct preposition is used, such as traveling to different places by different means of transportation.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe a friend's physical appearance and physical characteristics in a sentence.
teaching_strategy: Have students describe their friends using five sentences. Use a descriptive writing game where students must guess which friend is being described based on the sentences provided.

subject: English
topic: Writing a Letter or Email to a Foreign Friend
competency: Write a letter or email about a tourist destination in Nepal, including interesting facts and an invitation to visit.
teaching_strategy: Have students choose a tourist destination, research it, and write a letter or email to a hypothetical foreign friend. Use transition words to connect ideas smoothly.

subject: English
competency: Research and present a life story of a community personality who has made a special contribution.
teaching_strategy: Assign students to research a local personality, compile their findings, and present the story in class. Encourage the use of transition words to enhance the flow of the presentation.

subject: English
competency: Identify and use appropriate connectives and transition words to enhance coherence in writing and speech.
teaching_strategy: Create a connective chain game where students form sentences using different types of connectives. For example, provide a sentence starter like 'The teacher entered the classroom,' and have students add a connective and a clause, such as 'therefore, the students became quiet.' This activity helps students understand the function of each type of connective in different contexts.

subject: English
competency: Understand and apply various sentence structures to improve the flow and clarity of written and spoken English.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with sentences that lack connectives and have students add the appropriate connectives to make the sentences coherent. For instance, provide a sentence like 'She went to the store,' and have students add 'then' to make it 'She went to the store, then she bought groceries.' This exercise reinforces the use of transition words and enhances sentence structure.

subject: English
competency: Identify and discuss the characteristics of successful individuals
teaching_strategy: Role-playing and discussion

subject: English
competency: Understand the journey from humble beginnings to success
teaching_strategy: Guided reading and question-based analysis

subject: English
competency: Understand the challenges and successes in Walt Disney's life and how they contributed to his success in the entertainment industry.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing Activity: Divide students into groups and assign each group a significant event in Walt Disney's life (e.g., his childhood, his first business failure, his move to Los Angeles). Have each group prepare a short skit or presentation to share their assigned event with the class. This activity will help students understand the perseverance and creativity required for success.

subject: English
competency: Recognize the importance of resilience and adaptability in business and personal life.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Provide students with a scenario where a business faces multiple setbacks. Ask them to brainstorm strategies for overcoming these challenges and creating a successful business. This exercise will help students develop problem-solving skills and understand the value of persistence.

subject: English
competency: Understand the challenges and perseverance required in building a successful business.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students act out the scenario of Walt Disney starting over after losing his rights to Oswald the Lucky Rabbit. Discuss the importance of innovation and resilience in business.

subject: English
competency: Recognize key milestones and challenges in the early history of animation and film.
teaching_strategy: Create a timeline of Walt Disney's major achievements and setbacks. Use flashcards for key dates and events, and have students present their findings to the class.

subject: English
competency: Understand the importance of perseverance in business ventures and how failures can lead to success.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students act out scenarios of starting a business and facing initial challenges. Discuss how characters overcome these obstacles using Disney's quote as a guiding principle.

subject: English
competency: Recognize the initial difficulties faced by Disneyland and its eventual success.
teaching_strategy: Create a timeline activity where students plot the key events of Disneyland's opening, including the challenges and the eventual success. Use flashcards with images and brief descriptions of each event.

subject: English
topic: Chronological Order of Events in Walt Disney's Life
competency: Rewrite events in chronological order and understand the sequence of significant milestones in Walt Disney's career.
teaching_strategy: Ask students to arrange the given sentences in chronological order. Use flashcards with each sentence to make it interactive. Discuss the significance of each event as they place them in the correct sequence.

subject: English
competency: Analyze and discuss key aspects of Walt Disney's life, including his childhood, family background, and business failures and successes.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a role-playing activity where students take turns to be Walt Disney and answer the questions posed in section D. Use a timeline to plot his life events and discuss the impact of each event on his career.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to look up words in a dictionary, pronounce them correctly, and identify the stressed syllables.
teaching_strategy: Provide flashcards with words and have students practice pronunciation. Use a dictionary app or physical dictionary for reference. Play a game where students earn points for correctly identifying the stressed syllable.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to use appropriate expressions to convey congratulations in different situations.
teaching_strategy: Role-play different scenarios where students need to give and receive congratulations. Use the provided expressions as a guide and encourage students to create their own. Conduct a role-play competition where groups present different situations and the class votes on the most appropriate expression used.

subject: English
competency: Use appropriate prepositions in various contexts
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Create a phonics game where students match prepositions with their correct usage in sentences. For example, provide cards with prepositions and sentences, and have students place the prepositions in the correct spots.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use time expressions correctly
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Have students role-play different scenarios involving time expressions. For example, one student can ask another when they reached school, and the other student can respond using the correct preposition.

subject: English
competency: Use appropriate prepositions in context
teaching_strategy: Create a preposition scavenger hunt where students find and correct prepositions in sentences. Use flashcards with prepositions and have students match them with the correct sentences.

subject: English
competency: Write a formal congratulatory message
teaching_strategy: Role-play the scenario where students write a congratulatory message to the winning team. Provide a template and have students fill in the blanks with appropriate content. Follow up with peer review and editing sessions.

subject: English
competency: Compose a congratulatory letter to a family member
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students write and deliver congratulatory letters to each other, focusing on appropriate language and structure.

subject: English
competency: Identify and reflect on personal qualities for success
teaching_strategy: Guided discussion and reflective writing activity where students list and discuss qualities for success, followed by a personal reflection on their own adherence to these qualities.

subject: English
competency: Analyze the themes and emotions in Rudyard Kipling's poem 'If'.
teaching_strategy: Use role-playing to have students act out different scenarios from the poem, such as facing adversity or maintaining integrity in the face of criticism. Discuss the emotions and themes as they perform.

subject: English
competency: Identify personal qualities and virtues highlighted in the poem and discuss their relevance in real-life situations.
teaching_strategy: Create flashcards with key phrases from the poem and have students match them with the virtues they represent. Engage in guided discussions on how these virtues can be applied in daily life.

subject: English
competency: Match words/phrases with their correct meanings and use them in context.
teaching_strategy: Create a vocabulary matching game where students match the words/phrases with their meanings using flashcards. Then, have them use the words in sentences to reinforce their understanding.

subject: English
competency: Identify and discuss the themes and values in Rudyard Kipling's poem 'If'.
teaching_strategy: Read the poem aloud as a class and discuss the meanings behind each stanza. Use role-playing to act out different scenarios that embody the values discussed in the poem. Encourage students to reflect on how they can apply these values in their own lives.

subject: English
competency: Analyze the poet's advice on handling lies and dreams, and discuss the importance of perseverance and setting realistic goals.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing scenarios where students act out situations involving lies and dreams. Discuss the outcomes and the importance of honesty and setting achievable goals.

subject: English
competency: Understand the concept of personal responsibility and its role in achieving success, and explore the significance of overcoming failures.
teaching_strategy: Create a flashcard activity where students match quotes about success with their meanings. Discuss the importance of not giving up and learning from failures.

subject: English
competency: Identify reasons for success and hard work in personal narratives
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out scenarios where they face challenges and overcome them, emphasizing the importance of hard work and second chances.

subject: English
competency: Understand the speaker's perspective on success and opportunities
teaching_strategy: Guided discussion: Use the speech as a basis for a class discussion on what makes a person successful. Encourage students to share their own experiences and reflections.

subject: English
competency: Use prepositional phrases correctly in sentences
teaching_strategy: Provide flashcards with prepositional phrases. Have students match the phrases with their meanings and use them in sentences. Conduct a role-playing activity where students create scenarios and use the correct prepositional phrases.

subject: English
competency: Write a speech and draft a report on a given topic
teaching_strategy: Guide students through the process of drafting a speech on 'Failure as a Pillar of Success'. Use examples from successful personalities. For the project work, organize a field trip to meet a successful person in the community. Prepare a structured interview guide and have students conduct interviews. Follow up with a class discussion and sharing of reports.

subject: English
topic: Understanding and using archaic English words
competency: Identify and translate common archaic English words into modern usage
teaching_strategy: Create a matching game where students match the old English words with their modern equivalents. Use flashcards with the old English words on one side and the modern words on the other. Encourage students to use these words in sentences to reinforce their understanding.

subject: English
competency: Analyze and compare characteristics of different cities
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of different cities to facilitate a discussion on similarities and differences. Have students create their own flashcards and share with classmates.

subject: English
competency: Identify and compare key features of famous cities
teaching_strategy: Conduct a role-playing activity where students take on the roles of tourists visiting London and Paris. Encourage them to discuss and highlight the unique features of each city.

subject: English
topic: Geographical and Demographic Comparisons of London and Paris
competency: Students will understand the geographical locations, areas, and population densities of London and Paris.
teaching_strategy: Use a map to locate London and Paris. Have students calculate the population density of each city using provided data. Create a comparative chart to visualize the differences.

subject: English
topic: Cultural Differences in Greetings and Language
competency: Students will recognize and appreciate cultural differences in greetings and the importance of language in different societies.
teaching_strategy: Role-play different scenarios where students greet each other using the appropriate French or English greetings. Use flashcards with images of people greeting to reinforce the concept. Encourage students to practice speaking French with their peers.

subject: English
topic: Comparison of Paris and London in terms of cost of living and transportation
competency: Analyze the cost of living and transportation differences between Paris and London
teaching_strategy: Create a comparative chart using flashcards where students fill in the costs and transportation details for both cities. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of each city based on the data.

subject: English
topic: Cultural and culinary differences between Paris and London
competency: Describe the cultural and culinary scenes in Paris and London
teaching_strategy: Organize a role-playing activity where students act as tourists and decide which city to visit based on their preferences for cuisine and culture. Use flashcards with images of famous French and British dishes and landmarks.

subject: English
topic: Comparison of Tourism in London and Paris
competency: Analyze the economic and tourist attractions of London and Paris, and determine the ideal duration for a vacation based on budget and interests.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into groups and have them create a travel itinerary for a friend visiting either London or Paris. Each group should consider factors such as cost, attractions, and ideal duration.

subject: English
topic: Seasonal Weather and Events in London and Paris
competency: Evaluate the best times to visit London and Paris based on weather and cultural events.
teaching_strategy: Guided practice: Create a timeline of major events and festivals in London and Paris for each month of the year. Have students identify the best time to visit based on their interests and budget.

subject: English
competency: Practice sentences with correct intonation patterns through role-playing and phonics games.
teaching_strategy: Have students practice the given sentences in pairs or small groups, using phonics games to improve their intonation. Encourage them to record their voices and compare them with the correct intonation patterns.

subject: English
competency: Develop skills in comparing and contrasting objects through visual analysis and discussion.
teaching_strategy: Use the provided pictures of a traditional house and a modern house to conduct a class discussion. Ask students to identify similarities and differences. Follow up with a role-play activity where students describe the houses and justify their comparisons.

subject: English
topic: Using adjectives and adjectival phrases in conversations
competency: Practice forming and using descriptive phrases in dialogue
teaching_strategy: Pair role-playing activity where students create and have conversations using the provided adjectives and adjectival phrases.

subject: English
competency: Use adjectives and adverbs correctly in sentences
teaching_strategy: Phonics games: Create a phonics game where students match adjectives and adverbs with their correct forms. For example, provide cards with 'poor' and 'poorly' and have students place them in the correct sentences.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use comparative and superlative forms of adjectives and adverbs
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into groups and assign them different scenarios where they need to use comparative and superlative forms. For example, one group could role-play a market where they compare the prices and qualities of different goods.

subject: English
competency: Analyze the theme of contrast between rural and urban lifestyles through the narrative of the mice and the city mouse.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into groups and assign roles of the country mouse and the city mouse. Have them act out the story, emphasizing the differences in lifestyle and preferences.

subject: English
competency: Discuss the cultural differences in food preferences and the impact of environment on dietary habits.
teaching_strategy: Discussion and Debate: Organize a class discussion on the preferences of the mice and the city mouse. Follow up with a debate on whether food preferences are influenced by environment or personal choice.

subject: English
competency: Define and use words in context
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with the words 'trifle', 'deal with', 'regale', 'endure', and 'facial expression' to help students understand their meanings and usage.

subject: English
competency: Analyze and interpret a story
teaching_strategy: Role-play the story of the country and town mice. Ask students to discuss and answer the questions in part C to enhance their comprehension and critical thinking skills.

subject: English
topic: Geographical Knowledge of Quebec and Montreal
competency: Identify and differentiate between Quebec City and Montreal based on given statements.
teaching_strategy: Play the audio and have students listen carefully. Distribute flashcards with statements and have them match the correct city. Conduct a class discussion to reinforce the differences.

subject: English
competency: Use appropriate connectives to complete sentences.
teaching_strategy: Provide sentence starters and connectives. Have students work in pairs to complete the sentences. Use role-playing to act out scenarios where these connectives are used naturally.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and construct simple conditional sentences using 'if' and 'when'.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with conditional sentences to help students identify the structure. Create a role-playing activity where students practice forming sentences based on given scenarios.

subject: English
competency: Describe a place using sensory details and contextual information.
teaching_strategy: Guide students through a brainstorming session to gather details about Lamidada village. Use guided practice to write short descriptive paragraphs about the village, focusing on its natural beauty and rural charm. Provide examples of descriptive language and encourage students to use vivid adjectives and adverbs.

subject: English
competency: Identify and differentiate between independent and dependent clauses, and understand their usage in sentences.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with examples of independent and dependent clauses. Have students create their own sentences using coordinate conjunctions (for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so) to connect two independent clauses. Conduct a role-playing activity where students interview each other about their likes, dislikes, and skills, and then present a short report in class.

subject: English
competency: Analyze and discuss the frequency and types of movies watched and their preferences
teaching_strategy: Phonics games can be used to improve vocabulary related to movies and entertainment. Role-playing can be employed to simulate discussions about movie preferences and viewing habits.

subject: English
competency: Analyze the theme of loyalty and devotion through the story of Hachi and Parker Wilson, and discuss how these values are portrayed in the film.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity: Divide students into pairs and have them act out scenes from the film where Hachi waits for Parker at the station. Encourage students to express the emotions of both Hachi and Parker to understand the depth of their relationship.

subject: English
topic: Media and Public Recognition of Devotion
competency: Examine how Hachi's story gained media attention and discuss the impact of media on public perception of loyalty and devotion.
teaching_strategy: Guided discussion: Show clips from the film where Hachi's story is reported in the media. Discuss with students how media can influence public opinion and the importance of authentic stories in shaping societal values.

subject: English
competency: Understand the importance of stable and loving relationships in society.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students act out scenes of a stable and loving marriage, emphasizing communication and mutual respect.

subject: English
competency: Recognize cultural symbols and their meanings in films.
teaching_strategy: Flashcard activity where students match symbols (like the number 8) with their meanings and discuss the significance in different cultures.

subject: English
competency: Identify and define words from context
teaching_strategy: Provide students with the context and ask them to identify and define the words. Use flashcards to reinforce the meanings.

subject: English
competency: Evaluate the accuracy of statements based on the text
teaching_strategy: Have students read the statements and discuss as a class to determine the accuracy. Use role-playing to act out the scenarios described in the statements.

subject: English
competency: Analyze and discuss elements of a movie, including character relationships and critiques
teaching_strategy: Role-playing and group discussion

subject: English
competency: Practice and improve pronunciation of numbers and years
teaching_strategy: Phonics games and guided practice

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to ask for and give opinions on various topics.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide the class into pairs and have them take turns asking for and giving opinions on the provided topics (Nepali movies, social media, television, homework, examination, politics).

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to construct questions using proper word order and context.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Use phonics games to help students understand the correct pronunciation and order of words in questions. For example, create a game where students have to rearrange word cards to form correct questions.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to formulate appropriate questions in various real-life situations.
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Organize role-playing activities where students practice asking questions in different scenarios. For example, one student can pretend to be a friend inviting another to their home, and the other can respond appropriately.

subject: English
topic: Social Media Impact and Viral Content
competency: Analyze the impact of social media on real-life situations and the potential for viral content.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing Activity: Divide students into groups and have them create short skits or videos that could go viral on social media. Discuss the potential positive and negative impacts of such content.

subject: English
competency: Understand the role of social media in providing support and creating community connections.
teaching_strategy: Flashcard Activity: Create flashcards with different scenarios (e.g., lost pet, fundraising event) and have students brainstorm how social media could be used to support the cause. Discuss the importance of community support.

subject: English
competency: Understand the role of social media in raising awareness and funds for charitable causes.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing Activity: Divide students into groups and assign each group a social media influencer. Have them create a scenario where the influencer uses their platform to raise funds for a charitable cause. Encourage students to brainstorm creative ways to engage their followers and maximize donations.

subject: English
topic: Cause and Effect in Real-Life Scenarios
competency: Analyze real-life situations to understand the consequences of actions and the impact of technology on society.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Provide students with a series of real-life scenarios (e.g., a local community event, a natural disaster) and ask them to predict the potential outcomes and effects. Use this activity to discuss the importance of social responsibility and the role of technology in spreading awareness.

subject: English
competency: Students will learn to identify and use appropriate vocabulary in context.
teaching_strategy: Flashcards with images can be used to help students associate words with their meanings. For example, create flashcards for 'pandemic', 'overwhelm', 'somersaulting', 'accumulate', 'voicemail', 'sanctuary', and 'accumulate'.

subject: English
competency: Students will improve their reading comprehension and critical thinking skills by answering questions based on the text.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing can be used to enhance understanding. For instance, students can act out scenarios based on the questions provided, such as Nathan Apodaca's video or the social media impact on Charlie's birthday. This will help them think critically about the context and implications of the text.

subject: English
competency: Identify and use passive voice and causative verbs in sentences.
teaching_strategy: Create a role-playing activity where students act out scenarios using both active and passive voice sentences. For example, one student can be a technician fixing a television, and another can be getting their assignment edited. This helps students understand the structure and usage of causative verbs and passive voice.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and use correct verb forms in different contexts.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with sentences and blanks for students to fill in the correct verb forms. For instance, 'I don't let my children ___________ video games.' This activity reinforces the correct use of verb tenses and forms.

subject: English
competency: Developing argumentative writing and critical thinking
teaching_strategy: Have students engage in a debate or discussion on the impacts of social media, followed by writing an essay expressing their opinions. Use the provided essay prompt as a starting point.

subject: English
competency: Improving pronunciation of numbers in English
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with phone numbers to practice saying each digit individually, doubles, and triples. Incorporate role-playing scenarios where students practice giving and receiving phone numbers in English.

subject: Science
competency: प्रायोगिक कार्यक्रमको विवरण लेख्न र उनको महत्त्व सम्बन्धी जानकारी देने
teaching_strategy: प्रायोगिक कार्यक्रमको विवरण लेख्न र उनको महत्त्व सम्बन्धी जानकारी देने लागि विभिन्न प्रकारका उदाहरणहरू दिइएको र छात्रहरूले उनको विवरण लेख्न सक्ने प्रायोग गर्नुहोस्।

subject: Science
competency: संख्याहरू गणना र गुणन गर्ने क्षमता पनि विकसित गर्नुहोस्। यहाँ 36 भन्ने गणना र गुणन गर्ने अभ्यास दिइएको छ। यसको माध्यममा छात्रहरूले गणना र गुणन गर्ने अभ्यास गर्न सक्छन्।
teaching_strategy: निर्दिष्ट संख्याहरू गणना र गुणन गर्ने अभ्यास दिइएको छ जसको माध्यममा छात्रहरूले गणना र गुणन गर्ने अभ्यास गर्न सक्छन्। यसमा छात्रहरूले निर्दिष्ट संख्याहरू गणना र गुणन गर्ने अभ्यास गर्न सक्छन्।

subject: Science
competency: कार्यक्रम र योजना बनाउने र तर्क द्यने
teaching_strategy: स्टूडेंटलाई विभिन्न योजनाहरू तयार गर्नुपर्छ र उनलाई तर्क दिनुपर्छ। योजनाहरूलाई तयार गर्दा उनलाई विभिन्न विषयहरूमा कृत्रिम काम गर्ने र उनको परिणाम देख्ने अभ्यास गर्नुपर्छ।

subject: Science
competency: फोटोसिनथेसिस अनुसार वनस्पति को ऊर्जा निर्माण गर्ने प्रक्रिया विश्लेषण गर्नुहोस्।
teaching_strategy: प्लास्टिक छत्र र जलवायु विशेषताहरू सहित फोटोसिनथेसिस अनुसार वनस्पति को ऊर्जा निर्माण गर्ने प्रक्रिया दर्शाउनुहोस्। यसको लागि छत्र र जलवायुको विभिन्न अवस्थामा फोटोसिनथेसिस अनुसार ऊर्जा निर्माण गर्ने प्रक्रियाहरू दर्शाउनुहोस्।

subject: Science
competency: संख्या अनुक्रम र उनको फरक ज्ञान गर्नुहोस्।
teaching_strategy: 10 र 15 भन्ने संख्या अनुक्रम बनाउनुहोस्। यसको लागि गणितको गुणोत्तर गुणन र भागन द्वारा दिए गए उदाहरणहरू उपयोग गर्दा संख्या अनुक्रम र उनको फरक ज्ञान गर्नुहोस्।

subject: Science
competency: संख्याहरूको अनुपात र अनुपातीको अनुपात गणना गर्ने र उनको अनुपात ज्ञात गर्ने पाठकले पत्ता लगाउने।
teaching_strategy: क्षेत्रीय राशिहरू (जस्तो जमीन, बाटो) काउँटरहरू द्वारा दिइएको अनुपात र अनुपातीको अनुपात गणना गर्ने अभ्यास गर्नुहोस्।

subject: Science
competency: संख्याहरू गणना गर्नुहोस् र दो संख्याहरूको बीचको अंतर ज्ञात गर्नुहोस्।
teaching_strategy: कार्यक्रमहरूमा नीतिभित्र र निर्धारित अंतरहरूको दरम्यान गणना गर्ने अभ्यास दिनुहोस्। उदाहरणका लागि, दो निर्धारित अंतरहरूको दरम्यान गणना गर्ने अभ्यास दिनुहोस्।

subject: Science
competency: संख्याहरूको व्यवस्था र अंतर ज्ञात गर्नुहोस्।
teaching_strategy: संख्याहरूको व्यवस्था र अंतर ज्ञात गर्ने अभ्यास दिनुहोस्। उदाहरणका लागि, दो निर्धारित संख्याहरूको दरम्यान अंतर ज्ञात गर्ने अभ्यास दिनुहोस्।

teaching_strategy: संख्याहरूको योग र घटाहरू गर्ने अभ्यास सामग्री उपयोग गर्नुहोस्। उदाहरणका लागि, निर्वाचित संख्याहरूको योग र घटाहरू गर्ने अभ्यास गर्नुहोस्।

subject: English
competency: Describe travel plans and experiences
teaching_strategy: Use picture analysis and personal reflection to discuss travel intentions and experiences.

subject: English
competency: Develop questioning techniques to elicit information
teaching_strategy: Engage students in a discussion using the provided questions to enhance their questioning skills.

subject: English
topic: Trekking Experience in Pokhara and Annapurna Region
