subject: English
competency: Identify types of food and understand the importance of a balanced diet
teaching_strategy: Create a 'Food Circle' activity where students bring in pictures or real samples of food items they eat. Discuss as a class which foods are part of a balanced diet and which ones need to be consumed more. Use flashcards with images of different food groups to reinforce learning.

subject: English
competency: Describe ways to take care of one's body
teaching_strategy: Engage students in a 'Body Care Role-Play' where they act out different scenarios of taking care of their bodies, such as washing hands, brushing teeth, and exercising. Provide each student with a worksheet where they write five sentences about how they take care of their bodies.

subject: English
competency: Develop phonemic awareness and listening skills
teaching_strategy: Rhyming Game: Create a rhyming game where students match words that rhyme. Use flashcards with words like 'kind' and 'old' and have students find pairs.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use basic personal and family information in sentences
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Divide students into pairs and have them practice talking about their families using sentences similar to the example given. Encourage them to use simple sentences like 'My mother is thirty-five.'

subject: English
competency: Describe daily morning activities of a character and relate them to personal experiences.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out the morning routine of Bunny. Encourage them to use the sequence of events (getting up, eating breakfast, reading, dressing up, going to school) in their role-play.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use time-related vocabulary (o'clock, half past) in context.
teaching_strategy: Flashcards: Create flashcards with times (7:30, 8:30, 9:30) and corresponding activities (getting up, eating breakfast, going to school). Use these for quick recognition and recall exercises.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to identify and read the time on a clock.
teaching_strategy: Use a large clock model in the classroom and play a game where students take turns to set the clock to different times and ask each other 'What time is it now?'

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to identify common household objects and their uses.
teaching_strategy: Create a flashcard activity where students match objects like clock, television, lamp, and telephone with their functions. Use role-playing to act out scenarios involving these objects.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and sequence days of the week through dialogue and questions.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of the days of the week. Conduct a role-play activity where students take turns being Chunu and Munu, asking and answering questions about the day of the week.

subject: English
topic: Daily activities and responsibilities in the kitchen
competency: Describe and identify daily tasks and roles in the kitchen
teaching_strategy: Role-playing kitchen tasks. Divide students into pairs and assign roles (Bindu, mother, father). Have them act out the morning routine described in the text.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and describe personal skills and habits related to cleanliness and organization
teaching_strategy: Flashcard activity. Create flashcards with images and words related to kitchen tasks (cleaning plates, peeling potatoes, setting the table). Use these to reinforce vocabulary and encourage students to describe their own kitchen habits.

subject: English
competency: Describe daily activities of a student at school
teaching_strategy: Use picture cards of different activities (singing, dancing, playing games, reading, writing, playing ball) and have students match them to the corresponding actions in the story. Encourage students to act out these activities in small groups.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use time-related vocabulary
teaching_strategy: Create a timeline activity where students place events in order, such as 'arrives at school,' 'plays with friends,' 'reads and writes,' and 'goes home.' Use a clock or a digital timer to demonstrate the concept of time.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to sequence daily activities and times on a clock.
teaching_strategy: Use a large clock face to demonstrate times. Have students role-play getting up, eating breakfast, and other morning activities at the given times. Create a classroom clock and have students place pictures of activities at the appropriate times.

subject: English
competency: Students will practice speaking and listening skills by discussing their daily routines with classmates.
teaching_strategy: Pair students and have them take turns talking about their daily routines. Use flashcards with pictures of activities to prompt discussions. Encourage students to ask each other questions about their routines.

subject: English
competency: Ask and answer questions about daily school menu items
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Students can act as cafeteria staff and classmates, practicing asking and answering questions about the menu items for each day of the week.

subject: English
topic: Recognizing and naming common food items
competency: Identify and discuss favorite foods
teaching_strategy: Flashcards: Create flashcards with pictures and names of the food items mentioned in the menu. Use these for a quick recognition game or matching activity.

subject: English
competency: Identify and describe key features of a school
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of school buildings, grounds, and playthings. Have students match the flashcards to the descriptions in the text.

subject: English
competency: Express personal opinions and emotions related to school
teaching_strategy: Role-play different scenarios in the classroom, such as playing on the swings or observing butterflies. Encourage students to share their own experiences and feelings about school.

subject: English
competency: Describe daily activities after school
teaching_strategy: Use picture cards of Bunny's activities (playing with friends, doing homework, eating dinner, watching TV, listening to stories) and have students match them to the corresponding sentences. Encourage students to share their own evening activities using similar sentences.

subject: English
competency: Understand and describe a bedtime routine
teaching_strategy: Create a simple role-play scenario where students act out Bunny's bedtime routine. Use a clock to teach about time (e.g., dinner time, story time, bedtime).

subject: English
competency: Students will identify and name objects such as pond, fence, fish, swing, slide, nest, flowers, bench, trees, and lotus in a picture.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of the objects to help students recognize and name them. Have students point to the objects in the picture as they are named.

subject: English
competency: Students will describe objects found in a school garden and write about them.
teaching_strategy: Guide students to observe and describe objects in their own school garden. Use role-playing where students pretend to be teachers and ask students to identify and describe objects in the garden. Provide sentence starters like 'In our school garden, we have...' to help students write about the objects.

subject: English
competency: Recite and identify the days of the week in sequence.
teaching_strategy: Flashcard Game: Create flashcards with the days of the week. Have students recite the days in order, using the flashcards as prompts. Mix up the order to reinforce sequence recognition.

subject: English
topic: Daily routine and care of plants
competency: Describe daily activities and responsibilities related to gardening
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students act out Munu's morning routine in the garden. Use props like a watering can and small plants to enhance understanding.

subject: English
competency: Express personal preferences and activities
teaching_strategy: Create a 'My Favorite Garden' activity where students draw their own gardens and write about their favorite parts. Use flashcards with garden-related vocabulary to support writing.

subject: English
competency: Describe daily activities and leisure on weekends
teaching_strategy: Use picture cards of different activities (garden work, field work, bathing, playing with family) and have students match them to the corresponding sentences. Encourage students to share their own Saturday activities using the sentence structure provided.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to form simple sentences using given words.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Use phonics games to help students understand the sounds of the word 'guest' and construct sentences like 'The guest is coming to our house.'

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to create descriptive sentences about pictures.
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Have students act out scenarios involving guests, such as welcoming a guest or serving tea to a guest, and then describe these actions in sentences.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe weather conditions and engage in outdoor activities.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into groups and assign each group a weather condition (sunny, rainy, windy) and an activity (cycling, swimming, playing). Have them act out the scenario from the text, using props like a toy boat for the river and sand toys for the sand play.

subject: English
competency: Students will identify and use adjectives to describe objects and actions.
teaching_strategy: Adjective Hunt: Provide students with flashcards of adjectives like 'sunny', 'clean', 'hot', and 'calm'. Have them find examples in the text and use them in sentences. For example, 'The river water is calm and clean.'

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe their experiences at the zoo using simple sentences and vocabulary related to zoo activities.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into pairs. One student acts as Bunny, describing his zoo visit, while the other asks questions or comments. Switch roles to practice different scenarios.

subject: English
competency: Students will compare their own zoo experiences with those of their classmates, enhancing their speaking and listening skills.
teaching_strategy: Group Discussion: Organize a group discussion where students share their experiences at the zoo. Use flashcards with zoo-related vocabulary to support their conversation.

subject: English
topic: Greetings and Days of the Week
competency: Practice greetings and discuss favorite school days through dialogue.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students pair up and practice greetings followed by a conversation about their favorite school days. Use the dialogue from the page as a model.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and pronounce words with similar sounds.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Create flashcards with words from the list (get, set, night, right, take, lake, sit, bit, fair, pair, pet, net, pray, bray, read, lead). Play a matching game where students match words with similar sounds.

subject: English
competency: Read a short passage and answer true or false questions based on the information provided.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of the characters and events from the passage. Have students match the flashcards to the correct sentences. Then, engage them in a role-playing activity where they act out the story with peers.

subject: English
competency: Write a short paragraph about a personal experience.
teaching_strategy: Provide students with a simple template to fill in the blanks: 'During my last holiday, I went to _______. I did _______ and _______. I enjoyed _______ the most.' Guide them to fill in the blanks with their own experiences and encourage them to use simple past tense verbs.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe activities and items bought at a fair using simple sentences.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into pairs. One student acts as Bunny, and the other asks questions about Bunny's fair experience. Use flashcards with pictures of balloons, toys, and Ferris wheels to aid in the conversation.

subject: English
competency: Students will practice writing numbers 1 to 5.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Provide number cards 1-5. Have students match the numbers with corresponding quantities of objects (e.g., 1 balloon, 2 toys) and then write the numbers in their notebooks.

subject: English
competency: Engage in discussions about fair activities and practice writing about them.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into groups and assign each group a fair activity (e.g., riding a carousel, eating cotton candy). Have them act out the activity and then write about it in their notebooks.

subject: English
competency: Students will learn to identify and sequence days of the week in context of a school event.
teaching_strategy: Use a calendar or a weekly chart to visually demonstrate the sequence of days. Have students role-play the teacher and students to practice asking and answering questions about test dates.

subject: English
competency: Students will prepare for a unit test by organizing information and practicing related topics.
teaching_strategy: Create flashcards with test dates and subjects. Conduct a guided practice session where students ask and answer questions about the test schedule.

subject: English
competency: Describe daily activities and religious practices in a sequence.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out the sequence of activities Sanu performed on Sunday morning. Use props like a basket, flowers, and a small tika to enhance the role-play.

subject: English
competency: Identify common religious practices and places in the context of Hinduism.
teaching_strategy: Flashcards: Create flashcards with images of temples, goddess Durga, and tika. Use these to teach the significance of each element in the story.

subject: English
competency: Students will practice identifying and matching words with the same initial sound through listening and writing activities.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with words having the same initial sound for a phonics game. Have students listen and tick the matching pairs.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand and use simple sentences related to daily routines and habits.
teaching_strategy: Role-play daily activities with students. Use sentence completion exercises to reinforce vocabulary and sentence structure.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to correctly use 'and' and 'but' in sentences.
teaching_strategy: Conjunctions Game: Create a simple game where students match sentences with the correct conjunction. For example, provide cards with 'and' and 'but' and other sentence cards. Students must find the correct conjunction to complete each sentence.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to write about their daily routines.
teaching_strategy: Daily Routine Role-Play: Have students act out their daily routines in pairs or small groups. Encourage them to use the sentences they wrote and add more details. This can be followed by a writing activity where they write about their routines.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to identify and describe different activities performed by students during a snack break through observation and discussion.
teaching_strategy: Show students pictures of the activities mentioned (sitting, walking on the ground, skipping, talking) and have them describe the actions in their own words. Encourage them to share their own experiences of snack breaks.

subject: English
competency: Students will practice speaking and listening skills by discussing their own snack break activities with classmates.
teaching_strategy: Organize a role-playing activity where students act out different snack break scenarios. Have them practice asking and answering questions about what their classmates do during snack breaks.

subject: English
topic: Identifying Objects in a Lunch Box
competency: Students will be able to recognize and name common lunch box items through listening and interactive activities.
teaching_strategy: Use实物卡片展示不同的午餐盒物品，如面包、米饭、香蕉和三明治。通过提问和回答游戏，让学生识别并说出这些物品。例如，展示一张面包卡片，问学生：“Is it bread?” 学生回答后，教师确认：“No, it isn't. Is it rice?” 以此类推，直到确认正确的物品。

subject: English
competency: Students will construct simple sentences using given vocabulary.
teaching_strategy: Provide students with flashcards of the words 'sandwich', 'skunk', 'carrot', and 'lunch box'. Guide them to create sentences using these words. For example, 'I have a sandwich in my lunch box.' Encourage creativity and allow students to share their sentences with the class.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to identify and describe objects in a story context.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out the conversation between Will and Kate. Assign one student to be Will and another to be Kate. Encourage them to use descriptive language as they answer each other's questions.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand and solve simple riddles.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Create a phonics game where students match words with their sounds. Use words from the riddle like 'black', 'white', and 'flowers' to reinforce phonetic awareness.

subject: English
topic: Describing and asking about food items
competency: Students will be able to ask and write about what their friends have in their tiffin box.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students pair up and practice asking and answering questions about food items in their tiffin boxes. Use flashcards with pictures of different food items for students to refer to.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to draw their favorite snack item and display it in the class.
teaching_strategy: Guided practice: Provide students with drawing materials and guide them in drawing their favorite snack. Encourage them to label their drawings and share with the class. Display the drawings on a bulletin board or wall for a class snack time activity.

subject: English
competency: Identify and describe the roles of different occupations through listening and writing activities.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of doctors, farmers, teachers, actors, and singers. Have students match the words with the correct occupations. Conduct a role-playing activity where students act out the roles of these occupations.

subject: English
competency: Enhance listening skills and comprehension through dialogue-based activities.
teaching_strategy: Play a listening game where students listen to short dialogues and answer questions about what they hear. Use the provided dialogue between Barsha and Rohit as an example. Encourage students to practice similar dialogues in pairs.

subject: English
topic: Describing People and Actions in a Setting
competency: Identify and describe the roles of people in a given scenario and their actions.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity: Divide students into groups and assign roles (teachers, students, dentist). Have them act out the scene described in the text. Encourage them to use descriptive language to explain what each character is doing.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and use verbs in context to describe actions.
teaching_strategy: Phonics game: Create flashcards with verbs (sitting, walking, standing, talking, checking, giving, behaving, waiting). Have students match the verbs with their correct actions in the text. Reinforce the use of these verbs in sentences.

subject: English
competency: Describe daily activities after school
teaching_strategy: Role-playing different activities such as doing homework, playing outside, and watching cartoons. Have students act out scenes of Vijaya's routine.

subject: English
competency: Understand the importance of completing homework
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of homework tasks and have students match them to the correct activity. Discuss the importance of finishing homework on time.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use verbs in questions and statements
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out the scenarios given by the teacher, such as playing cricket, singing, dancing, and speaking Maithili. This helps them understand the context and usage of the verbs.

subject: English
competency: Read and comprehend simple sentences
teaching_strategy: Guided practice: Read the sentences aloud as a class and ask students to identify the subject and verb in each sentence. Use flashcards with the sentences for quick review.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand the concept of friendship and the importance of helping each other.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out the scenario where Riyana and Aryan help each other with homework. This can be done in pairs or small groups.

subject: English
competency: Students will recognize and compare numbers of homework problems.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Provide students with a set of problems where they must compare the number of items. For example, 'Riyana has 8 apples, Aryan has 5 apples. Who has more apples?' Use flashcards with numbers to help them practice.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand the value of peer assistance and cooperation in completing tasks.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out scenarios where they help each other with homework. This can be done in pairs or small groups.

subject: English
competency: Students will recognize the importance of doing homework and identify sources of help.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Provide students with simple math problems and ask them to work in pairs to solve them. Encourage them to explain their thought processes and solutions to each other.

subject: English
competency: Describe the features of a school
teaching_strategy: Show students pictures of different schools. Have them discuss and identify the features such as a computer lab and library. Read the provided text aloud and ask students to point out the features mentioned.

subject: English
competency: Relate personal experiences to the lesson
teaching_strategy: Ask students to share about their own school. Use role-playing where students can act as Rohan and describe their school. Create flashcards with pictures of school features and have students match them with the text.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe the location of objects and make sentences using prepositions.
teaching_strategy: Use a physical table and objects like a ball, chairs, and a pencil box. Have students practice placing objects on the table and describing their positions using prepositions like 'under', 'on', and 'in'.

subject: English
competency: Students will construct simple sentences using given words and phrases.
teaching_strategy: Provide flashcards with words and phrases like 'ball', 'chairs', 'pencil box', 'pencils', and 'table'. Have students make sentences orally and in writing. Use the scrambled sentences at the bottom of the page as a guide for creating correct sentences.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to identify locations and directions of landmarks relative to a central point.
teaching_strategy: Use a map or a large poster of Kathmandu to point out the locations of Durbar High School, Bir Hospital, Ghantaghar, Tri-Chandra College, and Jamal Nachghar. Have students practice giving directions from one landmark to another.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to count and understand the concept of storeys and rooms in a building.
teaching_strategy: Create a simple building model with four storeys and forty-five rooms using blocks or cards. Count the storeys and rooms together, and have students fill in the blanks with the correct numbers.

subject: English
competency: Create a simple drawing and write a brief description of a familiar place (school).
teaching_strategy: Have students draw a picture of their school and then guide them to write a short paragraph about it. Use flashcards with key words like 'building', 'playground', 'classroom' to help them describe their school.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to identify and match rhyming words through auditory and visual cues.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with rhyming words on one side and pictures on the other. Have students match the cards by sound and sight.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe objects using simple vocabulary.
teaching_strategy: Engage students in a phonics game where they describe objects using rhyming words. For example, 'This is a hat, it is not far.'

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to ask and answer questions about the location of objects in the classroom.
teaching_strategy: Use a classroom scavenger hunt where students find and name objects in the room, followed by asking and answering questions about their location.

subject: English
competency: Students will construct simple sentences using verbs related to daily activities.
teaching_strategy: Create a role-playing activity where students act out scenarios using the verbs 'spends', 'leaves', 'celebrates', and 'forgets' in sentences about their daily lives.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand and sequence events in a narrative.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out the sequence of events in the story. Divide the class into groups and assign each group a different part of the story to act out. This will help them understand the flow of events and improve their comprehension skills.

subject: English
topic: Recognizing and Using Verbs in Context
competency: Students will recognize and use verbs in context.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Create a game where students match verbs with their actions. For example, 'walk' with a picture of someone walking. This will help them understand the use of verbs in different contexts.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to understand and answer questions based on a short passage.
teaching_strategy: Read the passage aloud to the class and ask students to answer the questions individually. Use a think-pair-share method where students first think about the answers, then discuss with a partner, and finally share their answers with the class.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to understand and complete a simple schedule.
teaching_strategy: Create a similar schedule on the board and fill in the blanks together as a class. Use flashcards with the days of the week and subjects to make the activity more interactive. Have students practice filling in the schedule with different subjects and days.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand and appreciate various activities and fun aspects of school life.
teaching_strategy: Sing and act out the poem to reinforce the fun elements of school. Use flashcards with pictures of school activities (reading, writing, counting, drawing, singing, acting, dancing) for guided practice.

subject: English
competency: Students will recognize and describe their daily school activities.
teaching_strategy: Create a role-playing activity where students act out different school activities. Use a simple questionnaire to ask students what they do at school and encourage them to share with their classmates.

subject: English
competency: Identify and match words with their meanings related to school activities and routines
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of school activities. Have students match the words in Column A with their meanings in Column B through a game.

subject: English
competency: Follow simple instructions
teaching_strategy: Role-play the actions given in the 'Listen and act' section. Use props like a book, pencil, and a pretend door to make the activity more engaging.

subject: English
competency: Understand the school timetable and identify specific periods and subjects.
teaching_strategy: Create a visual timetable using colorful cards or a large poster. Have students match the subject names to the correct time periods. Use role-playing to act out the assembly and different class periods.

subject: English
competency: Recognize the sequence of daily activities and subjects.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of school activities (assembly, classes, breaks) and arrange them in the correct order. Conduct a guided practice where students place the cards in the right sequence and discuss the activities.

subject: English
competency: Students will practice breaking words into sounds and listening to the teacher.
teaching_strategy: Phonics games where students listen to the teacher and break words into sounds. Use flashcards with words like 'box', 'lab', 'crop', 'job', and 'read'.

subject: English
competency: Students will match locations with their directions.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students match locations like 'Rani Pokhari' with their directions 'north', 'Bir Hospital' with 'east', 'Tri-Chandra College' with 'south', and 'Jamal Naach Ghar' with 'opposite'. Use flashcards for visual reinforcement.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to read and complete sentences based on a given context.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of prizes, friends, popcorn, and parents. Have students match the words to the correct blanks in the sentences.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe a picture in five sentences.
teaching_strategy: Show the picture to the students and guide them to observe the details. Encourage them to use descriptive words and phrases. Provide examples of descriptive sentences to inspire their writing.

subject: English
topic: Identifying and Describing Rooms in a House
competency: Students will be able to identify and describe the main rooms in a house (living room, bedroom, kitchen, dining room, bathroom) and discuss their cleanliness and tidiness.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of different rooms to help students recognize and name them. Engage students in a role-playing activity where they describe their own house to classmates, focusing on the cleanliness and tidiness of each room.

subject: English
topic: Daily routines and rooms in the house
competency: Identify common rooms and their uses
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with room pictures and have students match them to the correct sentences. Engage students in a role-play activity where they act out different daily activities in various rooms of the house.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and describe common actions and objects
teaching_strategy: Create a set of action and object flashcards. Use the flashcards to have students identify and describe the actions and objects in the given sentences and pictures. Encourage students to create their own sentences using the flashcards.

subject: English
competency: Ask and answer questions about actions and activities
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out the actions described (writing, drawing, cycling, sitting) and practice asking and answering questions about each action.

subject: English
competency: Describe the features of a house
teaching_strategy: Guided practice: Provide students with pictures of different houses and have them describe the features, such as the number of rooms, materials used, and layout.

subject: English
competency: Identify and describe objects in a room
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of the objects mentioned (window, pillow, blanket, clock, book rack, chair, table, cupboard) and have students match them to the descriptions in the text. Play a memory game where students have to recall the objects and their locations.

subject: English
competency: Count and identify quantities of objects
teaching_strategy: Use实物卡片展示房间中的物品，并让学生根据文本内容进行数量匹配。例如，使用三张窗户的卡片，让学生指出文本中提到的窗户数量。进行角色扮演，让学生轮流描述房间中的物品及其数量。

subject: English
competency: Identify and name family members in a given context
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out scenes where they introduce their family members using the names provided in the text.

subject: English
competency: Design and create a poster using collected images
teaching_strategy: Guided practice: Provide students with a variety of house pictures and guide them in selecting, cutting, and arranging them on chart paper to create a classroom poster.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to identify and name different types of flowers such as rose, marigold, sunflower, lotus, and rhododendron.
teaching_strategy: Phonics games where students match the names of flowers with their pictures.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to express their favorite flower and justify their choice.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activities where students discuss their favorite flowers with classmates.

subject: English
competency: Identify and use plural forms of nouns
teaching_strategy: Flashcards: Create flashcards with singular and plural forms of nouns (rose/roses, fan/fans, radio/radios). Use these flashcards for a matching game where students match singular and plural forms.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use countable nouns in sentences
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Act out scenarios where students use countable nouns in sentences. For example, 'Ramesh has five coins in his pocket' or 'Rojina has one apple.' Encourage students to create their own sentences using the provided examples.

subject: English
competency: Identify and describe characters and their locations in a story
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out the scene where Ruby and Mr. Thapa are in the garden. Assign roles and encourage students to describe the characters and their locations.

subject: English
topic: Understanding and describing actions and interactions
competency: Understand and describe actions and interactions between characters
teaching_strategy: Guided practice: Provide students with a set of cards with different actions and interactions (e.g., planting, giving flowers, talking). Have them match the actions to the characters and discuss their roles in the story.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe feelings and actions of characters in a story.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out the scene where Mr. Thapa is in the garden and Ruby gives him something. Encourage them to use descriptive language to express Mr. Thapa's feelings.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand the basics of gardening and plant care.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Discuss why making holes in the soil is important for planting seeds. Have students practice making small holes in soil samples provided in class.

subject: English
competency: Students will engage in a rhythmic and rhyming song to understand the concept of nature through personification.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Use the song to practice phonetic sounds and rhythm. Have students clap along to the rhythm and identify rhyming words.

subject: English
competency: Students will learn to personify natural elements and understand their characteristics.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to observe and describe objects and scenes using appropriate vocabulary and sentence structures.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand and use prepositions in context.
teaching_strategy: Create a simple game where students place small figures or objects in different locations around a classroom map (river, forest, mountain, houses, temple, park). Ask them to describe the location using prepositions such as 'next to', 'near', 'in front of', etc.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to identify and write dates in a letter.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Date Detective. Provide students with a set of cards with different dates. Have them match the dates to the correct month and day. Then, have them write the dates in their notebooks.

subject: English
topic: Recognizing and Writing Names and Addresses
competency: Students will be able to recognize and write names and addresses in a letter.
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Letter Writing. Have students practice writing and sending letters to each other. Provide them with sample letters and have them identify and write down the names and addresses.

subject: English
competency: Students will learn to write a simple letter to a friend, including basic elements such as greeting, introduction, and a request for information.
teaching_strategy: Have students create their own letters to a friend, using the provided structure as a guide. Encourage them to fill in the blanks with their own names and village details. Use role-playing to practice writing and reading letters aloud.

subject: English
competency: Students will practice describing their village, enhancing their descriptive language skills.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of different village elements (houses, fields, animals, etc.) to help students describe their village. Guide them to use descriptive words and phrases in their writing.

subject: English

subject: English
competency: Students will practice observing the weather outside and discussing it with peers.

subject: English

teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of different weather conditions (sunny, rainy, cold, hot) and have students match them to the correct place (Kathmandu, Lukla, Chitwan, Biratnagar, Pokhara, Jomsom).

subject: English

subject: English
competency: Rewrite simple sentences using given vocabulary.

subject: English
competency: Discuss and distribute fruits and vegetables among family members
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students act as Bunny and distribute different fruits and vegetables to their family members (sister, father, mother). Use real or toy fruits and vegetables for practical engagement.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to list five vegetables and use them in sentences.
teaching_strategy: Provide flashcards with pictures of vegetables. Have students create sentences using the vegetables listed on the page. For example, 'I like to eat potatoes.'

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to compare prices of vegetables and fruits.
teaching_strategy: Use real or mock price tags for vegetables and fruits. Conduct a role-playing activity where students ask and answer questions about prices, such as 'How much is a kilogram of apples?' and 'What is the price of bananas per dozen?'

subject: English
competency: Understand how seeds travel to different places and the importance of this process in plant distribution.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of different fruits and their seeds. Play a game where students match the fruit to its seed type (e.g., one big seed, many small seeds, seeds on the outside). Discuss the role of animals and wind in seed dispersal.

subject: English
competency: Recognize that fruits protect seeds during their journey and understand the variety of seeds found in different fruits.
teaching_strategy: Create a fruit basket with various fruits and have students identify the seeds inside. Use this activity to explain the concept of a fruit as a protective carrier for seeds. Engage students in a guided practice where they draw and label different fruits and their seed types.

subject: English
competency: Identify fruits with many smaller seeds and understand the concept of fruits as seed carriers
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of various fruits. Discuss the seeds in each fruit. Play a 'fruit seed race' game where students identify fruits with many smaller seeds.

subject: English
competency: Express personal preferences and write simple sentences about fruits
teaching_strategy: Conduct a 'fruit tasting' activity where students sample different fruits. Have them write sentences about their favorite fruit, such as 'I like apples because they are sweet and crunchy.'

subject: English
competency: Students will practice listening and following instructions by pointing to the correct object in a picture and repeating a song.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Use the song to practice phonetic sounds related to vegetables. For example, 'c' in carrot, 'b' in broccoli.

subject: English
competency: Students will engage in pair work by asking and answering questions based on a picture.
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Assign roles such as a chef and a customer to practice asking for and naming vegetables.

subject: English
competency: Identify and name common vegetables and fruits.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of vegetables and fruits. Play a matching game where students match the names with the pictures.

subject: English
competency: Understand and answer questions based on a short letter.
teaching_strategy: Read the letter aloud and ask students to answer the questions individually or in pairs. Discuss the answers as a class.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to identify and express personal preferences through simple activities and songs.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of activities like riding a bike, watching TV, drawing, dancing, climbing a tree, speaking English, reading a book, and swimming. Engage students in a game where they match the activity to the corresponding picture. Sing a song about likes and dislikes to reinforce the concepts.

subject: English
competency: Students will practice listening to teacher instructions and writing correct words.
teaching_strategy: Provide flashcards with images and words (bike, TV, picture, tree, book, English) and have students match and write the correct words.

subject: English
competency: Students will engage in a dialogue to practice speaking and understanding simple questions and responses.
teaching_strategy: Role-play the conversation between Neena and Pemba. Have students ask and answer questions about free time activities.

subject: English
competency: Identify and describe personal preferences for indoor and outdoor activities.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out different activities such as reading, watching TV, swimming, cycling, and camping. Encourage them to share their favorite activities and why they like them.

subject: English
competency: Complete and interpret a simple table based on given information.
teaching_strategy: Guided practice: Provide students with a similar table and ask them to fill in the information for themselves or their classmates. Use flashcards with names, ages, and hobbies to make the activity more interactive.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to write about their free-time activities and those of family members and friends.
teaching_strategy: Have students brainstorm and discuss their free-time activities. Use a phonics game where students match activities with corresponding sounds. Create flashcards with activities and have students role-play different family members doing these activities.

subject: English
competency: Match activities with their descriptions and practice pronunciation through repetition
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of the activities (have a picnic, write a postcard, take photos, pack a bag, go camping, play volleyball) and have students match them with their descriptions. Conduct a phonics game where students listen to phrases and repeat them, reinforcing correct pronunciation.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to identify and discuss their favorite activities and those of their friends.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into pairs and have them ask and answer questions about their favorite activities on holidays. Use flashcards with pictures of activities like reading books, dancing, and drawing to aid in vocabulary acquisition.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand and describe the experiences of a grade 2 student during holidays, focusing on her activities and preferences.
teaching_strategy: Guided practice: Read the passage about Reena and discuss her holiday experiences. Use a map of Nepal to point out the places she visits. Have students create their own holiday plans and share them with the class.

subject: English
competency: Understand family roles and activities
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out scenes where they help their parents in the field. Discuss the importance of family activities and cooperation.

subject: English
competency: Improve reading and writing skills through phonics and word completion
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Use flashcards with words like 'ool', 'pare', 'aces', 'ends', 'differe', and 'ant'. Have students identify the missing letters and read the completed words aloud. Encourage them to use these words in sentences.

subject: English
competency: Engage in simple conversations and express preferences
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out conversations similar to the ones provided, focusing on greetings and making play suggestions.

subject: English
competency: Identify and discuss various games
teaching_strategy: Activity: Create a list of games on the board and have students vote on their favorites. Encourage them to explain why they like certain games.

subject: English
competency: Students will learn to follow sequential instructions and understand the concept of 'out' in a game context.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing the game 'Musical Bumps' with students. Have them practice the sequence of actions: dancing to music, stopping when the music stops, and quickly sitting down. Use a timer or a sound to simulate the music and make it more engaging.

subject: English
competency: Students will identify and use verbs related to actions in a game context.
teaching_strategy: Create flashcards with verbs like 'dance', 'sit', 'stand', and 'stop'. Use these flashcards in a game where students have to perform the action when the corresponding verb is shown. This will help them associate the verbs with the actions and improve their understanding of the game.

subject: English
competency: Understand and participate in a game involving standing and dancing to music until one child remains.
teaching_strategy: Organize a 'Musical Bumps' game in the classroom. Play some music and have the children dance. When the music stops, the children must sit down. The last child standing is the winner. This activity can be used to practice listening skills and following instructions.

subject: English
competency: Draw and write about a favorite game.
teaching_strategy: Ask students to draw their favorite game and write a short paragraph about it. Provide them with drawing materials and encourage them to use their creativity. Afterward, have a sharing session where students can present their drawings and paragraphs to the class.

subject: English
competency: Students will practice listening comprehension and writing by writing words under pictures.
teaching_strategy: Phonics games where students match sounds to pictures and write the corresponding words.

subject: English
competency: Students will engage in pair work to practice asking and answering questions about likes and dislikes.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students practice asking and answering questions about their preferences.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe animals and birds based on their characteristics such as color, diet, products, and habitat.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of various animals and birds. Have students describe the animals using the provided prompts. For example, 'The bird is blue and it eats seeds. It gives us eggs. It lives in the tree.' Encourage students to share their descriptions of animals they have at home.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and produce animal sounds through listening and singing
teaching_strategy: Phonics games where students match animal sounds to their pictures or names

subject: English
competency: Discuss basic concepts of animal communication through role-playing
teaching_strategy: Role-playing scenarios where students act as animals communicating with each other

subject: English
competency: Identify and imitate animal sounds
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Have students form groups and assign each group an animal. Each group will make the sound of their assigned animal and the class will guess which animal it is.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to understand and retell a story involving multiple characters and their dialogue.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing the characters in the story can help students understand and remember the dialogue and actions. Divide the class into groups and assign each group a character. Have them act out the scene where the characters meet and ask questions about their dialogue and actions.

subject: English
competency: Students will expand their vocabulary by learning new words and their usage in context.
teaching_strategy: Create flashcards with the new words from the story such as 'sky', 'lion', 'duck', 'fox'. Use these flashcards in a game where students have to match the word with its picture or use it in a sentence. This will help them understand the meaning and usage of the words.

subject: English
competency: Identify characters and settings in a story
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out the scene where Chicken Little meets Foxy Loxy. Use props like a cardboard lion's den to enhance the role-play.

subject: English
competency: Understand the outcome of a story
teaching_strategy: Discussion: Ask students why the characters never came out of the lion's den. Use flashcards with pictures of the characters to help them recall the story.

subject: English
competency: Students will identify the products and services provided by cows, buffaloes, and chickens.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of cows, buffaloes, and chickens. Have students match the animals with their respective products or services (e.g., milk, meat, eggs).

subject: English
competency: Students will describe the roles of dogs in human life.
teaching_strategy: Role-play scenarios where dogs assist humans (e.g., guarding the house, guiding the blind). Discuss the importance of dogs in these roles.

subject: English
competency: Identify common pets and their functions
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Students can act out conversations between friends discussing their pets. Use flashcards with pictures of different pets to enhance vocabulary.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use simple sentences to describe objects and actions
teaching_strategy: Phonics game: Create a matching game where students match objects (dogs, sheep, horses) with their functions (protect, give, carry).

subject: English
competency: Describe how the mouse's actions helped the lion
teaching_strategy: Role-playing

subject: English
competency: Identify the characters and their roles in the story
teaching_strategy: Character cards

subject: English
competency: Students will identify and name animals and birds based on given characteristics.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of animals and birds. Engage students in a game where they have to identify the animals and birds based on the given characteristics (horns, legs, teeth, wings, jungle habitat, shell, swimming, flying).

subject: English
competency: Engage in conversations about animal features
teaching_strategy: Role-playing

subject: English
competency: Participate in singing and responding to questions
teaching_strategy: Singing and action games

subject: English
competency: Identify different types of animal homes and their functions
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out different animals and their homes. For example, students can pretend to be birds building nests, rabbits digging burrows, or squirrels finding tree hollows.

subject: English
competency: Understand and answer questions based on a passage
teaching_strategy: Guided practice: Provide students with a passage about animals and their homes. Ask them to identify the type of home each animal builds and its purpose. Use flashcards with images of animals and their homes for reinforcement.

subject: English
competency: Identify different types of shelters and habitats for animals
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of various animals and their habitats. For example, show a picture of a turtle and its shell, a bird and its nest, and a spider and its web. Have students match the animals to their homes using the flashcards.

subject: English
competency: Understand the concept of domestic animals and the shelters provided by humans
teaching_strategy: Role-play different scenarios where students act as farmers and build shelters for animals like cows, buffaloes, and horses. Use construction toys or blocks to create simple structures and discuss why these are suitable for the animals.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to draw pictures of birds and animals and write about their abilities.
teaching_strategy: Provide students with drawing materials and ask them to draw pictures of birds and animals. After drawing, have them write or dictate sentences about what the animals can do. For example, 'The bird can fly high in the sky.'

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to combine two words to form new words.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with the given pairs of words (back + bird, cat + fish, etc.). Have students work in pairs to create new words and write them down. You can also play a word-building game where students take turns adding a word to a sentence using the new word they created.

subject: English
competency: Engage in conversations about food consumption among animals and humans
teaching_strategy: Use picture cards of various animals and ask students to match them with their typical food sources. Encourage students to share their own dietary habits by creating a class chart.

subject: English
competency: Understand and describe the actions of a cat and a bird
teaching_strategy: Role-playing the actions of a cat and a bird using props or body movements

subject: English
competency: Recognize and use comparative adjectives
teaching_strategy: Flashcards with pictures of different sizes of animals or objects to practice comparative adjectives

subject: English
competency: Students will understand the importance of critical thinking and problem-solving in finding solutions to everyday problems.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide the class into groups and assign each group a different problem (e.g., how to keep a pet safe, how to reduce waste). Have them brainstorm solutions and present their ideas to the class.

subject: English
competency: Students will improve their reading comprehension skills by identifying key details and answering questions based on the text.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Read the story aloud and ask students to identify the main characters and the problem. Then, provide them with the questions and guide them through the process of finding the answers in the text.

subject: English
competency: Describe past actions and events using appropriate verbs
teaching_strategy: Role-playing

subject: English
competency: Construct simple sentences
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice with Sentence Building

subject: English
competency: Develop listening skills and answer questions based on audio content
teaching_strategy: Use phonics games to improve listening skills. Play the audio and have students repeat the questions and answers.

subject: English
competency: Practice conversational skills and ask and answer questions about animals
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students take turns asking and answering questions about the given animals. Use flashcards with pictures of the animals for visual support.

subject: English
competency: Understand the moral of the story and relate it to real-life situations.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out the story in pairs, emphasizing the lion's initial disbelief and the mouse's unexpected help. Discuss the moral: 'Even the smallest can help the biggest.'

subject: English
competency: Complete sentences based on context and improve reading comprehension.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Provide students with similar sentences and ask them to fill in the blanks. Use flashcards with missing words for a fun, interactive activity.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and pronounce words with 'sh' and 's' sounds
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Create a phonics scavenger hunt where students find and match words with 'sh' and 's' sounds. Use flashcards and have students sort them into groups.

subject: English
competency: Build sentences using given words
teaching_strategy: Sentence Building Activity: Provide students with a set of words from the page and ask them to create sentences. For example, 'I wear my shoes to shop.' or 'The singer sings sunny songs.'

subject: English
competency: Identify and match numbers with descriptions of jobs
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of different professions and their descriptions. Have students match the correct number to each profession and say the name of the profession aloud.

subject: English
competency: Describe weather conditions in different months and regions of Nepal
teaching_strategy: Create a weather calendar where students can record daily weather conditions. Use flashcards with images of different weather patterns (sunny, cloudy, rainy, snowy) and have students match the correct card to the day's weather. Discuss the impact of weather on daily activities and plant growth.

subject: English
competency: Identify differences in climate between the mountains, hills, and Terai regions
teaching_strategy: Role-play different scenarios where students act out daily activities in various regions (e.g., playing in the snow in the mountains, planting rice in the Terai). Use a map of Nepal to point out the different regions and discuss the climate differences.

subject: English
competency: Identify and name family members
teaching_strategy: Flashcards with pictures of family members (grandfather, grandmother, mother, father, brother, sister) can be used to help students recognize and name these roles. Students can also create their own flashcards and play a matching game.

subject: English
competency: Understand and express feelings of love within the family
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activities where students can act out scenes of family members showing love and care for each other. This can include scenarios like hugging, giving a kiss, or sharing a meal together.

subject: English
competency: Students will practice using adjectives to describe people and objects.
teaching_strategy: Pair Discussion and Sentence Construction

subject: English
competency: Students will learn to arrange words in alphabetical order.
teaching_strategy: Sorting Game

subject: English
competency: Identify family members and their relationships (parents, siblings, aunts, uncles).
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out scenes introducing their own family members and their relationships to each other.

subject: English
competency: Describe physical characteristics and personality traits of individuals.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Create a phonics game where students match descriptions of physical traits (e.g., blonde hair, tall) with pictures or names of family members.

subject: English
competency: Determine the names and relationships of characters in a given context.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Assign students different roles (Ana, Laura, Ana's father, Tim, Ana's aunt, Richard, William, and Pirate) and have them introduce themselves to the class. This activity helps students understand and remember the names and relationships.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and describe the age and characteristics of characters.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Create flashcards with different ages and descriptions (e.g.,

subject: English
competency: Identify ownership and pets in a given scenario.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Provide students with pictures of different pets and their owners. Have them match the pets to the correct owners and discuss why certain pets belong to specific individuals.

subject: English
competency: Identify and match pairs of opposites
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pairs of opposites. Have students match the cards and discuss the meanings.

subject: English
competency: Describe family members in a paragraph
teaching_strategy: Engage students in a role-playing activity where they describe their family members using the words from the opposites list. Provide examples and guide them to write a short paragraph.

subject: English
competency: Match countries with their respective nationalities through dialogue and a matching activity
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with country and nationality names. Have students match the correct pairs. Engage in a role-play activity where students introduce themselves and their nationalities, similar to the dialogue between Mike and Sima.

subject: English
competency: Students will practice forming complete sentences using correct words and phrases related to nationality.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Use flashcards with different nationalities and have students match them with the correct adjectives (e.g., Russian, German, Chinese, Indian, Japanese).

subject: English
competency: Students will learn to introduce themselves and share personal information such as age and nationality.
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Divide the class into pairs and have them practice the dialogue between Mano and Kane. Encourage students to create their own dialogues using the provided structure.

subject: English
competency: Students will identify and compare cultural and geographical information about different countries.
teaching_strategy: Create a world map on the board and have students place flags or stickers representing the countries mentioned (Nepal, Italy, Japan, Colombia). Discuss the capital cities and popular sports of each country using the information provided.

subject: English
competency: Students will describe themselves and their origins using simple sentences.
teaching_strategy: Use role-playing activities where students introduce themselves, stating their name, language, and country of origin. For example, have students pair up and take turns introducing each other using the information from the text.

subject: English
competency: Identify cultural practices and languages of different countries
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of countries and their flags to help students associate languages and popular foods. Engage students in a role-playing activity where they introduce themselves as characters from different countries.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and use short forms of pronouns
teaching_strategy: Create a phonics game where students match full pronoun sentences with their short form equivalents. Use guided practice to ensure students understand the concept.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to change positive sentences into negative sentences.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Use a 'not' card game where students draw a card with a positive sentence and then add 'isn't' or 'is not' to form the negative sentence. For example, 'He is a good player' becomes 'He isn't a good player'.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to answer yes/no questions with short answers.
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Have students practice answering yes/no questions by role-playing different scenarios. For example, one student can ask 'Are you American?' and another can respond 'Yes, I am.' or 'No, I'm not.'

subject: English
competency: Students will practice introducing themselves, asking for age, and discussing birthdays.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing different characters from the dialogue to practice conversations.

subject: English
topic: Understanding and using names and places
competency: Students will learn to use names and discuss places of origin.
teaching_strategy: Create flashcards with names and places, and have students match them or use them in sentences.

subject: English
competency: Practice asking and answering questions about personal details such as name, origin, age, birthday, and best friend using simple sentences.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students pair up and practice asking and answering the provided questions. Use flashcards with names, countries, ages, and birthdays for additional practice.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use vocabulary related to household chores and family life, and complete sentences with appropriate words.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of household items and chores. Have students match the words 'big, garbage, wash, farm, make, sweep, small' with the correct actions or objects in the sentences. Role-play scenarios where students act out different chores and family interactions described in the text.

subject: English
competency: Describe family members and their roles in the household, and compare different family sizes and living situations.
teaching_strategy: Create a 'Family Tree' activity where students draw and label their family members. Compare and contrast the family structures of Nimesh and Gita using a Venn diagram. Discuss the chores each family member performs and how they contribute to the household.

subject: English
competency: Understand family roles and responsibilities
teaching_strategy: Role-playing and discussion

subject: English
competency: Recognize daily activities and community interactions
teaching_strategy: Story-telling and group activities

subject: English
competency: Identify and use correct verb forms in sentences
teaching_strategy: Create a verb matching game where students match verbs with their correct forms. Use flashcards with sentences like 'We go to the cinema every Friday' and 'My brother plays Karate three days a week'. Have students act out the verbs to reinforce their understanding.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use personal pronouns correctly
teaching_strategy: Engage students in a role-playing activity where they introduce themselves and their friends using personal pronouns. For example, 'I go to the cinema every Friday' and 'She loves her students'. Use a mirror activity where students look at themselves and say 'I have a bakery' or 'He washes his socks every day'.

subject: English
competency: Develop communication skills by discussing visual content
teaching_strategy: Phonics games where students describe actions using target vocabulary such as 'giving', 'talking', 'holding'. Use flashcards with action words for reinforcement.

subject: English
competency: Express personal feelings and experiences related to family
teaching_strategy: Role-playing scenarios where students share their experiences of giving gifts to their mothers, followed by a class discussion.

subject: English
competency: Understand and describe the roles of family members in a household setting.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students act out different family members performing tasks such as cooking, cleaning, and giving gifts.

subject: English
competency: Identify and form words from given letter sets and construct simple sentences.
teaching_strategy: Phonics game where students unscramble letters to form words and then use those words to create sentences. For example, using 'kchtine' to form 'kitchen' and then constructing a sentence like 'Jenni will wash and cook the rice and vegetables in the kitchen.'

subject: English
competency: Identify and use appropriate verbs in context
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out the actions described in the sentences (e.g., cutting fish, preparing lunch, giving gifts).

subject: English
competency: Recognize family members and understand the context of family celebrations
teaching_strategy: Flashcards: Create flashcards with pictures of family members and their names. Use them to practice identifying and discussing family relationships.

subject: English
competency: Identify and write the -ing forms of given verbs
teaching_strategy:
Phonics Game: Verb -ing Forms
Create flashcards with verbs on one side and their -ing forms on the other. Have students match the cards and say the verb and its -ing form aloud.

subject: English
competency: Describe daily activities and write sentences
teaching_strategy:
Role-Playing: Daily Activities
Divide students into pairs. One student acts out an activity, and the other writes a sentence about what is happening. For example, if one student pretends to read a book, the other writes 'She is reading a book.'

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to match names with their potential occupations based on context clues.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Assign each student a name from the list and have them act out a brief scenario related to their name (e.g., Mr. Karki could be a teacher, Ms. Shrestha could be a doctor). This will help students understand and remember the names and their possible roles.

subject: English
competency: Students will practice writing names correctly.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Provide each student with a worksheet containing the names from the list. Guide them through writing each name correctly, focusing on proper spelling and handwriting.

subject: English
competency: Students will match job descriptions with the correct job titles.
teaching_strategy: Use a matching game where students match the job titles (e.g., painter, barber, pilot) with the corresponding descriptions (e.g., paints pictures, serves food, cuts hair). This can be done through flashcards or a digital matching game.

subject: English
competency: Students will describe the roles of different jobs.
teaching_strategy: Engage students in a role-playing activity where they act out the roles of different jobs. For example, one student can be the pilot, another the barber, and so on. Encourage them to use descriptive language to explain what each job does.

subject: English
competency: Identify and understand different occupations and the actions associated with them.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing Activity: Assign students different occupations (driver, artist, nurse, pilot, airhostess, waiter) and have them act out the actions described in the sentences. For example, a student playing the role of a driver can pretend to drive a bus, and another student can act as a nurse caring for a patient.

subject: English
competency: Correctly use 'a' and 'an' before singular countable nouns.
teaching_strategy: Flashcard Game: Create flashcards with sentences like 'There is a book on the desk' and 'She's reading an old comic'. Have students match the correct article with the noun. Follow up with a guided practice session where students complete the given sentences.

subject: English
topic: Daily routine and work of a farmer
competency: Describe the daily activities and work conditions of a farmer.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students act out the daily routine of Ram Karki and his family. Use flashcards with key phrases and times to reinforce vocabulary and sequence of events.

subject: English
competency: Understand the importance of teamwork and family cooperation in daily tasks.
teaching_strategy: Group activity where students discuss and role-play different family roles and responsibilities. Use a family tree chart to visualize the relationships and tasks.

subject: English
competency: Compare and contrast given sentences using affirmative and negative forms
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with affirmative and negative sentences to practice identifying and contrasting information. Have students create their own flashcards and play a memory game where they match the correct affirmative and negative forms.

subject: English
topic: Understanding Daily Routine and Work Habits
competency: Describe the daily routine and work habits of characters in a story
teaching_strategy: Role-play the daily activities of Ram Karki and his family. Students can act out the scenes where they work, take a rest, and have meals. This helps in understanding and internalizing the context of the story.

subject: English
competency: Change given sentences into negative forms using appropriate auxiliary verbs.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Use a 'Yes or No' phonics game where students form negative sentences by adding 'doesn't', 'don't', or 'aren't' to the given sentences. For example, 'She makes all her money by herself.' becomes 'She doesn't make all her money by herself.'

subject: English
competency: Create a job chart for family members
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Have students role-play different family members and assign them jobs. Use flashcards with pictures of family members and jobs to help students match and discuss their roles. For example, 'Mother' could be assigned the job of 'cooking' or 'cleaning'.

subject: English
competency: Develop phonemic awareness and listening skills through rhyming words and sentence completion.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with rhyming words for a phonics game. For sentence completion, play a role-playing activity where students act out the sentences with props or drawings.

subject: English
competency: Understand family dynamics and daily routines through discussion and listening.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a role-play activity where students take turns talking about their family members and their work. Use pictures or drawings to help students visualize and describe their families.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use descriptive words to describe family members
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of family members and their descriptions. Have students match the words 'blonde', 'slim', and 'funny' with the appropriate descriptions of the characters in the text. Conduct a role-playing activity where students describe each other using these words.

subject: English
competency: Identify family members and their relationships
teaching_strategy: Create a family tree chart on the board. Have students identify and label the family members mentioned in the text. Discuss the relationships between the characters, such as 'Ana's brother', 'Ana's baby brother', and 'Ana's self'. Use a guided practice where students create their own family tree using their own family members.

subject: English
competency: Recite and understand a daily routine sequence through song and rhyme
teaching_strategy: Phonics games where students match actions to sounds in the song.

subject: English
competency: Identify and sequence daily activities
teaching_strategy: Role-playing where students act out the daily routine in groups.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to recognize and read different times and form sentences using given time phrases.
teaching_strategy: Time Flashcards: Create flashcards with different times (half past eight, quarter past ten, quarter to three, five o'clock, 9 o'clock, 3 o'clock) and have students practice reading them aloud. Sentence Formation Game: Divide the class into small groups and give each group a set of time flashcards. Each group must create sentences using the given times, such as 'It is half past eight.'

subject: English
competency: Ask and answer questions about time; identify the time as 'three o'clock'.
teaching_strategy: Time Telling Game: Create a large clock face on the board and use flashcards with different times. Call out 'What time is it?' and have students hold up the correct time card.

subject: English
competency: Understand and describe a daily routine of a character
teaching_strategy: Role-playing Pari's daily routine. Have students act out different parts of the routine, such as waking up, having breakfast, going to school, and returning home. Use props like a clock to show different times of the day.

subject: English
competency: Identify and sequence daily activities
teaching_strategy: Create a timeline or a sequence card game where students match activities with their corresponding times. For example, match

subject: English
competency: Recognize and describe family activities
teaching_strategy: Discuss and role-play family activities such as having dinner, listening to music, and watching TV. Use flashcards with pictures of family members doing these activities to reinforce learning.

subject: English
competency: Describe daily activities and routines
teaching_strategy: Role-playing daily activities. Have students act out the daily routine of Pari and then write or describe their own routines.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use time-related vocabulary
teaching_strategy: Use a clock or timer to demonstrate and practice telling time. Have students calculate how long they spend on various activities.

subject: English
competency: Describe and express relationships with friends
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Students can act out scenarios where they are with their best friends, discussing activities they share.

subject: English
competency: Identify and use common verbs and nouns in context
teaching_strategy: Phonics games: Use flashcards with words like 'share', 'play', 'go', and 'together' and have students match them with pictures or use them in sentences.

subject: English
competency: Describe daily activities and routines
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out their daily routines, such as getting up, playing with friends, and leaving for school. Use flashcards with pictures of common activities to reinforce vocabulary.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use social interactions and behaviors
teaching_strategy: Group Activity: Organize students into pairs or small groups to practice asking and answering questions about daily routines. Use sentence starters like 'When do you...?' and 'I... at...'.

subject: English
competency: Identify and discuss daily activities and routines of oneself and peers
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Students can act out their daily routines, including when they take snacks, go to bed, and reach home. This can be extended to include their best friends' routines.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and describe characteristics of a best friend
teaching_strategy: Guided discussion: Ask students to identify the qualities of Alia's best friend Hana and discuss why these qualities make Hana a good friend. Use flashcards with pictures of friends engaging in different activities to reinforce the concept.

subject: English
competency: Describe daily activities and friendships among peers.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out different scenarios of the activities described (e.g., sharing snacks, walking home together, talking about homework).

subject: English
competency: Identify family activities and leisure time.
teaching_strategy: Flashcards: Create flashcards with activities (e.g., drawing competition, going to the cinema) and have students match them with the correct sentences.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe actions and traits of characters in a story through sentence formation.
