teaching_strategy: Role-playing and Sentence Construction Game: Divide students into pairs. Assign each pair a character (Alia, Hana, their parents) and have them create sentences describing the character's actions or traits based on the given sentences. For example, 'Alia is nine years old' can be expanded to 'Alia is nine years old and she has many friends.'

subject: English
competency: Students will practice forming sentences using given words and phrases.
teaching_strategy: Sentence Building Blocks: Provide students with cards containing words and phrases like 'is', 'am', 'are', 'has', 'have', and 'fifty rupees'. Have them construct sentences using these blocks. For example, 'I am a good boy' and 'They have many toys'.

subject: English
competency: Write a short paragraph about a best friend
teaching_strategy: Have students share their best friends and discuss qualities of a good friend. Guide them to write a paragraph focusing on these qualities.

subject: English
competency: Understand and represent different times of the day
teaching_strategy: Use the clock model to teach time. Have students rotate the clock hands to different times and describe activities typically done at those times.

subject: English
competency: Identify and describe common breakfast items
teaching_strategy: Show students pictures of different breakfast foods. Have them match the foods to the sentences on the page. Conduct a role-playing activity where students pretend to order breakfast at a restaurant, using the vocabulary learned.

subject: English
competency: Express personal preferences and engage in simple conversations
teaching_strategy: Ask students to bring in their favorite breakfast items to class. Have them describe their breakfast to the class using the vocabulary from the lesson. Use flashcards with breakfast items for a memory game where students have to find a match for the item they brought.

subject: English
competency: Engage in simple conversations using polite expressions and apologies
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students pair up and practice the dialogue between Bijaya and the teacher. Encourage them to use different scenarios and add their own context to the conversation.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and use common food items in English
teaching_strategy: Flashcards: Create flashcards with pictures and names of food items. Use the flashcards for a memory game where students have to match the food items with their names. Alternatively, use the flashcards for a quick quiz where students have to name the food items as quickly as possible.

subject: English
competency: Construct sentences using provided vocabulary
teaching_strategy: Sentence Building Game

subject: English
competency: Describe daily activities
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing Daily Activities

subject: English
competency: Describe daily routines and preferences related to breakfast, including personal likes and dislikes.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out Rupesh's morning routine. Use props like a toy comb, a pretend plate of porridge, and a glass of milk. Encourage students to share their own breakfast preferences and routines.

subject: English
competency: Understand the consequences of actions and their impact on others.
teaching_strategy: Discussion: Ask students to discuss the consequences of Rupesh's actions (throwing the porridge out of the window) and how it affected the woman. Use flashcards with pictures of different actions and their outcomes to reinforce the concept.

subject: English
competency: Change verbs from present to past tense
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with present and past tense verbs. Have students match the present tense verbs with their past tense counterparts and then apply this knowledge to rewrite sentences.

subject: English
competency: Identify and use verbs in the present simple tense in sentences and questions.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with verbs in the present simple tense for a quick recognition game. Have students create their own sentences using the verbs provided (e.g., throw, take, understand, feel, run) in the present simple tense.

subject: English
competency: Construct simple paragraphs using personal experiences.
teaching_strategy: Guide students to write about their breakfast habits. Provide examples and encourage them to include descriptive words and personal details.

subject: English
competency: Describe and compare activities done during summer and winter holidays
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into groups and have them act out the activities mentioned in the text. Each group can choose one activity and perform a short skit. This will help students understand and remember the activities better.

subject: English
competency: Engage in creative writing and storytelling
teaching_strategy: Guided practice: Provide students with a scenario related to the holidays, such as visiting a zoo or making crafts. Ask them to write a short story or poem about their experience. Use flashcards with holiday-related words to help them expand their vocabulary.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand and use future tense in sentences.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of Rara, Bandipur, and Lake to help students associate these places with the future tense verbs 'will visit'. Conduct a role-playing activity where students practice saying 'I will visit Rara' and 'I will visit Bandipur'.

subject: English
competency: Students will engage in simple telephone conversations.
teaching_strategy: Create pairs of students and provide them with the dialogue script. Have them practice the dialogue, focusing on correct pronunciation and intonation. Encourage them to add their own names and modify the dialogue to make it more personal.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use vocabulary related to planting and weather
teaching_strategy: Flashcards: Create flashcards with words on one side and their meanings on the other. Use the flashcards for a matching game where students match the words with their meanings.

subject: English
competency: Apply vocabulary in context
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Assign roles to students and have them use the words in sentences. For example, one student can be Amar, another can be a farmer, and another can be a dancer. Encourage them to use the words 'observe', 'attractive', 'experience', 'monsoon', 'plant', and 'amazing' in their sentences.

subject: English
competency: Describe summer holiday experiences and activities
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Students can act out different scenarios of summer holidays, such as visiting friends, staying at maternal uncle's home, and going on trips. This helps in understanding and practicing the use of first and second person pronouns.

subject: English
competency: Identify seasonal activities and cultural practices during summer
teaching_strategy: Flashcards: Create flashcards with images and words related to summer activities and cultural practices. Use these cards for a memory game or a quick quiz to reinforce learning.

subject: English
competency: Use context clues and vocabulary to complete sentences
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with context clues to help students fill in the blanks. Provide sentences related to summer activities and local culture to enhance understanding.

subject: English
competency: Arrange words in alphabetical order
teaching_strategy: Create a game where students sort words into alphabetical order using flashcards. Include a variety of words to practice sorting.

subject: English
competency: Create sentences using future tense
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with sentences in future tense. Have students create their own sentences using the provided examples and additional words like 'buy', 'visit', 'do', 'return'.

subject: English
competency: Describe activities during holidays
teaching_strategy: Role-play different holiday scenarios. Students can act out activities like playing with friends, going to the market, or visiting relatives. Encourage them to list and discuss their own holiday activities.

subject: English
competency: Recite and understand the sequence of days in a week
teaching_strategy: Sing a song or chant to memorize the days of the week. Use flashcards with pictures of each day to reinforce learning.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and discuss daily routines such as brushing teeth and washing face
teaching_strategy: Role-play different daily activities. Create a chart where students can mark their daily routines and discuss them in class.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe their weekend activities and use simple past tense verbs.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out the scenarios given, such as waking up early, visiting a park, or going to a restaurant. This will help them understand and use the past tense verbs correctly.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe a recent trip and use appropriate vocabulary related to travel.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Provide students with flashcards of travel-related vocabulary (e.g., airport, hotel, train, etc.). Use these cards to create sentences about a trip to Kathmandu or any other place of interest.

subject: English
competency: Understand word meanings and usage
teaching_strategy: Flashcard game: Create flashcards with words on one side and their meanings on the other. Have students match the words with their meanings.

subject: English
competency: Apply word usage in context
teaching_strategy: Sentence construction: Provide students with the words and ask them to create sentences. For example, 'Let's gather the toys before we leave.' or 'The curtain shut quickly.'

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe and sequence daily activities using appropriate vocabulary and context.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into groups and assign each group a different activity (skipping, Chor-police, hide and seek, number game). Have them act out the activities as described in the text. This will help them understand the sequence and context of the activities.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to identify and solve problems in a given scenario.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Present the situation where Nisha is hiding and her feet are visible. Ask students to brainstorm and suggest solutions on how to make the game more fair. This will encourage critical thinking and problem-solving skills.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to identify and use correct verb forms in sentences.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Verb Tense Match-Up. Create flashcards with singular verb forms on one set and correct verb forms in sentences on another set. Students match the verb forms to create correct sentences.

subject: English
topic: Fill in the Gaps with Correct Verb Forms
competency: Students will be able to use correct verb forms in context.
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Assign students roles (John, father, etc.) and have them act out the sentences using the correct verb forms. This helps reinforce the use of verbs in context.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe their weekend activities in a paragraph.
teaching_strategy: Ask students to share their weekend activities in small groups. Provide sentence starters like 'Last Saturday, I...' and encourage them to use the past tense. Have students write their paragraphs and then share them with the class.

subject: English
competency: Students will practice completing sentences and writing a paragraph.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with past tense verbs and have students complete sentences like 'Last Saturday, I ___ with friends.' Follow up by having them write a paragraph about their weekend activities using the completed sentences as a guide.

subject: English
competency: Listen to and repeat rhyming words and complete sentences
teaching_strategy: Phonics games and sentence completion exercises

subject: English
competency: Describe daily activities and use vocabulary related to routines and actions
teaching_strategy: Role-playing daily activities, flashcards for vocabulary

subject: English
competency: Develop narrative writing skills by creating stories based on visual cues
teaching_strategy: Use picture cards of different school activities and events. Have students create stories in small groups, encouraging them to include a beginning, middle, and end in their narratives.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use time in the morning context
teaching_strategy: Create a morning routine chart with different activities and times. Use a clock or a digital timer to demonstrate and practice telling time at different intervals during the morning.

subject: English
competency: Students will practice writing the letters a, b, c under correct pictures related to morning activities.
teaching_strategy: Phonics game: Create a matching game where students match pictures of morning activities with the correct initial letters. Use flashcards with pictures and letters for this activity.

subject: English
competency: Students will describe and write about morning routines of their friends.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students role-play different morning routines. They can act out the activities and then write down what their classmates do. This can be done in pairs or small groups.

subject: English
competency: Describe different ways people travel
teaching_strategy: Create a matching game where students match pictures of people traveling with the corresponding mode of transportation. Use flashcards with images and words to reinforce learning.

subject: English
competency: Students will categorize different means of transport into land, water, and air groups.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of various vehicles (cars, boats, planes) and have students sort them into the correct groups. Provide each student with a set of cards and a worksheet to practice categorization.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand and use adverbs of frequency to describe how often they go to school using different means of transport.
teaching_strategy: Engage students in a role-playing activity where they discuss their daily routines. Use a chart with the adverbs 'always', 'usually', 'sometimes', and 'never' and have them fill in sentences about their classmates. For example, 'Kailash usually goes to school by car.'

subject: English
competency: Describe favorite subjects and school activities, and discuss likes and dislikes.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Students can act out scenarios where they are Rupa, discussing their favorite subjects and activities. This can be followed by a group discussion where students share their own experiences.

subject: English
competency: Understand and discuss school rules and the importance of wearing a uniform.
teaching_strategy: Flashcards: Create flashcards with rules and consequences. Use these for a memory game where students match rules to their outcomes. Discuss the importance of following rules and wearing a uniform.

subject: English
topic: Describing Personal Interests and School Activities
competency: Students will describe their personal interests and school activities.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out scenarios where they describe their favorite subjects, games, and activities. For example, they can role-play as Rupa and Harka discussing their interests.

subject: English
competency: Students will identify true and false statements based on given information.
teaching_strategy: True or False Game: Create a game where students read statements and use tick (√) and cross (X) to indicate if the statement is true or false. Use the provided statements as examples.

subject: English
competency: Identify and create rhyming words in a song
teaching_strategy: Have students work in pairs or small groups to find and list the rhyming words in the song 'Round and Round'. Use flashcards with the words from the song to help them identify rhyming pairs.

subject: English
topic: Asking for Permission and Responding Appropriately
competency: Students will practice asking for permission and responding with yes or no in various contexts such as using a computer, going to the library, and cleaning the classroom.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide the class into pairs. One student asks for permission using phrases like 'May I...?' or 'Can I...?', and the other responds with 'Yes, of course.' or 'No, I'm sorry.' Provide scenarios such as using a computer, going to the library, and cleaning the classroom.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to create appropriate questions seeking permission to perform various actions.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Have students create questions using the given clues. For example, 'May I put my paper in the dustbin?' or 'Can I have my breakfast?' Use flashcards with actions written on them to help students form their questions.

subject: English
competency: Identify and write words related to school facilities
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Have students listen to the teacher pronounce each word and then write it below the corresponding picture. Use flashcards to reinforce the pronunciation and spelling of each term.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe their school and its facilities using descriptive language and proper sentence structure.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity: Divide students into pairs. One student will be Reshma, and the other will be Reetu. Reshma will describe her school, and Reetu will ask questions to clarify details. This activity will help students practice descriptive language and improve their comprehension skills.

subject: English
competency: Students will identify and describe various school facilities and activities.
teaching_strategy: Flashcard game: Create flashcards with pictures of different school facilities (playground, library, classrooms, labs, computer room, seminar hall). Show a flashcard and ask students to name the facility and mention an activity that can be done there. This will help students recognize and recall different school facilities and activities.

subject: English
competency: Identify and categorize school facilities
teaching_strategy: Create a matching game where students match the facilities with the correct symbol (tick or cross). Use flashcards with pictures of the facilities for a visual aid.

subject: English
competency: Complete sentences and write a reply letter
teaching_strategy: Guide students to fill in the blanks with appropriate information. Use role-playing to practice writing sentences. Provide examples of sentences to help students understand the structure.

subject: English
competency: Identify and discuss different classes available in a school
teaching_strategy: Show students pictures of each class (social class, English class, mathematics class, etc.). Have students match the pictures to the correct class names. Encourage them to discuss their favorite class and why.

subject: English
competency: Express personal preferences and reasons
teaching_strategy: Engage students in a role-playing activity where they can practice saying 'I like... because...'. Use flashcards with class names and reasons to help them structure their sentences.

subject: English
competency: Listen to and follow classroom instructions and ask for help
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Students can act out the dialogue in pairs or small groups, practicing listening and responding appropriately to classroom announcements and questions.

subject: English
competency: Identify and manage personal items in the classroom
teaching_strategy: Flashcards: Create flashcards with pictures of classroom items and have students identify and discuss their personal belongings.

subject: English
competency: Students will practice listening and speaking skills in a library setting, learn about borrowing books, and understand basic library rules.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity: Divide students into pairs. One student acts as the librarian, and the other acts as Mohan. They should practice the dialogue multiple times, focusing on pronunciation and intonation. After role-playing, conduct a class discussion on the importance of libraries and the rules of borrowing books.

subject: English
competency: Identify proper disposal of litter
teaching_strategy: Create a game where students sort different types of litter into the correct bins. Use flashcards with images of common litter items and have students place them in the appropriate bin.

subject: English
competency: Understand various school activities and their schedules
teaching_strategy: Role-play the club meeting notice. Assign students roles such as club members, teachers, and monitors. Practice reading the notice and discussing the activities, schedules, and responsibilities.

subject: English
competency: Students should know where to go for the Child Club meeting.
teaching_strategy: Create a simple map of the classroom or school and label the location of the Child Club meeting. Have students practice pointing to the correct spot.

subject: English
competency: Students should understand when to submit their creations for the wall magazine.
teaching_strategy: Use a large clock or a digital timer to demonstrate the submission time. Have students practice setting the time and writing it down.

subject: English
competency: Students should know why and how to contact the reception.
teaching_strategy: Role-play scenarios where students need to contact the reception. Provide a list of reasons why they might need to do so and practice saying them out loud.

subject: English
competency: Students will identify and name various playground equipment such as slides, monkey bars, sandbox, merry go round, seesaw, swing, basket hoop, climbing bars, hopscotch, and skipping rope.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of the playground equipment. Have students match the flashcards with the corresponding words in their textbooks. Conduct a class discussion to identify which equipment is present in their school playground.

subject: English
competency: Students will compare their school playground with others and discuss the presence or absence of different equipment.
teaching_strategy: Divide the class into small groups. Assign each group a different playground to observe and document. Have them create a list of equipment found in their assigned playground. Then, compare the lists as a class and discuss the similarities and differences.

subject: English
competency: Students will practice responding to praise and congratulations in a social context.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students pair up and practice giving and receiving congratulations and praise in different scenarios, such as academic achievements or personal accomplishments.

subject: English
competency: Students will develop social interaction skills and learn to use polite language in everyday conversations.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Provide students with sentence starters and have them practice polite responses in various social situations, such as thanking someone or complimenting a peer.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to use appropriate expressions to convey good news and respond to such news.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into pairs and have them practice the dialogue using the given expressions. Encourage them to use different scenarios such as winning a contest, getting a scholarship, or a family member returning home.

subject: English
topic: Problem Solving and Turn-Taking in Games
competency: Students will understand the importance of turn-taking and problem-solving in social interactions.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing the scenario with two students to practice turn-taking and problem-solving skills. Use a timer to count to 100 and have students switch roles to experience both perspectives.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to sequence events in a story.
teaching_strategy: Create a timeline or sequence chart on the board. Have students place the given events in the correct order and discuss the sequence as a class.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe a school event using provided clues and personal experiences.
teaching_strategy: Ask students to choose one event from the list (sports competition, races, etc.) and use the given clues to write a short paragraph about it. Encourage them to include details such as the location (playground), participants (students and parents), and outcomes (winners, prizes).

subject: English
competency: Students will identify and discuss appropriate and inappropriate behaviors in the classroom through visual aids and peer interaction.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of students performing various classroom activities. Have students tick (√) the ones they can do and cross (X) the ones they can't do. Encourage group discussions to identify additional behaviors.

subject: English
competency: Students will identify and describe appropriate and inappropriate behaviors in the classroom and school.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out scenarios where they respect teachers and classmates, and scenarios where they engage in inappropriate behaviors like chewing gum. Discuss the consequences of each scenario.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand the importance of adhering to school rules and the consequences of breaking them.
teaching_strategy: Guided practice: Create a list of school rules and have students categorize them into 'must do' and 'must not do'. Discuss the reasons behind each rule and the potential consequences of breaking them.

subject: English
competency: Identify and apply school rules
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out scenarios where they must follow or not follow the rules (e.g., being on time, keeping the classroom clean, not bringing mobile phones).

subject: English
competency: Create words from given roots
teaching_strategy: Phonics games: Use flashcards with roots like 'corridor,' 'headmaster,' 'teacher,' and 'assembly' and have students create as many words as possible by adding prefixes or suffixes.

subject: English
competency: Develop listening skills and answer questions based on audio recordings.
teaching_strategy: Play the recording and have students answer the questions individually, then discuss their answers in pairs.

subject: English
competency: Practice conversational skills in various scenarios.
teaching_strategy: Divide students into pairs and assign roles. Use role-playing to practice the given situations.

subject: English
competency: Develop problem-solving skills and understand the importance of friendship and fair play.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out the scenario with Indu and Bindu. Discuss possible solutions and encourage students to think of ways to resolve conflicts amicably.

subject: English
competency: Understand the concept of counting and time in a practical context.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Use a timer to count to 100 together as a class. Have students practice counting in pairs and discuss the importance of following rules.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to observe and describe pictures, and engage in discussions about their observations.
teaching_strategy: Use the pictures in the lesson to initiate a discussion. Ask students to describe what they see and share their thoughts. Encourage them to use descriptive words like 'beautiful' and 'flowers'.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to construct simple sentences using 'I like' to express personal preferences.
teaching_strategy: Provide flashcards with different objects or places. Have students form sentences using 'I like' followed by the object or place. For example, 'I like this beautiful flowers.' Use role-playing to make the activity more engaging.

subject: English
competency: Identify and describe objects in pictures
teaching_strategy: Use the pictures of high mountains, a big city, a green forest, and an old house to have students describe the scenes. Encourage them to use descriptive words and phrases.

subject: English
competency: Learn and use new vocabulary
teaching_strategy: Introduce the words trunk, sign, tired, and magic through flashcards. Use role-playing activities where students act out scenarios involving these words to reinforce their understanding.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to select appropriate words to complete sentences and form meaningful phrases.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with the words 'thick', 'beautiful', 'high', 'tall', 'long', 'garden', 'house', 'river', 'forest', 'hill' and have students match them with the correct context. Encourage students to form sentences using these words in different scenarios.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to read a short passage and answer questions based on the content.
teaching_strategy: Read the passage aloud to the class and ask students to identify the setting and the main event. Use role-playing to act out the scene where the boy encounters the magic tree. Discuss the magic tree's sign and the importance of saying the magic words.

subject: English
competency: Understand the significance of polite language in communication.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing game: Have students act out scenarios where they use polite phrases like 'please' and 'thank you' in different situations. This will help them understand the importance of these words in daily interactions.

subject: English
topic: Sequence of Events in a Story
competency: Identify and sequence events in a narrative.
teaching_strategy: Sequence cards: Create cards with each event (a. toys and chocolates, b. tried magic words, c. saw magic tree, d. had party, e. door opened). Have students arrange the cards in the correct order to retell the story. This activity reinforces comprehension and sequencing skills.

subject: English
competency: Use adjectives and verbs to describe objects and people
teaching_strategy: Ask students to describe their classmates using the words 'own', 'strange', and 'attractive'. Provide flashcards with pictures of people and objects, and have students practice using the words in sentences.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use the verb 'introduce' in context
teaching_strategy: Role-play introducing oneself and others. Use props like name tags and have students practice introducing themselves and their classmates.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe people based on physical attributes and characteristics.
teaching_strategy: Use role-playing activities where students describe each other using the provided template. Create flashcards with pictures of people and have students match them with the correct descriptions.

subject: English
competency: Students will compare and contrast physical attributes of different individuals.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a guided practice session where students compare the physical attributes of Nima and Phurba. Use a Venn diagram to visually represent similarities and differences.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe physical attributes and facial features of people using adjectives and adverbs.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of people with different physical attributes. Have students describe the people using adjectives and adverbs. For example, show a card with a tall, blonde woman and ask, 'What is she like?' Encourage students to use sentences like, 'She is tall and has blonde hair.'

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to compare and contrast physical features of people.
teaching_strategy: Create pairs of students and give each pair a set of cards with different physical features. Have them compare and contrast the features, using sentences like, 'His face is round, but hers is oval.' Encourage role-playing where students describe each other using the adjectives and adverbs learned.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe people based on physical appearance and personal information.
teaching_strategy: Use a matching game where students match descriptions of people with corresponding pictures or descriptions. Provide students with cards with different attributes such as hair color, age, and clothing items. Have them work in pairs to match the correct attributes.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to fill in information in a table based on given data.
teaching_strategy: Create a similar table on the board and provide students with a set of cards with information about different people. Have them sort the cards and place them in the correct columns of the table. Encourage them to ask questions to each other to fill in missing information.

subject: English
competency: Students will learn to gather and organize information to describe a friend.
teaching_strategy: Have students work in pairs. Each student should describe their friend to their partner, using the provided prompts. Encourage them to ask follow-up questions to gather more details. Afterward, students can write a short paragraph about their friend based on the notes they took.

subject: English
competency: Identify and describe the four seasons (summer, winter, autumn, spring) and their characteristics (e.g., weather changes, sun, rain, snow, leaf fall, flower growth).
teaching_strategy: Use picture cards of each season to discuss and identify the seasons. Play a seasonal song where students can sing along and reinforce the names of the seasons. Go outside to observe the current season and discuss the weather and changes observed.

subject: English
competency: Describe and discuss seasons with peers using appropriate vocabulary.
teaching_strategy: Divide students into small groups and provide them with picture cards of different seasons. Have them use the words 'sweater', 'scarf', 'fireplace', and 'heater' to describe the pictures and discuss the seasons with each other.

subject: English
competency: Understand the concept of seasons and their impact on weather and surroundings.
teaching_strategy: Create a seasonal calendar where students can track the changes in weather and activities throughout the year. Use flashcards with pictures of different seasons to reinforce learning.

subject: English
competency: Describe characteristics of winter and the actions people take to cope with the cold weather.
teaching_strategy: Role-play different winter activities such as reading by the fireplace or playing in the snow. Use gloves and scarves as props to enhance the role-play.

subject: English
competency: Describe changes in seasons and their impact on daily life and nature.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of different seasons to discuss the changes in weather, day length, and natural phenomena. Engage students in a role-playing activity where they act out different activities associated with each season.

subject: English
competency: Express personal preferences and write short paragraphs.
teaching_strategy: Have students draw their favorite season and write a paragraph about it. Encourage them to use descriptive language and include reasons for their choice. Provide examples of good sentence structures and vocabulary.

subject: English
topic: Understanding cardinal directions (North, South, East, West)
competency: Engage in conversations using directions to describe locations
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of cardinal directions and have students place them correctly on a map. Conduct role-playing activities where students describe the location of their school and other places from their home using 'north', 'south', 'east', and 'west'.

subject: English
competency: Students will learn and use the words: vain, passerby, visit, stay, holiday in context.
teaching_strategy: Create a word wall with the given vocabulary. Use flashcards for each word and have students match the words with their meanings. Play a vocabulary game where students use the words in sentences.

subject: English
competency: Students will read a passage about a family's holiday and answer questions based on the passage.
teaching_strategy: Read the passage aloud and ask students to identify key events and characters. Use role-playing to act out parts of the story. Have students create their own holiday plans using the vocabulary learned.

subject: English
competency: Identify and use cardinal directions (north, south, east, west) in context
teaching_strategy: Use a large classroom map or a created map on the board. Place north at the top, south at the bottom, east on the left, and west on the right. Have students role-play placing items in different directions relative to a central point, such as a campfire or a cabin.

subject: English
competency: Form and recognize compound words
teaching_strategy: Create flashcards with single words on one side and the combined compound word on the other. Use these flashcards for a matching game where students must find the correct compound word for each set of single words provided.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to read and follow directions to navigate from one location to another using a map.
teaching_strategy: Use a physical map or create a simple map on the board. Have students practice giving and following directions using the map. You can use a game format where students take turns giving directions and another student follows them on the map.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand cardinal directions and how to use them to describe the location of objects or places.
teaching_strategy: Create a classroom activity where students use flashcards with different directions (north, south, east, west) and place them on a large map or a grid on the floor. Have students practice standing in different positions and describing their location using the directions.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to identify and describe the location of objects in a picture.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of animals in different locations. Have students practice asking and answering where the animals are.

subject: English
competency: Students will improve their listening skills by understanding and repeating simple sentences.
teaching_strategy: Play a listening game where students listen to a sentence and then repeat it. Use the sentence 'Where is the horse? It's jumping over the fence.' for practice.

subject: English
competency: Use positional prepositions correctly in sentences
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures depicting various positional relationships. Have students create their own sentences using the prepositions from the box.

subject: English
competency: Developing understanding of social interactions and empathy towards others
teaching_strategy: Role-playing different scenarios where students act as the elephant and other forest animals to practice social interactions and empathy.

subject: English
competency: Identifying and solving problems through critical thinking
teaching_strategy: Guided discussion on why the elephant was able to solve the problem of being accepted by the other animals, and creating similar problem-solving scenarios for the students.

subject: English
competency: Describe the locations of animals and their interactions in a forest setting
teaching_strategy: Role-playing game where students act out the roles of different animals in a forest. Use props like a big tree, a small box for the rabbit, and a toy tiger to enhance the scenario.

subject: English
competency: Identify and discuss the reasons behind animals' actions and emotions
teaching_strategy: Guided discussion on the reasons why the animals were running in fear. Use flashcards with pictures of the animals to trigger memory and discussion.

subject: English
competency: Students will practice active listening and following verbal instructions.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Use a 'listening treasure hunt' where students follow verbal directions to find objects around the classroom.

subject: English
competency: Students will develop their ability to describe pictures and engage in oral communication.
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Have students describe the picture to a partner and then switch roles, practicing descriptive language and oral communication skills.

subject: English
competency: Identify key elements in a story and describe actions.
teaching_strategy: Ask students to read the story and then answer the questions using flashcards with the options. For example, create flashcards with 'behind a tree', 'two birds', and 'chirping'. Encourage students to use these flashcards to retell the story in their own words.

subject: English
competency: Describe a local place using given clues.
teaching_strategy: Provide students with a local place, such as a park or a temple, and ask them to write a short description using the given clues. Use guided practice by first discussing the place as a class and then having students write individual descriptions. Follow up with peer review and feedback sessions.

subject: English
competency: Identify and practice rhyming words through interactive activities
teaching_strategy: Phonics games where students match and pronounce rhyming words like 'fog' and 'dog', 'door' and 'more', 'hook' and 'look', 'wall' and 'fall'.

subject: English
competency: Describe objects in a room using adjectives and prepositions
teaching_strategy: Role-playing where students describe and place objects in a pretend room, using sentences like 'The purple carpet is on the floor' and 'The funny picture is on the wall'.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and name common household items such as bookshelf, coffee table, fireplace, curtain, carpet, and stool.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of the objects. Have students match the flashcards to the words in the box.

subject: English
competency: Identify and describe the features of a room
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students describe their own rooms using the vocabulary and structure from the text. Provide flashcards with room features like 'sofa', 'carpet', 'bookshelf', etc., and ask students to match them with the correct descriptions.

subject: English
competency: Determine the accuracy of given statements
teaching_strategy: Interactive Quiz: Create a true or false quiz based on the statements provided. Use a game format like 'Jeopardy' where students earn points for correct answers. This reinforces reading comprehension and critical thinking.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe the features of a living room using descriptive sentences.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of different objects (books, curtains, table lamp, etc.) and have students create sentences describing the living room. Encourage them to use the given objects and add their own.

subject: English
competency: Develop comprehension and response skills through matching exercises
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of the classroom objects and their corresponding sentences. Have students match the questions to the correct answers.

subject: English
competency: Enhance questioning and response abilities in context
teaching_strategy: Role-play scenarios where students ask and answer questions about their classroom or neighborhood. Use props like a toy bus station or a model river to make the practice more engaging.

subject: English
topic: Asking and answering about classroom objects
competency: Formulate and respond to yes/no questions and short answers
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with classroom objects to practice forming yes/no questions and answering them with 'Yes, there is' or 'No, there isn't'.

subject: English
competency: Construct questions to inquire about various town elements
teaching_strategy: Role-play a visitor asking locals about shops, restaurants, and other town features using the provided question starters. Encourage students to fill in the blanks with specific town elements.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to identify and name common classroom objects and their locations.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of classroom objects. Have students take turns identifying and naming the objects in the picture. Encourage them to use the objects' names in sentences, such as 'I see a globe on the teacher's desk.'

subject: English
competency: Students will practice writing the names of classroom objects.
teaching_strategy: Provide each student with a worksheet containing pictures and a box of objects. Instruct them to write the names of the objects in the spaces below the pictures. Use a phonics game where students match the written names with the objects to reinforce spelling and recognition.

subject: English
competency: Practice using 'my', 'your', and 'his/her' in context through pair and group activities.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of objects and have students practice pointing and speaking in pairs and threes using the possessive pronouns.

subject: English
competency: Use possessive adjectives correctly in sentences
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Create a phonics game where students match the possessive adjectives with their corresponding objects. For example, 'yours' with 'bed', 'mine' with 'pencil case', etc.

subject: English
competency: Describe a classroom and its inventory
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Have students role-play as Pasang and Miss Rita, describing the classroom and its inventory. Encourage them to use the vocabulary and phrases from the text.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to form sentences using given words.
teaching_strategy: Provide students with flashcards containing the words from the text. Have them create sentences using these words in small groups, encouraging creativity and sentence structure.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe their school and classroom using adjectives and possessive pronouns.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into pairs and have them take turns asking and answering questions about their classroom and school. Use flashcards with pictures of classroom objects for vocabulary reinforcement.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe personal items and their attributes using adjectives.
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Provide students with a list of objects and adjectives. Have them create sentences describing the objects, such as 'My desk is blue' or 'Pasang has a sharpener'. Use flashcards for additional practice.

subject: English
competency: Identify and use correct personal pronouns and possessive adjectives in sentences
teaching_strategy: Phonics games: Create a 'pronoun relay' game where students pass around a ball and each time they catch it, they must use a different personal pronoun or possessive adjective in a sentence.

subject: English
competency: Form questions using who, what, and why
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out scenarios where they ask and answer questions using who, what, and why.

subject: English
competency: Students will match words to corresponding pictures of clothing items and discuss what people are wearing.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of clothing items and have students match them to the words. Conduct a class discussion on the types of clothes people wear.

subject: English
competency: Students will learn the meanings of new vocabulary related to clothing.
teaching_strategy: Create a word wall with the new vocabulary words. Use a dictionary or a digital dictionary app to find and explain the meanings of each word. Encourage students to use these words in sentences.

subject: English
competency: Identify and use clothing names in sentences
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Create a phonics scavenger hunt where students find and pronounce the names of clothes in the puzzle. Use flashcards to reinforce the spelling and pronunciation of each word.

subject: English
competency: Form simple sentences using clothing vocabulary
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Have students act out scenarios where they describe their clothes using the words from the puzzle. For example, 'I am wearing a shirt that is red.'

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to conduct a simple shopping transaction and understand the roles of a customer and a salesperson.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students can practice the dialogue between Nitu and the saleswoman. Divide the class into pairs, assign roles, and have them act out the conversation multiple times.

subject: English
competency: Students will learn to describe products and understand basic pricing.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of different colored sweaters and have students match the colors to the descriptions. For pricing, use real or mock currency to demonstrate transactions and counting.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and use adjectives to describe objects
teaching_strategy: Adjective Game: Provide students with flashcards of adjectives (e.g., dark, red, yellow, white, long, small) and nouns (e.g., sweater, shirt, T-shirt, tie, coat, hair band). Have students match the adjectives with the appropriate nouns and create sentences using the correct adjectives.

subject: English
competency: Describe objects using appropriate adjectives
teaching_strategy: Cloze Activity: Fill in the blanks in the sentences provided on the page. Use the adjectives given in the examples to complete the sentences. Encourage students to create their own sentences using the adjectives and nouns provided.

subject: English
competency: Understand and describe the process of shopping and purchasing items for family members.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students act as Mrs. Karki and select items for different family members. Use props like toy clothes and shopping bags to make the activity more engaging.

subject: English
competency: Match words with their correct meanings.
teaching_strategy: Flashcard game where students match words like 'shopping', 'store', 'belt', 'slippers', and 'sale' with their definitions. Use the dictionary as a reference.

subject: English
competency: Students will construct sentences using given words and create their own sentences.
teaching_strategy: Provide students with flashcards of the words 'store', 'belt', 'slippers', and 'sale'. Have them create sentences using these words. For example, 'I bought slippers on sale at the store.'

subject: English
competency: Students will identify true or false statements based on a given scenario.
teaching_strategy: Read the scenario aloud: 'It was a weekend. Mrs. Karki's children love shopping. She forgot to buy clothes for her husband. The slippers were on sale. She bought nothing for herself. She got tired at the end. She rested at a restaurant.' Then, ask students to circle T for true and F for false for each statement. Encourage them to discuss their answers with a partner.

subject: English
topic: Using conjunctions (and, but, because) in sentences
competency: Students will be able to correctly use 'and', 'but', and 'because' in sentences
teaching_strategy: Conjunctions Game: Create a game where students match conjunctions with appropriate sentences. Use flashcards with conjunctions on one side and sentences on the other. Students can play in pairs or small groups to reinforce their understanding.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to complete sentences using appropriate conjunctions
teaching_strategy: Sentence Completion Activity: Provide students with sentence starters and have them complete the sentences using 'and', 'but', or 'because'. Encourage them to use context clues to determine the correct conjunction.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to write numbers from 50 to 100 in words.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with numbers and their corresponding word forms for guided practice. Have students create their own flashcards and play a memory game.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to describe clothes using simple sentences.
teaching_strategy: Engage students in a role-playing activity where they describe different clothes to each other. Provide sentence starters like 'I have a [color] [type of clothing].'

subject: English
competency: Develop listening skills and answer questions based on a recording.
teaching_strategy: Play the recording and have students work individually to answer the questions. Follow up with a class discussion to review the answers.

subject: English
competency: Practice speaking and descriptive skills by describing objects and numbers.
teaching_strategy: Divide students into pairs. One student describes an object shown by the teacher, and the other guesses what it is. For the number activity, the teacher points to numbers on the board or a chart, and students take turns saying the number names aloud.

subject: English
competency: Understand and match items with family members and contexts.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Create a matching game where students match items (polo shirts, jacket, grey suit, slippers) with family members (daughter, herself, son, husband) using flashcards. This can be done through a memory game or a quick quiz format.

subject: English
competency: Answer questions related to a shopping scenario.
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Divide the class into groups and assign roles (e.g., mother, daughter, son, husband). Act out a shopping scenario where the mother buys items for the family. Ask students to answer questions based on the scenario, such as 'Do the children like to go shopping?' and 'Where did she buy the grey suit from?'

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to identify and describe the characteristics of different musical instruments such as Madal, Sarangi, Dhimay, Basuree, and Khaijadi Damphu.
teaching_strategy: Show students pictures of the musical instruments and have them describe the instruments in pairs or small groups. Use flashcards with images and names of the instruments for a memory game.

subject: English
competency: Students will learn the basic playing techniques of the instruments mentioned in the lesson.
teaching_strategy: Demonstrate the correct way to play each instrument using props or videos. Encourage students to practice playing the instruments using guided practice sessions.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to identify and differentiate sounds produced by various musical instruments through listening and singing activities.
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Use the sounds of the instruments to create a phonics game where students match the sound to the correct instrument.

subject: English
competency: Students will develop their ability to ask and answer questions in a conversational context, enhancing their communication skills.
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Conduct role-playing activities where students ask and answer questions about daily activities, using the provided examples as a guide.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use vocabulary related to objects and their functions
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of the objects and their meanings. Have students match the words to the correct images.

subject: English
competency: Apply vocabulary in context
teaching_strategy: Create a role-playing activity where students act out the sentences. For example, one student can pretend to be a dog being hit with a stick, while another student describes the action using the correct word.

subject: English
competency: Identify and describe the five main instruments of Panche Baja and their functions in ceremonies, and understand their basic structure and playing methods.
teaching_strategy: Create a flashcard game where students match the names of the instruments (Damaha, Jhyali, Tyamko, Dholaki, Sahanai) with their descriptions and images. Use real or toy instruments for hands-on practice.

subject: English
competency: Change sentences to past tense
teaching_strategy: Provide flashcards with sentences in present tense. Have students change the sentences to past tense using the flashcards as examples. Use role-playing to act out the past tense sentences.

subject: English
competency: Describe musical instruments
teaching_strategy: Show pictures of different musical instruments. Use a phonics game where students describe the instruments using adjectives. Guide them to write descriptions of two instruments they like.

subject: English
competency: Identify and describe different festivals celebrated in Nepal and their significance.
teaching_strategy: Show students pictures of Tihar, Maghi, Holi, Bisket Jatra, and Eid. Discuss the cultural significance of each festival. Have students share their experiences of celebrating recent festivals with classmates.

subject: English
competency: Understand and appreciate the cultural diversity in Nepal through the celebration of various festivals.
teaching_strategy: Role-play different festivals with students. For example, have students dress up in traditional attire and perform dances related to Tihar and Holi. Use flashcards to teach vocabulary related to the festivals.

subject: English
topic: Discussing and Describing Clothing and Accessories
competency: Students will be able to describe traditional Nepali attire and accessories using descriptive words and phrases.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of different traditional clothing and accessories. Have students describe the items using adjectives and discuss their cultural significance.

subject: English
topic: Listening and Comprehension of Simple Sentences
competency: Students will be able to understand and retell simple sentences related to cultural events and traditions.
teaching_strategy: Read the sentences aloud and ask students to repeat them. Use role-playing to act out the scenarios described in the sentences.

subject: English
competency: Identify and describe the significance of Gaura Parva
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out a scene where they are in Kathmandu celebrating Gaura Parva with their families. Encourage them to use the information provided about the festival, such as the activities and the worship of goddess Gauri.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and appreciate different cultural practices
teaching_strategy: Flashcards: Create flashcards with images and names of festivals mentioned (Christmas, Gai Jatra, New Year, Teej, Chhat, Lhosar, Gaura Parva). Use these flashcards to introduce and discuss the cultural significance of each festival.

subject: English
competency: Understand the structure and performance of Deuda Dance
teaching_strategy: Role-playing the Deuda Dance with students, using props like handkerchiefs or scarves to represent holding hands in a circle. Encourage students to practice the steps of moving forwards and backwards in a circular formation.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and describe the cultural significance of Gaura Parva
teaching_strategy: Create a timeline activity where students place key events of the festival in order. Use flashcards with images of the festival to reinforce vocabulary and concepts.

subject: English
competency: Understand and describe local festivals
teaching_strategy: Role-playing

subject: English
competency: Compose a paragraph about a festival
teaching_strategy: Guided practice

subject: English
competency: Discuss and identify special days such as Thanksgiving Day, Father's Day, Mother's Day, Buddha Jayanti, and Aamako Mukh Herne Din, and their significance in terms of respect and love for family members and cultural practices.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of the special days to engage students in a discussion. Have students role-play different scenarios where they express gratitude and respect towards their parents and the Buddha. Provide guided practice by asking students to write short messages or draw pictures representing their feelings on these days.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to form and answer questions about daily activities.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide the class into pairs. One student asks questions using 'What did you do yesterday?' and the other responds with one of the provided activities. For example, 'What did you do yesterday?' 'I watched cartoons.'

subject: English
competency: Understand word meanings and use them appropriately
teaching_strategy: Flashcards: Create flashcards with words on one side and their meanings on the other. Use these for quick matching games and quizzes.

subject: English
competency: Apply vocabulary in context
teaching_strategy: Sentence completion: Provide sentences and have students fill in the blanks with the correct words. Encourage them to use the words in their own sentences for better understanding.

subject: English
competency: Understand and describe the significance of Knowledge Day in Russia, including school routines and traditions on this day.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out the assembly, with some students playing the roles of students, teachers, and parents. Use props like flowers and a simple handmade gift to enhance the experience.

subject: English
competency: Identify the roles of different school staff and understand the structure of a typical school day.
teaching_strategy: Flashcards: Create flashcards with pictures of teachers, students, and school staff. Use these to teach the roles and responsibilities of each. Guided Practice: Have students match roles to their descriptions.

subject: English
competency: Identify and describe cultural practices and events
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Students can act out a scene where they are welcoming students to school and celebrating Knowledge Day. Use flashcards with dates and events to reinforce the concept.

subject: English
competency: Understand and follow school routines and roles
teaching_strategy: Guided practice: Create a classroom activity where students match roles (teachers, students) with their responsibilities (welcoming students, informing about timetable). Use role cards and a classroom layout to enhance understanding.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to convert given statements into questions.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with statements on one side and questions on the other. Have students match the correct question to each statement. For example, 'Rupesh woke up late this morning.' can be turned into 'Who woke up late this morning?'

subject: English
competency: Students will understand and use the past tense in questions and statements.
teaching_strategy: Role-play scenarios where students ask and answer questions about past events. For example, one student can say, 'I went to Pokhara last week.' and another can ask, 'Where did you go last week?'

subject: English
competency: Understand the significance and practices of Saraswati Puja, including its alternative name, timing, and importance in education.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out the scene of worshipping Saraswati and teaching their children. Use props like books and pens to enhance the activity.

subject: English
competency: Develop writing skills by composing a paragraph on a given topic.
teaching_strategy: Guided practice: Provide students with a structured outline to write about Saraswati Puja, then have them write a paragraph individually.

subject: English
competency: Understand and describe cultural festivals
teaching_strategy: Role-playing and discussion

subject: English
competency: Form sentences in past tense
teaching_strategy: Sentence transformation exercises

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to match sentences with corresponding pictures and create additional sentences.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures on one side and sentences on the other. Have students match the cards and then create their own sentences about the pictures.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand and recognize different cultural festivals and their significance.
teaching_strategy: Engage students in a role-playing activity where they act out the festivals and traditions mentioned. Use props and costumes to enhance the experience.

subject: English
competency: Students will identify and name common household and communication devices such as TV, radio, mobile phone, and computer.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of TV, radio, mobile phone, and computer. Conduct a quick quiz where students match the names with the images.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand and describe daily communication activities such as watching news, listening to songs, and making calls.
teaching_strategy: Role-play scenarios where students act out calling their grandparents or listening to the radio. Encourage students to share their own experiences with communication devices.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to compare objects or situations from the past to the present using given examples.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of objects or situations from the past and present. Have students compare and contrast these using the provided examples as a guide.

subject: English
competency: Developing social skills through dialogue and problem-solving
teaching_strategy: Role-playing the conversation between Sami and Tara to practice dialogue and problem-solving skills.

subject: English
competency: Understanding the evolution of technology over time
teaching_strategy: Create a timeline activity where students place the invention of the telephone in the correct historical context, comparing it with modern-day technology.

subject: English
competency: Understand the development from landline telephones to cell phones and smartphones.
teaching_strategy: Use a timeline activity where students place key events (invention of the telephone, introduction of cell phones, introduction of smartphones) in chronological order. Discuss the impact of these changes on communication.

subject: English
topic: Comparison of Landline and Cell Phones
competency: Compare and contrast the features and uses of landline telephones and cell phones, including smartphones.
teaching_strategy: Create a Venn diagram on the board. List features of landline telephones on one circle and features of cell phones (including smartphones) on the other. Have students fill in the overlapping area with common features. Discuss the differences and similarities.

subject: English
topic: Comparison between telephone and cell phone
competency: Students will compare the features and benefits of a telephone and a cell phone through discussion and writing.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out scenarios where they need to use a telephone versus a cell phone. Follow-up with a writing activity where they compare the two devices.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand the evolution of television technology over the years through reading and writing.
teaching_strategy: Flashcards: Create flashcards with key points about the evolution of TV sets (black and white vs. color, number of channels, remote controls). Use these for a memory game or quick review session.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and describe different places in the town and the people one might encounter
teaching_strategy: Sing and act out the song to reinforce the concept of various places in the town and the people one might meet. Use flashcards with pictures of different town places and people to help students associate the lyrics with real-world objects.

subject: English
competency: Understand the importance of community and recognition within it
teaching_strategy: Role-play scenarios where students are introduced to new people in the community and practice saying their names and faces are known. Use a class map to mark different places in the town and discuss the roles of community members.

subject: English
competency: Identify and discuss various means of transportation in their town
teaching_strategy: Phonics Game: Create a phonics game where students match words like 'car', 'subway', 'bus', 'taxi', and 'bike' with their corresponding pictures. This helps in reinforcing the pronunciation and recognition of these words.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and categorize different places in their town for transportation and shopping
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Divide students into groups and assign roles such as a bus conductor, a taxi driver, and a shopkeeper. Have them act out scenarios where they interact with each other, discussing places to go and shop in the town. This activity enhances their understanding of the town's layout and the roles of different people.

subject: English
competency: Identify common places for shopping and services
teaching_strategy: Role-playing game: Divide students into groups and assign each group a place (vegetable market, stationery shop, barber shop, supermarket, bakery, pharmacy). Each group should create a short skit demonstrating what happens at their assigned place. Encourage students to use the correct words from the sentences provided.

subject: English
competency: Engage in simple conversations using common phrases and questions
teaching_strategy: Role-playing

subject: English
competency: Expand vocabulary related to shopping and preferences
teaching_strategy: Flashcards and guided practice

subject: English
competency: Conduct a simple transaction at a shoe shop, including dialogue, price negotiation, and payment.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity: Divide students into pairs, one as the shopkeeper and the other as the customer. Provide them with price tags and shoe cards. Have them practice the dialogue from the text and create their own scenarios.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use currency symbols and values in a real-life context.
teaching_strategy: Flashcard activity: Create flashcards with different prices and currency symbols. Students should match the prices with the correct symbols and discuss the values.

subject: English
competency: Engage in a dialogue about shopping experiences
teaching_strategy: Role-playing

subject: English
competency: Identify and use vocabulary related to shopping
teaching_strategy: Flashcards

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to identify and name different denominations of Nepalese currency (notes and coins).
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of different currency notes and coins. Have students match the images to their names and practice writing them.

subject: English
competency: Students will understand the importance and necessity of money in daily transactions.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a role-playing activity where students act out scenarios without money and discuss the challenges faced. Follow up with a discussion on why money is essential.

subject: English
competency: Practice buying and selling items using money and engage in role-playing conversations.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing game where students act as customers and shopkeepers to practice buying and selling items and handling money.

subject: English
competency: Construct sentences using conjunctions 'and', 'but', and 'because' to express preferences and reasons.
teaching_strategy: Sentence building activity where students complete sentences using the given conjunctions and create their own sentences.

subject: English
competency: Practice dialogue and service interaction in a restaurant setting
teaching_strategy: Role-playing activity where students take turns being guests and a waiter. Provide props like menus and place settings to enhance the role-play.

subject: English
competency: Understand and use vocabulary related to ordering food and drinks in a restaurant
teaching_strategy: Create flashcards with food and drink items. Use the flashcards for a game where students must order items from a pretend waiter.

subject: English
competency: Use dictionary to find meanings and apply words in sentences
teaching_strategy: Phonics Games: Create a phonics scavenger hunt where students find words starting with the same sound as the target words (hungry, menu, order) in the supermarket environment. Have them use these words in sentences.

subject: English
competency: Understand and express preferences for food and activities
teaching_strategy: Role-Playing: Divide students into groups and assign roles (Bikas, Bijaya, Nabina). Act out a scene where they are at the supermarket, deciding what to buy and watch. Encourage them to use the words 'hungry', 'menu', and 'order' in their dialogue.

subject: English
competency: Identify and discuss likes and dislikes in shopping and food preferences
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out a shopping scenario where they choose items and discuss their preferences. Use flashcards with pictures of different foods and clothes for practice.

subject: English
competency: Locate and describe the positions of objects or people
teaching_strategy: Interactive Map Game: Create a simple map on the board or using a digital tool. Place markers for Bikas, the restaurant, and other relevant locations. Have students practice asking and answering questions about the positions of these items.

subject: English
competency: Understand the evolution of telephones from landlines to cell phones.
teaching_strategy: Use a timeline activity where students place key events in chronological order. Have students role-play a conversation about the invention of the telephone and the changes over time using props like a lunchbox and a cell phone.

subject: English
competency: Use comparative adjectives and vocabulary related to technology and daily objects.
teaching_strategy: Ask students to compare and contrast different household items using comparative adjectives. For example, they can compare the size of a lunchbox and a telephone. Use flashcards with images of different objects to reinforce vocabulary.

subject: English
competency: Use conjunctions to connect sentences.
teaching_strategy: Play a game where students have to connect sentences using 'and', 'but', or 'because'. For example, 'I like bread and curry because it's good for our health.' Use sentence strips and conjunction cards to facilitate this activity.

subject: English
competency: Students will engage in a rhyming game and sing a simple nursery rhyme to improve phonemic awareness and vocabulary.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with pictures of pumpkins and other rhyming words to enhance visual and auditory learning. Sing the rhyme together, encouraging students to join in and use their voices.

subject: English
competency: Students will participate in an action-based activity to reinforce the rhyme and develop motor skills.
teaching_strategy: Have students act out the rhyme by rolling a ball (representing the pumpkin) and tickling their feet. This will help them connect the rhyme with physical actions and enhance their understanding.

subject: English
competency: Engage in conversations about vegetables, describe their characteristics, and identify them based on given features.
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Divide students into pairs and have them take turns asking and answering questions about different vegetables. Use flashcards with pictures of vegetables to prompt discussions.

subject: English
competency: Expand vocabulary by learning new words and using them in context.
teaching_strategy: Word Games: Create a word hunt where students find and use the new words (hunt, maiden, replied, message, ordered) in sentences. Use flashcards for guided practice.

subject: English
competency: Identify and correct grammatical errors in sentences.
teaching_strategy: Use sentence correction games where students identify and fix errors in given sentences. For example, provide sentences like 'Kopila sent me a on my birthday.' and have students rewrite them correctly.

subject: English
competency: Understand and interpret a short story.
teaching_strategy: Read the story 'The Pumpkin in the Jar' aloud and ask students to retell the story in their own words. Use role-playing to act out different parts of the story, such as the king and the maiden.

subject: English
competency: Analyze the actions and motivations of characters in a story
teaching_strategy: Role-playing: Have students act out the scene where the maiden breaks the jar and the king's reaction. Discuss the king's initial anger and his eventual understanding of the maiden's actions.

subject: English
competency: Identify and solve problems presented in the story
teaching_strategy: Guided Practice: Present the task of fitting a pumpkin into a small opening jar and discuss the strategies the maiden might use. Have students brainstorm and share their ideas.

subject: English
competency: Determine the accuracy of given statements
teaching_strategy: Use a truth or false game where students create their own statements about the story and categorize them. Provide flashcards with statements and have students sort them into true and false.

subject: English
competency: Arrange events in a logical order
teaching_strategy: Create a timeline activity where students place events in the correct order. Use index cards with each event written on them and have students arrange them in sequence.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to express personal preferences and reasons for those preferences.
teaching_strategy: Conduct a role-playing activity where students pair up and ask each other about their fruit preferences. Provide flashcards with pictures of different fruits for students to refer to and use in their conversations.

subject: English
competency: Students will be able to complete a table based on given information.
teaching_strategy: Guide students through filling out the table by discussing the examples provided. Use guided practice where students fill in the blanks for a few entries before doing it independently.

subject: English
topic: Understanding the difference between fruits and vegetables
competency: Discuss the characteristics of fruits and vegetables
teaching_strategy: Role-playing a conversation between Casey and her mother to discuss the characteristics of fruits and vegetables.

subject: English
competency: Recognize and use context clues to match words with their meanings
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with the words and their meanings to reinforce learning. Have students create their own flashcards for additional practice.

subject: English
competency: Understand the difference between fruits and vegetables in terms of their botanical characteristics and culinary uses.
teaching_strategy: Use flashcards with images of various fruits and vegetables. Have students categorize them into fruits and vegetables based on the discussion in the text. Discuss the botanical characteristics of each, emphasizing the presence of seeds in fruits and the different parts of plants that vegetables come from.

subject: English
competency: Recognize that fruits are seed-covered parts of plants and that vegetables are other parts of plants such as stems, leaves, and roots.
teaching_strategy: Create a role-playing activity where students act as botanists identifying different plant parts.
